arguments.markdown:
Tesla's reported segments describe a vehicle business whose gross margin does not cover group research and development and selling costs, a storage business and a services business that together earn the group's operating profit, and a third quarter of 2026 in which both of those profit pools were helped by tariff refunds and warranty true-ups — the return is earned on storage and on the cash pile, not on the car.

### Three segments, three ways of getting paid

The automotive segment took 73.3% of third-quarter 2026 revenue ($20,560M of $28,046M), services and other 16.4% ($4,605M) and energy generation and storage 10.3% ($2,881M). The buyer differs in each: a retail or fleet customer pays cash or finances a car when control transfers; an energy customer — a utility, developer or data-centre operator — pays on project milestones across quarters; a service customer pays per transaction for collision repair, maintenance or a Supercharging session; another automaker pays for regulatory credits at transfer of title. The mix has moved: energy was 6.2% of FY2023 revenue ($6,035M) and 13.5% in FY2025 ($12,771M), while automotive revenue fell from $82,419M to $69,526M. The only recurring software charge is FSD (Supervised) at $99 a month, with 1.74 million active subscriptions on 2026-09-30 against 1.04 million a year earlier [S8, S1, S121].

### The vehicle does not pay for the research budget

| Per unit (one vehicle delivered), Q3 2026 | USD per unit | Note | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| Automotive revenue | 42,259 | $20,560M ÷ 486,532 deliveries | S9 |
| Cost of automotive revenue | (34,436) | materials, labour, overhead, warranty, tariffs | S8 |
| Automotive gross profit | 7,823 | 18.5% margin | S8 |
| Regulatory credits inside that profit | 232 | $113M ÷ 486,532; no matching cost | S8 |
| Automotive gross profit excluding credits | 7,590 | 18.1% of $20,447M ex-credit revenue | S8 |
| Group R&D and SG&A per unit | (9,817) | $4,776M ÷ 486,532, all charged to the car | S9 |
| Automotive-only operating contribution | (1,994) | a loss before energy and services | derived |
| Energy and services gross profit per unit | 3,470 | $1,688M ÷ 486,532 | S8 |
| Group operating profit per unit | 1,476 | $718M ÷ 486,532 | S9 |
| Interest income per unit | 915 | $445M ÷ 486,532 | S8 |
| Pre-tax profit per unit | 1,965 | $956M ÷ 486,532 | S8 |

A delivered car carried $42,259 of automotive revenue and $34,436 of cost, leaving $7,823 of gross profit, or $7,590 once regulatory credits are removed; spreading $4,776M of group research and development and selling cost over 486,532 deliveries costs $9,817 a vehicle, so the automotive line alone runs at roughly -$1,994 a vehicle. Energy and services add $3,470 a vehicle and turn that into $1,476 of operating profit and, with $445M of interest income, $1,965 of pre-tax profit. Cost per vehicle was $33,666 in Q4 2025, $35,786 in Q1 2026 and $34,436 in Q3 2026, so unit cost is not falling; the rise in ex-credit automotive margin from 15.4% to 18.1% year on year arrived with a richer Asia-Pacific delivery mix in Q3 2026, not from the factory [S9, S8].

::: evidence
**The reported credit collapse is a clawback of past revenue, not yet a collapse in current demand — but the contracted backlog says it is coming.**

Reported credit revenue fell from $542M in Q4 2025 to $380M in Q1 2026, $146M in Q2 2026 and $113M in Q3 2026, after $1,993M in FY2025 and $2,763M in FY2024. The Q3 2026 figure is net of a $475M reversal of previously recognised credit revenue for contractual return of already-delivered credits, so gross credit sales in the quarter were about $588M — higher than Q4 2025 — and the reported line overstates the speed of the decline. The forward indicator is worse: contracted credit obligations with original terms over one year fell to $384M at 2026-09-30 from $841M at 2025-12-31, only $201M of it due within twelve months, against $1,993M earned in FY2025. Toyota and Stellantis left Tesla's European CO2 pool for 2026, with Subaru also reported out, and UBS put the pool at more than €1 billion of annual revenue. Tesla names no credit buyer in its filings [S8, S83, S1, S123].
:::

### Storage earns the best margin and the least predictable one

Energy generation and storage produced $954M of gross profit on $2,881M of revenue in Q3 2026 (33.1%), after 20.4% in Q2 2026 and 39.5% in Q1 2026. Revenue per GWh deployed fell from $274 per kWh in Q1 2026 to $210 per kWh in Q3 2026, and gross profit per kWh went $108, $47, $70 across the three quarters, so the segment's margin moves with Megapack pricing, cell cost, tariff recoveries and warranty true-ups. Demand evidence is strong: $10.73 billion of unsatisfied energy obligations at 2026-09-30 with $4.80 billion due within twelve months, and a Megapack book management described as nearly sold out through 2027. The counter-evidence is that part of that growth is a related party: SpaceX bought $626M of Megapacks in the first nine months of 2026 ($221M in Q3), left $729M of receivables at 2026-09-30 — $588M of it for units not yet delivered — and $648M of deferred revenue, so energy's fastest-growing account is the chief executive's other company [S8, S1, S117].

| Line of business | Pricing metric | Price per unit | Period | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Vehicles | per vehicle delivered, blended across models | $42,259 revenue, $34,436 cost | Q3 2026 | S9 |
| Regulatory credits | per credit sold to another automaker | not disclosed; $113M net of a $475M reversal | Q3 2026 | S8 |
| Energy storage | per kWh deployed, Megapack and Powerwall blended | $210/kWh revenue, $70/kWh gross profit | Q3 2026 | S9 |
| FSD (Supervised) | per vehicle per month | $99 | 2026-10 | S121 |
| Megapack to SpaceX | per project, milestone billed | not disclosed; $626M of revenue | 9M 2026 | S8 |
| Vehicle leasing | per vehicle per month | not disclosed; $353M leasing revenue | Q3 2026 | S8 |
| Supercharging | per session or per kWh | not disclosed | Q3 2026 | S8 |
| Robotaxi and Cybercab | per ride | not disclosed | Q3 2026 | S9 |

### Services is the quiet second engine

Services and other grew revenue 33% year on year to $4,605M and lifted gross profit to $734M, a 15.9% margin against 10.5% in Q3 2025 and an all-time high. Behind it are used-vehicle sales, collision and non-warranty maintenance, paid Supercharging across 8,904 stations and 84,465 connectors, and an insurance book — parts-and-labour businesses with largely variable costs riding on a charging network with largely fixed ones, so utilisation lifts the marginal margin. Rivian's software and services segment earned 42% on $605M of revenue in the same quarter, so Tesla's margin is well below the best comparable but on 7.6 times the revenue, and services now supplies 13.4% of group gross profit from 16.4% of revenue. The risk sits in the used-car and collision lines, which depend on the resale values that also underpin Tesla's lease residuals and insurance claims [S9, S120].

### What breaks even, and what cannot be measured

At Q3 2026 unit economics and constant group cost, the automotive line covers its share of the group only at about 611,000 deliveries a quarter, 26% above the 486,532 delivered. Tesla discloses no customer-acquisition cost — there is no marketing line in the statements — so SG&A at 7.2% of revenue is the nearest proxy and a CAC payback or LTV:CAC ratio cannot be computed from the filings; that limit matters, because the claim that Tesla acquires buyers more cheaply than Ford or GM is untested. Judged on operating margin, Tesla's 2.6% sits below GM's 8.2% EBIT-adjusted and Ford's 5.5%, while its 18.1% ex-credit gross margin is level with BYD's 18%: the difference is the operating cost line, not the car. For an investor underwriting the shares at the current quote, the implication is that the next twelve months pay for a storage margin that has printed anywhere between 20% and 40% and a software attach that carries no disclosed revenue — the diligence question is what FSD subscription revenue and Megapack-only margin actually are, because those two numbers decide whether the group earns more than its cost of capital [S115, S116, S119].

arguments.markdown:
Tesla's legal and ownership structure is unusually plain for a founder-led company — one class of stock, a Texas parent with no VIE or dual-class layer, and a CEO who owns 19.8% — so what constrains a 12-month equity return is not the charter but a 10.7% contingent dilution struck at market capitalisations from $2 trillion upward, no dividend or buyback, and a classified board that minority holders cannot replace. Tesla, Inc. trades on Nasdaq under TSLA; 3,952,648,559 shares were outstanding at 2026-09-30 and market capitalisation was $1.58 trillion at the $399.81 close on 2026-10-30 [S10, S112].

### One operating group, no holding-company layer

The registrant was incorporated in Delaware on 2003-07-01 and converted to a Texas corporation on 2024-06-13. The structure is flat: country operating companies, single-purpose solar and lease vehicles and insurance captives, with no contractual-control or variable-interest layer separating legal from economic ownership. The filings disclose no separate intellectual-property holding company; the listed parent files the group's consolidated accounts, while the operating subsidiaries hold the plants, local licences and financing books [S1, S58].

| Entity | Jurisdiction | Type | Role | Ownership | Controller | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Tesla, Inc. | Texas, US | Listed corporation | Registrant; consolidated group; public equity | 100% of subsidiaries | Board; Musk 19.8% | S1, S58 |
| Tesla (Shanghai) Co., Ltd. | China | Limited liability company | Gigafactory and Megafactory Shanghai operating entity | 100% | Tesla, Inc. | S1 |
| Tesla Manufacturing Brandenburg SE | Germany | European company | Gigafactory Berlin-Brandenburg | 100% | Tesla, Inc. | S1 |
| Tesla Robotaxi, LLC | Texas, US | LLC | Robotaxi operations | 100% | Tesla, Inc. | S1 |

### The dilution path runs through a $2 trillion gate

Musk holds 699,580,882 shares, or 19.8%, including 286,428,773 restricted shares from the 2018 award, and 207,498,721 of his shares are pledged against personal borrowings. The 2018 award was exercised in full on 2026-06-16 for 303,960,630 shares, which is why the count rose 202m, or 5.4%, in the nine months to 2026-09-30. Forward dilution is the 2025 CEO Performance Award: 423,743,904 shares, 10.7% of the current count, in 12 equal tranches, none earned as of 2026-10-19. Each earned share carries a $334.09 offset payable in cash or shares, a five-year holding requirement, and every tranche needs a market-cap milestone before any operating milestone counts, starting at $2 trillion — 26.6% above the 2026-10-30 value — then nine $500bn and two $1tn increments to $8.5 trillion. The economics sit closer to a premium-struck option than a free grant: at $399.81 the gross spread is $65.72 a share, and at the plan's top the transfer is $769.6bn net of offsets, 9.1% of an $8.5 trillion capitalisation [S10, S107].

| Holder | Class | Shares | % of shares | % of votes | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Elon Musk (CEO, director) | Common | 699,580,882 | 19.8% | 19.8% | S10 |
| Vanguard Capital Management | Common | 210,796,512 | 5.3% | 5.3% | S10 |
| All directors and officers (11 persons) | Common | 706,496,615 | 20.0% | 20.0% | S10 |
| Public float, calculated (excludes insider shares and 423.7m unvested restricted shares) | Common | 2,822,467,040 | 71.4% | 71.4% | S10 |

### What the customer actually buys

The business is three P&Ls sold to different budget owners. Automotive ($69.53bn of FY2025 revenue, 73% of the total) sells vehicles to consumers, leasing companies and fleets, and monetises the installed base through Supercharging, service, parts, used cars and insurance; the software layer is FSD (Supervised), with 1.74m active subscriptions at 2026-09-30. Energy ($12.77bn, 13.5% of revenue, 29.8% gross margin) sells Megapack and Powerwall to utilities, developers, industrial sites and, increasingly, data-centre operators whose budget is a power-availability capex line rather than a transport one. Services ($12.53bn, +19% in FY2025) is largely a captive aftermarket on Tesla's own parc. Growth has shifted from unit volume — Q3 2026 deliveries were 486,532, down 2% year on year — to storage deployment (13.7 GWh in Q3 2026), software attach and the Robotaxi and Optimus optionality the pay award is designed to reward [S1, S9].

### Capacity is built; volume is the question

Tesla runs eight primary plants: Fremont (Model 3/Y, more than 550,000 units), Shanghai (more than 950,000), Berlin (more than 375,000), Texas (Model Y more than 375,000, Cybertruck and Cybercab more than 125,000 each) and Nevada (Semi 25,000), plus Megapack plants in California (40 GWh), Shanghai (20 GWh) and Texas (50 GWh). Headcount was 134,785 at 2025-12-31. Nameplate vehicle capacity of 2.53m units against an annualised Q3 2026 run rate of 1.95m leaves a fifth of the system idle, while Semi, Cybercab and Optimus lines add depreciation before revenue; that is the mechanism by which a flat revenue year becomes either margin expansion or further compression [S9, S1].

### No payout, and a board that cannot be replaced

Tesla has never paid a dividend, has no repurchase authorisation and made no purchases in FY2025, while holding $45.45bn of cash and short-term investments; with no distribution, a holder's 12-month total return is the share price alone. Governance reinforces retention: the board has three classes, a 2025 management proposal to remove supermajority voting requirements won 39.4% of shares outstanding and failed, and the 2026-12-03 meeting asks holders only to elect three Class I directors, cast a say-on-pay vote and ratify the auditor. The counter-evidence is real — one share class is more minority-proportional than Rivian's ten-vote Class B, seven of nine directors are independent, the CEO takes no salary, and unearned award shares carry no independent votes because an irrevocable proxy votes them with the rest of the stock — but none of it returns cash or lets a majority change the charter. For a holder at $399.81 the structure therefore offers no cash yield, caps the upside above $2 trillion by 9.1%, and gives no route to force a change of capital-return policy: that argues for sizing the position as a price-only bet, not for rejecting the equity. The open question is whether a $1.58 trillion price for $94.83bn of revenue and a 16.2% automotive gross margin leaves anything after that gate is crossed [S1, S10, S114].

| Contingent dilution, 2025 CEO award | 423.7m shares, 10.7% of shares out; 0 of 12 tranches earned | First gate $2tn, 26.6% above the 2026-10-30 price | warn | S10, S107 |
| CEO ownership | 19.8% of one class; 207.5m shares pledged | Rivian Class B carries 10 votes | good | S10, S114 |
| Public float, calculated | 2,822.5m shares, 71.4% of the count | Above 50% typical of Nasdaq large caps | good | S10 |
| FY2025 revenue | $94.83bn, down 3% from $97.69bn | Automotive $69.53bn, energy $12.77bn, services $12.53bn | warn | S1 |
| Energy share of revenue | 13.5% in FY2025, from 10.3% in FY2024 | 29.8% segment gross margin vs 16.2% automotive | good | S1 |

| 2018-01 | 2018 CEO Performance Award: 303,960,630 options in 12 tranches from a $100bn gate | Created the market-cap-gated pay architecture | S10 |
| 2024-01-30 | Delaware Chancery rescinds the 2018 award in Tornetta v. Musk | Voided a $56bn package | S110 |
| 2024-06-13 | Converts from a Delaware to a Texas corporation | Texas law now governs the charter | S58 |
| 2024-12-02 | Chancery rejects shareholders' ratification and rescinds the award again | Set up the Delaware Supreme Court appeal | S110 |
| 2025-08-03 | Board grants the 2025 CEO Interim Award of 96,000,000 restricted shares | Bridge award, forfeited in full in April 2026 | S10 |
| 2025-09-03 | Board grants the 2025 CEO Performance Award of 423,743,904 shares | The current dilution path | S10 |
| 2025-11-06 | Shareholders approve the award with 76.6% of votes cast | Record-size approved CEO pay package | S59 |
| 2025-12-19 | Delaware Supreme Court unanimously reverses the rescission | Restores the 2018 options with $1 nominal damages | S108 |
| 2026-01-16 | Agrees to invest $2.0bn in xAI, converted to SpaceX Class A stock on 2026-03-12 | Related-party capital allocation | S10 |
| 2026-06-16 | Musk exercises all 303,960,630 options of the 2018 award | Adds 202m shares in nine months | S10, S8 |

arguments.markdown:
Tesla's board is majority independent on paper, but the three decisions that mattered in 2024-2026 — a $2.0bn investment in the CEO's own AI company after shareholders rejected the measure, a pay award that can reach 423.7m shares, and the retention of a classified board — all went against the minority's expressed preference, so key-person and capital-allocation risk are real, formally disclosed, and only partly offset by the award's extreme vesting gates [S10].

### Independence is not the same as accountability

Nine directors sit on the board, seven of them independent under Nasdaq rules, with Robyn Denholm as independent chair since November 2018 and all four committees composed solely of independents. The structure that matters is elsewhere: three staggered classes with three-year terms, supermajority voting requirements that a 2025 management proposal failed to remove with 39.4% of shares outstanding in favour, and two family directors — Elon and Kimbal Musk — in the room. Compensation Committee chair Ira Ehrenpreis has also served on SpaceX's board since February 2026, the counterparty to Tesla's $2.0bn investment and $143.3m of 2025 revenue, a relationship the proxy calls immaterial [S10].

### Pay is gated on market value, not on operating return

The 2025 CEO Performance Award is 423,743,904 shares in 12 equal tranches. Each tranche needs a market-capitalisation milestone first — from $2 trillion, 26.6% above the 2026-10-30 value, through nine $500bn and two $1tn steps to $8.5 trillion — and one of 12 operational milestones: four strategic-product goals (10m active FSD subscriptions, 1m bots delivered, 1m Robotaxis in commercial operation among them) or eight Adjusted EBITDA goals. Each earned share carries a $334.09 offset and a five-year hold, and tranches 11 and 12 also require a board-approved CEO succession framework, the only formal succession mechanism disclosed. Against that, General Motors paid Mary Barra $48.2m of realized compensation in 2025, and Musk has taken no salary since 2019 and has no employment agreement or severance; reported 2025 total compensation of $158.36bn was an accounting value, with realized pay at $0 [S10, S107, S109].

### The xAI vote is the test the board failed

At the 2025-11-06 meeting shareholders approved the pay award with 1,892,235,822 votes for, 564,940,908 against and 12,227,846 abstentions, 76.6% of votes cast. A separate non-binding measure authorising funding for xAI drew 1.06bn votes for and 916.3m against but was recorded as rejected because Tesla's bylaws count abstentions as votes against; on 2026-01-16 the company nonetheless agreed to invest $2.0bn in xAI, completing on 2026-03-12 as SpaceX Class A stock after the SpaceX-xAI merger. The Audit Committee reviews related-person transactions above $120,000 under a written policy, but the sequence shows the review is procedural: a holder should assume future flows to Musk-controlled companies are a board decision, not a shareholder one [S59, S104, S105].

### One person carries the strategy; the bench is uneven

The 10-K says Musk "does not devote his full time and attention to Tesla" and lists management roles at SpaceX, xAI, Neuralink and The Boring Company, while the proxy records that xAI became a SpaceX subsidiary in February 2026 and that Musk is SpaceX's CEO, CTO and chairman. The operating bench is strongest in manufacturing and finance: Tom Zhu, SVP APAC and global vehicle manufacturing since June 2025, joined in 2014 and built Gigafactory Shanghai; Vaibhav Taneja has been CFO since August 2023 and inside Tesla's finance function since 2017. Demand execution is the weak spot: Omead Afshar left in June 2025, Troy Jones was dismissed as head of North American sales in July 2025, the North American service head left in August 2025 and Raj Jegannathan departed in February 2026 after 13 years. Headcount was 134,785 at 2025-12-31; the attrition is concentrated in senior commercial roles [S1, S111, S124].

### What the record confirms, and what diligence must settle

Public records confirm the founder-market fit: Musk co-founded Zip2 (sold to Compaq in 1999) and PayPal (sold to eBay in 2002), has run Tesla since October 2008, and still owns 19.8% with 207,498,721 shares pledged. They also confirm the concentration: no chief operating officer, no permanent North American sales leader, a board with no director who has run a vehicle programme at another OEM, and a CEO whose other companies are now suppliers, investees and counterparties. The gaps a diligence team should close are the succession plan behind tranches 11-12, the terms and lenders behind the pledge, the fairness opinion, if any, for the $2.0bn xAI/SpaceX purchase, and references on Zhu and Taneja from SolarCity and Shanghai. For a 12-month holder the concentration is not a separately observable discount in the share price: it argues for a smaller position and for demanding evidence that Zhu and Taneja can run the operating business while Musk is elsewhere [S10, S2].

::: evidence
**The strongest proof of execution is a manufacturing ramp the founder did not personally run; the strongest doubt is a board that proceeded with a related-party investment after shareholders rejected it.**

Tom Zhu built Gigafactory Shanghai, the largest plant in the system at more than 950,000 units, and Berlin set a quarterly production record in Q3 2026; Tesla passed 10.2m cumulative vehicles. The counterweight is procedural: an xAI funding measure lost on a 1.06bn-to-916.3m vote, yet $2.0bn was committed five weeks later, and the Compensation Committee chair sits on SpaceX's board (sources S9, S104, S10).
:::

arguments.markdown:
Tesla still converts about $1.5 billion of free cash flow a quarter, but the statements no longer show it earning its cost of capital: a 5.5% trailing return on invested capital sits 57 basis points above the ten-year Treasury, $41.8 billion of capex since 2023 has coincided with a 61% fall in operating income, and the profit that remains leans on interest from the cash pile and a payables build rather than on operations.

### Revenue recovered, operating profit did not

| Line item ($M unless stated) | FY2023 | FY2024 | FY2025 | 9M 2026 | TTM to 2026-09-30 | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Revenue | 96,773 | 97,690 | 94,827 | 78,669 | 103,570 | S12, S13, S1, S8 |
| Gross profit | 17,660 | 17,450 | 17,094 | 14,965 | 19,974 | S12, S13, S1, S8 |
| Gross margin | 18.2% | 17.9% | 18.0% | 19.0% | 19.3% | S12, S13, S1, S8 |
| Research and development | 3,969 | 4,540 | 6,411 | 7,078 | 8,861 | S12, S13, S1, S8 |
| Selling, general and administrative | 4,800 | 5,150 | 5,834 | 5,830 | 7,485 | S12, S13, S1, S8 |
| Operating income | 8,891 | 7,076 | 4,355 | 2,057 | 3,466 | S12, S13, S1, S8 |
| Operating margin | 9.2% | 7.2% | 4.6% | 2.6% | 3.3% | S12, S13, S1, S8 |
| Net income | 14,997 | 7,091 | 3,794 | 2,378 | 3,218 | S12, S13, S1, S8 |
| Diluted EPS ($) | 4.30 | 2.04 | 1.08 | 0.67 | 0.91 | S12, S13, S1, S8 |
| Operating cash flow | 13,256 | 14,923 | 14,747 | 14,897 | 18,710 | S12, S13, S1, S8 |
| Capital expenditure | 8,898 | 11,339 | 8,527 | 13,014 | 15,407 | S12, S13, S1, S8 |
| Free cash flow | 4,358 | 3,584 | 6,220 | 1,883 | 3,296 | S12, S13, S1, S8 |

Revenue fell for two years before the 2026 rebound while operating income fell throughout, from $8,891M in FY2023 to $3,466M trailing, because research and development rose from $3,969M to $8,861M and selling and administrative cost from $4,800M to $7,485M against gross profit that moved between $17.1B and $20.0B. The Q3 2026 operating margin of 2.6% came on revenue that was flat year on year with deliveries down 2% to 486,532 from 497,099, so price, mix and a weaker dollar carried the top line while volume slipped; the nine-month increase of 13% owed more to the prior year's factory changeover than to 2026 demand. Reported versus adjusted is a wide gap: Q3 2026 GAAP net income of $787M against non-GAAP of $1,697M, and diluted EPS of $0.22 against $0.48 [S12, S13, S1, S8].

### Free cash flow is a payables loan and a capex pause

Nine-month operating cash flow of $14,897M exceeded the $13,014M of capital expenditure to leave $1,883M of free cash flow, against $6,220M for FY2025. Two facts weaken the conversion. Management attributes $3.51 billion of the $3.96 billion year-on-year operating-cash-flow increase to working capital: accounts payable rose $3,868M from 2025-12-31 to $17,239M, the cash conversion cycle fell to 2.6 days from 13.0, and without the payables build nine-month free cash flow would have been about -$1,985M. Capital expenditure nearly doubled from $6,134M a year earlier, and the 2026 plan was restated between filings — "in excess of $25 billion" in the July 2026 quarterly report, "in excess of $20 billion" in the October 2026 one, and about $20 billion on the Q3 2026 call — so the year closes near break-even free cash flow rather than FY2025's $6.2B. Inventory rose $1,700M to $14,092M with finished goods at $5,243M, and inventory write-downs fell to $217M from $275M [S8, S9, S83].

### The balance sheet carries the plan; the off-balance items carry the risk

| Metric | FY2023 | FY2024 | FY2025 | TTM to 2026-09-30 | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Return on invested capital | 28.3% | 13.7% | 7.0% | 5.5% | S12, S13, S1, S8 |
| Return on equity | 27.9% | 10.5% | 4.9% | 3.8% | S12, S13, S1, S8 |
| Return on assets | 15.9% | 6.2% | 2.9% | 2.2% | S12, S13, S1, S8 |
| Days sales outstanding | 13.2 | 16.5 | 17.6 | 16.3 | S12, S13, S1, S8 |
| Days inventory outstanding | 62.9 | 54.7 | 58.2 | 61.5 | S12, S13, S1, S8 |
| Days payables outstanding | 66.6 | 56.7 | 62.8 | 75.3 | S12, S13, S1, S8 |
| Cash conversion cycle (days) | 9.5 | 14.4 | 13.0 | 2.6 | S12, S13, S1, S8 |
| Interest coverage | 56.99x | 20.22x | 12.88x | 9.96x | S12, S13, S1, S8 |
| Stock-based compensation / revenue | 1.9% | 2.0% | 3.0% | 4.2% | S12, S13, S1, S8 |
| Capital expenditure / revenue | 9.2% | 11.6% | 9.0% | 16.5% (9M) | S12, S13, S1, S8 |
| Net cash | 24,437 | 28,685 | 35,906 | 36,180 | S12, S13, S1, S8 |

Cash of $17,853M and short-term investments of $27,594M against $9,267M of debt gave $36,180M of net cash at 2026-09-30, and three credit agreements signed in September 2026 lifted unused committed facilities to $30.00B from $6.43B at 2025-12-31, so the $20B capex year is funded several times over without equity. The obligations outside the debt line matter more: $7,955M of minimum lease payments at 2025-12-31 ($1,320M within twelve months), an accrued warranty reserve of $7,414M that grew 20.9% in nine months against 10% delivery growth, and $7,055M of deferred revenue. Goodwill and intangibles of $381M are 0.2% of assets, so there is no acquisition accounting to discount, and interest coverage of 9.96x is ample but has fallen from 56.99x in FY2023 as operating income shrank [S8, S1].

### The capital is not earning its keep

Returns have fallen faster than margins. Return on invested capital went from 28.3% in FY2023 to 13.7%, 7.0% and 5.5% trailing, and return on equity from 27.9% to 3.8%; the 5.5% compares with a 4.93% ten-year Treasury yield on 2026-10-30, leaving almost no premium for equity risk and far less than an automaker with this operating volatility should demand. The capex record explains it: $41,778M spent in FY2023, FY2024, FY2025 and the first nine months of 2026 against a $5,425M fall in operating income over the same span — measured from FY2022's peak of $13,656M the fall is $10,190M — an incremental return that is negative at the group level. Nothing has been returned to shareholders: no dividend and no repurchase from FY2021 to Q3 2026, while $2.00B of cash went into SpaceX common stock in the first nine months of 2026 and the FY2025 report disclosed an agreement to make a minority equity investment in xAI, both companies controlled by the chief executive. GM authorised a $20B repurchase in the same quarter [S12, S13, S1, S8, S115].

### What flatters the number, and what would change it

Three items soften the reported result. Interest income of $1,301M was 42.9% of nine-month pre-tax income and $445M was 46.5% of the Q3 2026 figure, up from 17.5% in FY2024. Stock-based compensation of $3,346M in nine months (4.3% of revenue) is the main reason non-GAAP profit more than doubles GAAP profit, and an effective tax rate of 20% against 27% was helped by a valuation-allowance release on California deferred tax assets in Q2 2026. Cost of automotive sales also benefited from what management calls warranty adjustments while the warranty reserve rose 20.9%. Sensitivity: a percentage point of ex-credit automotive margin is worth about $800M a year on $80B of automotive revenue, roughly six times a point of energy margin at $12.5B, and each $1B of capex is $1B of free cash flow. On a base case of flat volume, a 30% energy margin, 18% ex-credit automotive margin and $20B of capex, FY2027 free cash flow is about $2B; the downside, with energy back at Q2 2026's 20.4% and automotive back at 15.4%, is roughly -$3B; the upside, with energy held at 33% and capex unchanged, is about $4B. The variable that moves the outcome most is capex — a management decision worth $5B in a single restatement between July and October 2026, more than six points of automotive margin [S8, S83, S1, S117].

::: info danger
The most serious red flag is the composition of free cash flow rather than its level: nine-month free cash flow is smaller than the rise in payables that produced it, capital expenditure has already been re-scoped once in the same quarter that $30B of new credit lines were arranged, and the cash balance that generates almost half of pre-tax profit is the only reason reported earnings look positive at the operating level. Reported free cash flow should be treated as a ceiling, not a run-rate.
:::

arguments.markdown:
Tesla's legal and ownership structure is unusually plain for a founder-led company — one class of stock, a Texas parent with no VIE or dual-class layer, and a CEO who owns 19.8% — so what constrains a 12-month equity return is not the charter but a 10.7% contingent dilution struck at market capitalisations from $2 trillion upward, no dividend or buyback, and a classified board that minority holders cannot replace. Tesla, Inc. trades on Nasdaq under TSLA; 3,952,648,559 shares were outstanding at 2026-09-30 and market capitalisation was $1.58 trillion at the $399.81 close on 2026-10-30 [S10, S112].

### One operating group, no holding-company layer

The registrant was incorporated in Delaware on 2003-07-01 and converted to a Texas corporation on 2024-06-13. The structure is flat: country operating companies, single-purpose solar and lease vehicles and insurance captives, with no contractual-control or variable-interest layer separating legal from economic ownership. The filings disclose no separate intellectual-property holding company; the listed parent files the group's consolidated accounts, while the operating subsidiaries hold the plants, local licences and financing books [S1, S58].

| Entity | Jurisdiction | Type | Role | Ownership | Controller | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Tesla, Inc. | Texas, US | Listed corporation | Registrant; consolidated group; public equity | 100% of subsidiaries | Board; Musk 19.8% | S1, S58 |
| Tesla (Shanghai) Co., Ltd. | China | Limited liability company | Gigafactory and Megafactory Shanghai operating entity | 100% | Tesla, Inc. | S1 |
| Tesla Manufacturing Brandenburg SE | Germany | European company | Gigafactory Berlin-Brandenburg | 100% | Tesla, Inc. | S1 |
| Tesla Robotaxi, LLC | Texas, US | LLC | Robotaxi operations | 100% | Tesla, Inc. | S1 |

### The dilution path runs through a $2 trillion gate

Musk holds 699,580,882 shares, or 19.8%, including 286,428,773 restricted shares from the 2018 award, and 207,498,721 of his shares are pledged against personal borrowings. The 2018 award was exercised in full on 2026-06-16 for 303,960,630 shares, which is why the count rose 202m, or 5.4%, in the nine months to 2026-09-30. Forward dilution is the 2025 CEO Performance Award: 423,743,904 shares, 10.7% of the current count, in 12 equal tranches, none earned as of 2026-10-19. Each earned share carries a $334.09 offset payable in cash or shares, a five-year holding requirement, and every tranche needs a market-cap milestone before any operating milestone counts, starting at $2 trillion — 26.6% above the 2026-10-30 value — then nine $500bn and two $1tn increments to $8.5 trillion. The economics sit closer to a premium-struck option than a free grant: at $399.81 the gross spread is $65.72 a share, and at the plan's top the transfer is $769.6bn net of offsets, 9.1% of an $8.5 trillion capitalisation [S10, S107].

| Holder | Class | Shares | % of shares | % of votes | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Elon Musk (CEO, director) | Common | 699,580,882 | 19.8% | 19.8% | S10 |
| Vanguard Capital Management | Common | 210,796,512 | 5.3% | 5.3% | S10 |
| All directors and officers (11 persons) | Common | 706,496,615 | 20.0% | 20.0% | S10 |
| Public float, calculated (excludes insider shares and 423.7m unvested restricted shares) | Common | 2,822,408,040 | 71.4% | 71.4% | S10 |

### What the customer actually buys

The business is three P&Ls sold to different budget owners. Automotive ($69.53bn of FY2025 revenue, 73% of the total) sells vehicles to consumers, leasing companies and fleets, and monetises the installed base through Supercharging, service, parts, used cars and insurance; the software layer is FSD (Supervised), with 1.74m active subscriptions at 2026-09-30. Energy ($12.77bn, 13.5% of revenue, 29.8% gross margin) sells Megapack and Powerwall to utilities, developers, industrial sites and, increasingly, data-centre operators whose budget is a power-availability capex line rather than a transport one. Services ($12.53bn, +19% in FY2025) is largely a captive aftermarket on Tesla's own parc. Growth has shifted from unit volume — Q3 2026 deliveries were 486,532, down 2% year on year — to storage deployment (13.7 GWh in Q3 2026), software attach and the Robotaxi and Optimus optionality the pay award is designed to reward [S1, S9].

### Capacity is built; volume is the question

Tesla runs eight primary plants: Fremont (Model 3/Y, more than 550,000 units), Shanghai (more than 950,000), Berlin (more than 375,000), Texas (Model Y more than 375,000, Cybertruck and Cybercab more than 125,000 each) and Nevada (Semi 25,000), plus Megapack plants in California (40 GWh), Shanghai (20 GWh) and Texas (50 GWh). Headcount was 134,785 at 2025-12-31. Nameplate vehicle capacity of 2.53m units against an annualised Q3 2026 run rate of 1.95m leaves a fifth of the system idle, while Semi, Cybercab and Optimus lines add depreciation before revenue; that is the mechanism by which a flat revenue year becomes either margin expansion or further compression [S9, S1].

### No payout, and a board that cannot be replaced

Tesla has never paid a dividend, has no repurchase authorisation and made no purchases in FY2025, while holding $45.45bn of cash and short-term investments; with no distribution, a holder's 12-month total return is the share price alone. Governance reinforces retention: the board has three classes, a 2025 management proposal to remove supermajority voting requirements won 39.4% of shares outstanding and failed, and the 2026-12-03 meeting asks holders only to elect three Class I directors, cast a say-on-pay vote and ratify the auditor. The counter-evidence is real — one share class is more minority-proportional than Rivian's ten-vote Class B, seven of nine directors are independent, the CEO takes no salary, and unearned award shares carry no independent votes because an irrevocable proxy votes them with the rest of the stock — but none of it returns cash or lets a majority change the charter. For a holder at $399.81 the structure therefore offers no cash yield, caps the upside above $2 trillion by 9.1%, and gives no route to force a change of capital-return policy: that argues for sizing the position as a price-only bet, not for rejecting the equity. The open question is whether a $1.58 trillion price for $94.83bn of revenue and a 16.2% automotive gross margin leaves anything after that gate is crossed [S1, S10, S114].

arguments.markdown:
Tesla converted $1,531M of free cash flow in Q3 2026, but the statements no longer show it earning its cost of capital: a 5.5% trailing return on invested capital sits 57 basis points above the ten-year Treasury, $41,778M of capex since 2023 has coincided with a 61% fall in operating income, and the profit that remains leans on interest from the cash pile and a payables build rather than on operations [S8, S12, S11].

### Revenue recovered, operating profit did not

| Line item ($M unless stated) | FY2023 | FY2024 | FY2025 | 9M 2026 | TTM to 2026-09-30 | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Revenue | 96,773 | 97,690 | 94,827 | 78,669 | 103,570 | S12, S13, S1, S8 |
| Gross profit | 17,660 | 17,450 | 17,094 | 14,965 | 19,974 | S12, S13, S1, S8 |
| Gross margin | 18.2% | 17.9% | 18.0% | 19.0% | 19.3% | S12, S13, S1, S8 |
| Research and development | 3,969 | 4,540 | 6,411 | 7,078 | 8,861 | S12, S13, S1, S8 |
| Selling, general and administrative | 4,800 | 5,150 | 5,834 | 5,830 | 7,485 | S12, S13, S1, S8 |
| Operating income | 8,891 | 7,076 | 4,355 | 2,057 | 3,466 | S12, S13, S1, S8 |
| Operating margin | 9.2% | 7.2% | 4.6% | 2.6% | 3.3% | S12, S13, S1, S8 |
| Net income | 14,997 | 7,091 | 3,794 | 2,378 | 3,218 | S12, S13, S1, S8 |
| Diluted EPS ($) | 4.30 | 2.04 | 1.08 | 0.67 | 0.91 | S12, S13, S1, S8 |
| Operating cash flow | 13,256 | 14,923 | 14,747 | 14,897 | 18,710 | S12, S13, S1, S8 |
| Capital expenditure | 8,898 | 11,339 | 8,527 | 13,014 | 15,407 | S12, S13, S1, S8 |
| Free cash flow | 4,358 | 3,584 | 6,220 | 1,883 | 3,296 | S12, S13, S1, S8 |

Revenue fell for two years before the 2026 rebound while operating income fell throughout, from $8,891M in FY2023 to $3,466M trailing, because research and development rose from $3,969M to $8,861M and selling and administrative cost from $4,800M to $7,485M against gross profit that stayed between $17.1B and $20.0B. The Q3 2026 operating margin of 2.6% came on revenue flat year on year with deliveries down 2% to 486,532 from 497,099, so price, mix and a weaker dollar carried the top line while volume slipped. Reported against adjusted is a wide gap: Q3 2026 GAAP net income of $787M against non-GAAP of $1,697M, and diluted EPS of $0.22 against $0.48. FY2023's $14,997M net income included a $5,001M tax benefit that has not recurred [S12, S13, S1, S8].

### Free cash flow is a payables loan and a capex pause

Nine-month operating cash flow of $14,897M exceeded the $13,014M of capital expenditure to leave $1,883M of free cash flow, against $6,220M for FY2025. Two facts weaken the conversion. Management attributes $3.51 billion of the $3.96 billion year-on-year operating-cash-flow increase to working capital, and in Q3 2026 alone free cash flow of $1,531M rested on a $2,590M working-capital inflow, of which accounts payable supplied $1,920M and accrued liabilities $1,950M; stripping it out, quarterly free cash flow was -$1,059M, and $3,670M of capex sat in liabilities at 2026-09-30. Across the nine months, payables rose $3,868M from 2025-12-31 to $17,239M and the cash conversion cycle fell to 2.6 days from 13.0, so without the payables build nine-month free cash flow would have been -$1,985M. Capital expenditure nearly doubled from $6,134M a year earlier, and the 2026 plan was restated between filings — "in excess of $25 billion" in the July 2026 report, "in excess of $20 billion" in the October 2026 one, and $20 billion on the Q3 2026 call — leaving full-year 2026 free cash flow between -$1,290M and +$1,160M depending on whether Q4 operating cash flow matches Q4 2025's $3,813M or Q3 2026's $6,263M [S8, S9, S83, S102].

### The balance sheet carries the plan; the off-balance items carry the risk

| Metric | FY2023 | FY2024 | FY2025 | TTM to 2026-09-30 | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Return on invested capital | 28.3% | 13.7% | 7.0% | 5.5% | S12, S13, S1, S8 |
| Return on equity | 27.9% | 10.5% | 4.9% | 3.8% | S12, S13, S1, S8 |
| Return on assets | 15.9% | 6.2% | 2.9% | 2.2% | S12, S13, S1, S8 |
| Days sales outstanding | 13.2 | 16.5 | 17.6 | 16.3 | S12, S13, S1, S8 |
| Days inventory outstanding | 62.9 | 54.7 | 58.2 | 61.5 | S12, S13, S1, S8 |
| Days payables outstanding | 66.6 | 56.7 | 62.8 | 75.3 | S12, S13, S1, S8 |
| Cash conversion cycle (days) | 9.5 | 14.4 | 13.0 | 2.6 | S12, S13, S1, S8 |
| Interest coverage | 56.99x | 20.22x | 12.88x | 9.96x | S12, S13, S1, S8 |
| Stock-based compensation / revenue | 1.9% | 2.0% | 3.0% | 4.2% | S12, S13, S1, S8 |
| Capital expenditure / revenue | 9.2% | 11.6% | 9.0% | 16.5% (9M) | S12, S13, S1, S8 |
| Net cash | 24,437 | 28,685 | 35,906 | 36,180 | S12, S13, S1, S8 |

Cash of $17,853M and short-term investments of $27,594M against $9,267M of debt gave $36,180M of net cash at 2026-09-30, and three credit agreements signed in September 2026 lifted unused committed facilities to $30.00B from $6.43B at 2025-12-31, so the $20B capex year is funded several times over without equity. The obligations outside the debt line matter more: $7,955M of minimum lease payments at 2025-12-31, of which $1,320M falls due within twelve months; an accrued warranty reserve of $7,414M that grew 20.9% in nine months against 10% delivery growth; and $7,055M of deferred revenue. Goodwill and intangibles of $381M are 0.2% of assets, so there is no acquisition accounting to discount, and interest coverage of 9.96x is ample but has fallen from 56.99x in FY2023 as operating income shrank [S8, S1].

### The capital is not earning its keep

Returns have fallen faster than margins. Return on invested capital went from 28.3% in FY2023 to 13.7%, 7.0% and 5.5% trailing, and return on equity from 27.9% to 3.8%; the 5.5% compares with a 4.93% ten-year Treasury yield on 2026-10-30, leaving 57 basis points for equity risk in a business whose operating margin has halved twice in three years. The capex record explains it: $41,778M spent in FY2023, FY2024, FY2025 and the first nine months of 2026 against a $5,425M fall in operating income over the same span — from FY2022's peak of $13,656M the fall is $10,190M — an incremental return that is negative at group level. Nothing has been returned to shareholders: no dividend and no repurchase from FY2021 to Q3 2026, while $2,000M of cash went into SpaceX common stock in the first nine months of 2026, the FY2025 report disclosed an agreement to make a minority equity investment in xAI, and media reported in January 2026 that the xAI investment was $2 billion. GM authorised a $20B repurchase in the same quarter [S1, S8, S115, S104].

### What flatters the number, and what would change it

Four items soften the reported result. Interest income of $1,301M was 42.9% of nine-month pre-tax income, and $445M was 46.5% of the Q3 2026 figure, against 17.5% in FY2024. Stock-based compensation of $3,346M in nine months is 4.3% of revenue and the main reason non-GAAP profit more than doubles GAAP profit; the reported EPS is struck on 3,240M basic and 3,541M diluted weighted-average shares, while the 2026-09-30 cover reports 3,952,648,559 shares outstanding after the June 2026 exercise of the 2018 award — a gap of about 410M shares the filings do not reconcile, and one that would lower every per-share figure if the cover count is the live one. An effective tax rate of 20% against 27% was helped by a valuation-allowance release on California deferred tax assets in Q2 2026. Cost of automotive sales also benefited from what management calls warranty adjustments while the warranty reserve rose 20.9%. Sensitivity: a percentage point of ex-credit automotive margin is worth $800M a year on $80,000M of automotive revenue, 6.4 times a point of energy margin at $12,500M, and each $1B of capex is $1B of free cash flow. Base case FY2027 free cash flow of $2,000M assumes operating cash flow of $22,000M less capex of $20,000M with energy at 30% and automotive at 18%; energy back at Q2 2026's 20.4% and automotive at 15.4% removes $3,360M and turns it into -$1,360M; energy held at 33.1% adds $390M. The variable that moves the outcome most is capex, a management decision worth $5B in a single restatement between July and October 2026 — more than six points of automotive margin. The diligence question is what the 2027 capex number is and whether the payables build reflects renegotiated terms or deferred payments [S8, S83, S1, S117, S102].

::: info danger
The most serious red flag is the composition of free cash flow rather than its level: nine-month free cash flow is smaller than the rise in payables that produced it, capital expenditure was re-scoped in the same quarter that new credit lines were arranged, and the cash balance generating almost half of pre-tax profit is the only reason reported earnings look positive at the operating level. Reported free cash flow is a ceiling, not a run-rate.
:::

China's retail sales of new energy vehicles (NEVs) fell 16.7% year-on-year to 1.084 million in September, but rose 7.8% from August, according to data released by the China Passenger Car Association (CPCA) on Monday.
The decline marked the ninth consecutive month of falling NEV retail sales from a year earlier. Sales in the first 9 months totaled 7.758 million, down 12.8%.
Battery electric vehicles (BEVs) outperformed hybrid vehicles, with retail sales in September totaling 765,000 units — a 7.38% year-on-year decline but a 9.60% month-on-month increase.

NEV penetration reached 84.5% among domestic Chinese brands and 44.9% among luxury brands, compared with just 15.9% among mainstream joint-venture brands.
NEV retail sales at domestic brands fell 19% year-on-year in September, while those at mainstream joint-venture brands rose 36% and luxury brands declined 8%. Domestic A00-segment electric vehicles suffered steep declines due to unfavorable subsidy policies, the CPCA said.
NEV wholesale sales rose 11.3% year-on-year and 10.0% month-on-month to 1.666 million in September. NEV penetration at the wholesale level reached a record 65.4%, up 12 percentage points from a year earlier.

Exports continued to support the industry. China's total passenger vehicle exports rose 73.7% year-on-year to 917,000 in September, accounting for 36% of automakers' passenger vehicle sales.
NEV exports surged 163.5% year-on-year and rose 7.7% month-on-month to 558,000 in September. They accounted for 60.8% of total passenger vehicle exports, up 21 percentage points from a year earlier. NEV exports in the first 9 months rose 138.8% to 3.887 million.

Retail sales of gasoline-powered vehicles fell 43% year-on-year in September. Within that category, sales of conventional gasoline vehicles dropped 49%, while conventional hybrids rose 25%.
The CPCA attributed September's retail decline to several factors. The Mid-Autumn Festival holiday fell earlier, in late September, with sales weakening notably that week. A rush to buy before subsidies expired in some provinces last September also created a high comparison base.
Meanwhile, high oil prices continued to dampen demand for gasoline vehicles. AI-driven surges in memory and chip prices, along with supply shortages, slowed the sales contribution from new NEV models, the CPCA said.
BYD (HKEX: 1211) continued to lead China's domestic NEV retail market, with September sales of 246,816 vehicles.
Geely Auto (HKEX: 0175) and Leapmotor (HKEX: 9863) ranked second and third, with 119,682 and 78,202 vehicles, respectively.
They were followed by Tesla (NASDAQ: TSLA) with 64,837, Changan Automobile with 61,732 and SAIC-GM-Wuling with 54,810.
Chery (HKEX: 9973) recorded NEV retail sales of 46,860 in September, followed by SAIC Passenger Vehicle with 40,280 and Xiaomi (HKEX: 1810) with 40,015.
Huawei-backed HIMA (Harmony Intelligent Mobility Alliance) sold 37,490 vehicles, Nio (NYSE: NIO) sold 37,231, GWM (HKEX: 2333) sold 32,048, Li Auto (Nasdaq: LI) sold 31,817 and Xpeng (NYSE: XPEV) sold 30,599.
China's emerging EV makers held a 23.6% share of the retail market in September, up 3.4 percentage points from a year earlier, driven mainly by Leapmotor and Nio, the CPCA said.
BEVs accounted for 75% of these automakers' sales, up from 70% a year earlier.
Looking ahead to October, the CPCA said the month has 18 working days, unchanged from a year earlier. With the Mid-Autumn Festival holiday already over in September, more time will be available for sales, potentially helping showroom traffic recover.
Trade-in subsidies are expected to increase later this year after a slower start, contrasting with the gradual withdrawal of subsidies last October and helping stabilize the auto market, the CPCA said.
High oil prices will continue to accelerate the shift from gasoline vehicles to NEVs, with NEV penetration expected to remain above 65%, the CPCA added.

{"content":[{"type":"text","text":"## Company Overview (company_overview, revision 5 by Company Analyst, 8,950 characters)
Tesla's legal and ownership structure is unusually plain for a founder-led company — one class of stock, a Texas parent with no VIE or dual-class layer, and a CEO who owns 19.8% — so what constrains a 12-month equity return is not the charter but a 10.7% contingent dilution struck at market capitalisations from $2 trillion upward, no dividend or buyback, and a classified board that minority holders cannot replace. Tesla, Inc. trades on Nasdaq under TSLA; 3,952,648,559 shares were outstanding at 2026-09-30 and market capitalisation was $1.58 trillion at the $399.81 close on 2026-10-30 [S10, S112].

### One operating group, no holding-company layer

The registrant was incorporated in Delaware on 2003-07-01 and converted to a Texas corporation on 2024-06-13. The structure is flat: country operating companies, single-purpose solar and lease vehicles and insurance captives, with no contractual-control or variable-interest layer separating legal from economic ownership. The filings disclose no separate intellectual-property holding company; the listed parent files the group's consolidated accounts, while the operating subsidiaries hold the plants, local licences and financing books [S1, S58].

| Entity | Jurisdiction | Type | Role | Ownership | Controller | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Tesla, Inc. | Texas, US | Listed corporation | Registrant; consolidated group; public equity | 100% of subsidiaries | Board; Musk 19.8% | S1, S58 |
| Tesla (Shanghai) Co., Ltd. | China | Limited liability company | Gigafactory and Megafactory Shanghai operating entity | 100% | Tesla, Inc. | S1 |
| Tesla Manufacturing Brandenburg SE | Germany | European company | Gigafactory Berlin-Brandenburg | 100% | Tesla, Inc. | S1 |
| Tesla Robotaxi, LLC | Texas, US | LLC | Robotaxi operations | 100% | Tesla, Inc. | S1 |

### The dilution path runs through a $2 trillion gate

Musk holds 699,580,882 shares, or 19.8%, including 286,428,773 restricted shares from the 2018 award, and 207,498,721 of his shares are pledged against personal borrowings. The 2018 award was exercised in full on 2026-06-16 for 303,960,630 shares, which is why the count rose 202m, or 5.4%, in the nine months to 2026-09-30. Forward dilution is the 2025 CEO Performance Award: 423,743,904 shares, 10.7% of the current count, in 12 equal tranches, none earned as of 2026-10-19. Each earned share carries a $334.09 offset payable in cash or shares, a five-year holding requirement, and every tranche needs a market-cap milestone before any operating milestone counts, starting at $2 trillion — 26.6% above the 2026-10-30 value — then nine $500bn and two $1tn increments to $8.5 trillion. The economics sit closer to a premium-struck option than a free grant: at $399.81 the gross spread is $65.72 a share, and at the plan's top the transfer is $769.6bn net of offsets, 9.1% of an $8.5 trillion capitalisation [S10, S107].

|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Elon Musk (CEO, director) | Common | 699,580,882 | 19.8% | 19.8% | S10 |
| Vanguard Capital Management | Common | 210,796,512 | 5.3% | 5.3% | S10 |
| All directors and officers (11 persons) | Common | 706,496,615 | 20.0% | 20.0% | S10 |
| Public float, calculated (excludes insider shares and 423.7m unvested restricted shares) | Common | 2,822,408,040 | 71.4% | 71.4% | S10 |

### What the customer actually buys

The business is three P&Ls sold to different budget owners. Automotive ($69.53bn of FY2025 revenue, 73% of the total) sells vehicles to consumers, leasing companies and fleets, and monetises the installed base through Supercharging, service, parts, used cars and insurance; the software layer is FSD (Supervised), with 1.74m active subscriptions at 2026-09-30. Energy ($12.77bn, 13.5% of revenue, 29.8% gross margin) sells Megapack and Powerwall to utilities, developers, industrial sites and, increasingly, data-centre operators whose budget is a power-availability capex line rather than a transport one. Services ($12.53bn, +19% in FY2025) is largely a captive aftermarket on Tesla's own parc. Growth has shifted from unit volume — Q3 2026 deliveries were 486,532, down 2% year on year — to storage deployment (13.7 GWh in Q3 2026), software attach and the Robotaxi and Optimus optionality the pay award is designed to reward [S1, S9].

### Capacity is built; volume is the question

Tesla runs eight primary plants: Fremont (Model 3/Y, more than 550,000 units), Shanghai (more than 950,000), Berlin (more than 375,000), Texas (Model Y more than 375,000, Cybertruck and Cybercab more than 125,000 each) and Nevada (Semi 25,000), plus Megapack plants in California (40 GWh), Shanghai (20 GWh) and Texas (50 GWh). Headcount was 134,785 at 2025-12-31. Nameplate vehicle capacity of 2.53m units against an annualised Q3 2026 run rate of 1.95m leaves a fifth of the system idle, while Semi, Cybercab and Optimus lines add depreciation before revenue; that is the mechanism by which a flat revenue year becomes either margin expansion or further compression [S9, S1].

### No payout, and a board that cannot be replaced

Tesla has never paid a dividend, has no repurchase authorisation and made no purchases in FY2025, while holding $45.45bn of cash and short-term investments; with no distribution, a holder's 12-month total return is the share price alone. Governance reinforces retention: the board has three classes, a 2025 management proposal to remove supermajority voting requirements won 39.4% of shares outstanding and failed, and the 2026-12-03 meeting asks holders only to elect three Class I directors, cast a say-on-pay vote and ratify the auditor. The counter-evidence is real — one share class is more minority-proportional than Rivian's ten-vote Class B, seven of nine directors are independent, the CEO takes no salary, and unearned award shares carry no independent votes because an irrevocable proxy votes them with the rest of the stock — but none of it returns cash or lets a majority change the charter. For a holder at $399.81 the structure therefore offers no cash yield, caps the upside above $2 trillion by 9.1%, and gives no route to force a change of capital-return policy: that argues for sizing the position as a price-only bet, not for rejecting the equity. The open question is whether a $1.58 trillion price for $94.83bn of revenue and a 16.2% automotive gross margin leaves anything after that gate is crossed [S1, S10, S114].

arguments.markdown:
Tesla converted $1,531M of free cash flow in Q3 2026, but the statements no longer show it earning its cost of capital: a 5.5% trailing return on invested capital sits 57 basis points above the ten-year Treasury, $41,778M of capex since 2023 has coincided with a 61% fall in operating income, and the profit that remains leans on interest from the cash pile and a payables build rather than on operations [S8, S12, S11].

### Revenue recovered, operating profit did not

| Line item ($M unless stated) | FY2023 | FY2024 | FY2025 | 9M 2026 | TTM to 2026-09-30 | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Revenue | 96,773 | 97,690 | 94,827 | 78,669 | 103,570 | S12, S13, S1, S8 |
| Gross profit | 17,660 | 17,450 | 17,094 | 14,965 | 19,974 | S12, S13, S1, S8 |
| Gross margin | 18.2% | 17.9% | 18.0% | 19.0% | 19.3% | S12, S13, S1, S8 |
| Research and development | 3,969 | 4,540 | 6,411 | 7,078 | 8,861 | S12, S13, S1, S8 |
| Selling, general and administrative | 4,800 | 5,150 | 5,834 | 5,830 | 7,485 | S12, S13, S1, S8 |
| Operating income | 8,891 | 7,076 | 4,355 | 2,057 | 3,466 | S12, S13, S1, S8 |
| Operating margin | 9.2% | 7.2% | 4.6% | 2.6% | 3.3% | S12, S13, S1, S8 |
| Net income | 14,997 | 7,091 | 3,794 | 2,378 | 3,218 | S12, S13, S1, S8 |
| Diluted EPS ($) | 4.30 | 2.04 | 1.08 | 0.67 | 0.91 | S12, S13, S1, S8 |
| Operating cash flow | 13,256 | 14,923 | 14,747 | 14,897 | 18,710 | S12, S13, S1, S8 |
| Capital expenditure | 8,898 | 11,339 | 8,527 | 13,014 | 15,407 | S12, S13, S1, S8 |
| Free cash flow | 4,358 | 3,584 | 6,220 | 1,883 | 3,296 | S12, S13, S1, S8 |

Revenue fell for two years before the 2026 rebound while operating income fell throughout, from $8,891M in FY2023 to $3,466M trailing, because research and development rose from $3,969M to $8,861M and selling and administrative cost from $4,800M to $7,485M against gross profit that stayed between $17.1B and $20.0B. The Q3 2026 operating margin of 2.6% came on revenue flat year on year with deliveries down 2% to 486,532 from 497,099, so price, mix and a weaker dollar carried the top line while volume slipped. Reported against adjusted is a wide gap: Q3 2026 GAAP net income of $787M against non-GAAP of $1,697M, and diluted EPS of $0.22 against $0.48. FY2023's $14,997M net income included a $5,001M deferred-tax valuation-allowance release that has not recurred at that scale [S12, S13, S1, S8].

### Free cash flow is a payables loan and a capex pause

Nine-month operating cash flow of $14,897M exceeded the $13,014M of capital expenditure to leave $1,883M of free cash flow, against $6,220M for FY2025. Two facts weaken the conversion. Management attributes $3.51 billion of the $3.96 billion year-on-year operating-cash-flow increase to working capital, and in Q3 2026 alone free cash flow of $1,531M rested on a $2,590M working-capital inflow, of which accounts payable supplied $1,920M and accrued liabilities $1,950M; stripping it out, quarterly free cash flow was -$1,059M, and $3,670M of capex sat in liabilities at 2026-09-30. Across the nine months, payables rose $3,868M from 2025-12-31 to $17,239M and the cash conversion cycle fell to 2.6 days from 13.0, so without the payables build nine-month free cash flow would have been -$1,985M. Capital expenditure nearly doubled from $6,134M a year earlier, and the 2026 plan was restated between filings — "in excess of $25 billion" in the July 2026 report, "in excess of $20 billion" in the October 2026 one, and $20 billion on the Q3 2026 call — leaving full-year 2026 free cash flow between -$1,290M and +$1,160M depending on whether Q4 operating cash flow matches Q4 2025's $3,813M or Q3 2026's $6,263M [S8, S9, S83, S102].

### The balance sheet carries the plan; the off-balance items carry the risk

| Metric | FY2023 | FY2024 | FY2025 | TTM to 2026-09-30 | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Return on invested capital | 28.3% | 13.7% | 7.0% | 5.5% | S12, S13, S1, S8 |
| Return on equity | 27.9% | 10.5% | 4.9% | 3.8% | S12, S13, S1, S8 |
| Return on assets | 15.9% | 6.2% | 2.9% | 2.2% | S12, S13, S1, S8 |
| Days sales outstanding | 13.2 | 16.5 | 17.6 | 16.3 | S12, S13, S1, S8 |
| Days inventory outstanding | 62.9 | 54.7 | 58.2 | 61.5 | S12, S13, S1, S8 |
| Days payables outstanding | 66.6 | 56.7 | 62.8 | 75.3 | S12, S13, S1, S8 |
| Cash conversion cycle (days) | 9.5 | 14.4 | 13.0 | 2.6 | S12, S13, S1, S8 |
| Interest coverage | 56.99x | 20.22x | 12.88x | 9.96x | S12, S13, S1, S8 |
| Stock-based compensation / revenue | 1.9% | 2.0% | 3.0% | 4.2% | S12, S13, S1, S8 |
| Capital expenditure / revenue | 9.2% | 11.6% | 9.0% | 16.5% (9M) | S12, S13, S1, S8 |
| Net cash | 24,437 | 28,685 | 35,906 | 36,180 | S12, S13, S1, S8 |

Cash of $17,853M and short-term investments of $27,594M against $9,267M of debt gave $36,180M of net cash at 2026-09-30, and three credit agreements signed in September 2026 lifted unused committed facilities to $30.00B from $6.43B at 2025-12-31, so the $20B capex year is funded several times over without equity. The obligations outside the debt line matter more: $7,955M of minimum lease payments at 2025-12-31, of which $1,320M falls due within twelve months; an accrued warranty reserve of $7,414M that grew 20.9% in nine months against 10% delivery growth; and $7,055M of deferred revenue. Goodwill and intangibles of $381M are 0.2% of assets, so there is no acquisition accounting to discount, and interest coverage of 9.96x is ample but has fallen from 56.99x in FY2023 as operating income shrank [S8, S1].

### The capital is not earning its keep

Returns have fallen faster than margins. Return on invested capital went from 28.3% in FY2023 to 13.7%, 7.0% and 5.5% trailing, and return on equity from 27.9% to 3.8%; the 5.5% compares with a 4.93% ten-year Treasury yield on 2026-10-30, leaving 57 basis points for equity risk in a business whose operating margin has halved twice in three years. The capex record explains it: $41,778M spent in FY2023, FY2024, FY2025 and the first nine months of 2026 against a $5,425M fall in operating income over the same span — from FY2022's peak of $13,656M the fall is $10,190M — an incremental return that is negative at group level. Nothing has been returned to shareholders: no dividend and no repurchase from FY2021 to Q3 2026, while $2,000M of cash went into the xAI investment agreed in January 2026, converted into SpaceX Class A stock on 2026-03-12, and media reported the investment went ahead against a shareholder vote. GM authorised a $20B repurchase in the same quarter [S1, S8, S10, S115, S104].

### What flatters the number, and what would change it

Four items soften the reported result. Interest income of $1,301M was 42.9% of nine-month pre-tax income, and $445M was 46.5% of the Q3 2026 figure, against 17.5% in FY2024. Stock-based compensation of $3,346M in nine months is 4.3% of revenue and the main reason non-GAAP profit more than doubles GAAP profit; EPS is struck on 3,240M basic and 3,541M diluted weighted-average shares against 3,952,648,559 shares outstanding at 2026-09-30, and the 713M difference is the 423.7M unvested shares of the 2025 CEO award plus 286.4M restricted shares from the 2018 award, both excluded until earned — so dividing earnings by the diluted count understates the share base by 12%, and the award, if earned, lifts the count by a further 12%. An effective tax rate of 20% against 27% was helped by a smaller valuation-allowance release in Q2 2026, and cost of automotive sales benefited from what management calls warranty adjustments while the warranty reserve rose 20.9%. Sensitivity: a percentage point of ex-credit automotive margin is worth $800M a year on $80,000M of automotive revenue, 6.4 times a point of energy margin at $12,500M, and each $1B of capex is $1B of free cash flow. Base case FY2027 free cash flow of $2,000M assumes operating cash flow of $22,000M less capex of $20,000M with energy at 30% and automotive at 18%; energy back at Q2 2026's 20.4% and automotive at 15.4% removes $3,360M and turns it into -$1,360M; energy held at 33.1% adds $390M. The variable that moves the outcome most is capex, a management decision worth $5B in a single restatement between July and October 2026 — more than six points of automotive margin. The diligence question is what the 2027 capex number is and whether the payables build reflects renegotiated terms or deferred payments [S8, S83, S1, S117, S102].

::: info danger
The most serious red flag is the composition of free cash flow rather than its level: nine-month free cash flow is smaller than the rise in payables that produced it, capital expenditure was re-scoped in the same quarter that new credit lines were arranged, and the cash balance generating almost half of pre-tax profit is the only reason reported earnings look positive at the operating level. Reported free cash flow is a ceiling, not a run-rate.
:::

arguments.markdown:
Tesla sells for $399.81 on NasdaqGS at the 2026-10-30 close, a $1,580.4bn market capitalisation and $1,544.2bn of enterprise value, and on the businesses its filings describe — cars, storage, services — it is worth roughly $139-160bn, or $35-40 a share. That leaves $1.42-1.44tn, about 90% of the equity, resting on robotaxi, FSD and Optimus revenue the quarterly report does not yet book, and the buyer at this price pays 103x trailing adjusted EBITDA for the privilege. The judgement is that the reported businesses cannot carry the price, that the residual is a probability-weighted option whose required scale is 17-34 years of installed Cybercab capacity, and that the shares are therefore a claim on a multiple rather than on Tesla's earnings [S8, S9].

| Metric | Value | Signal |
|---|---|---|
| Last price | $399.81, 2026-10-30 20:00 UTC, NasdaqGS, USD | — |
| Market capitalisation | $1,580.4bn on 3,952.6m shares | 5.4% more shares than at 2025-12-31 |
| Enterprise value | $1,544.2bn after $36.2bn net cash | Cash is 2.3% of the equity |
| 52-week range | $297.38-$498.83 | 51% of the way up the range |
| Returns | 1M +12.7%, 3M +28.5%, 12M -12.4% | 12M trails the S&P 500 by 23.2 points |
| Moving averages | 50-day $369.60 (+8.2%), 200-day $385.30 (+3.8%) | Extended after a 28.5% quarter |
| Liquidity | $13.8bn traded a day (20-day average) | No exit constraint on size |
| Trailing P/E | 439.4x against a peer median of 19.1x | Earnings, not price, did the falling |
| EV/adjusted EBITDA | 103.0x on $14,995m trailing | 144x before the $4,300m stock-compensation add-back |
| Insider activity, 6 months | No purchases; 19 sales of $13.3m, 17 under 10b5-1 plans | No management buying at these levels |
| Source | | S8, S11, S2 |

### The price pays for a multiple, not for earnings

Trailing revenue is $103.6bn, adjusted EBITDA $15.0bn, operating income $3.47bn and free cash flow $3.3bn, the last after $15.4bn of capital expenditure in twelve months [S9]. On those numbers Tesla trades at 445x EV/operating income, a 0.2% free-cash-flow yield and 14.9x sales, against 17.3x EV/EBITDA for BYD and 19.1x earnings for General Motors [S131, S15]. The EBITDA figure the company prefers is itself generous: it adds back $4.3bn of stock compensation, up from $2.8bn in FY2025, so the 103x becomes 144x on EBITDA before that add-back. At this multiple one turn of EV/adjusted EBITDA is worth about $15bn, which is three years of Tesla's current net income — the price is a rating, and any delay in the autonomy story compresses the rating rather than the earnings.

### What the reported businesses are worth

| Method | Inputs | Value | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| Automotive and regulatory credits | $75.0bn trailing revenue at 0.6-0.8x EV/sales (GM about 0.4x, Ford about 0.25x, BYD about 1.0x) | $45-60bn | S9, S15, S17, S132 |
| Energy generation and storage | $12.3bn trailing revenue, 30.2% nine-month gross margin, at 2.5-3.0x sales; cross-check CATL at 19.8x earnings | $31-37bn | S9, S133 |
| Services and other | $16.3bn trailing revenue, +32% year on year, at 1.5x sales | $24bn | S9 |
| Net cash at 2026-09-30 | $45.4bn cash and short-term investments less $9.3bn debt | $36.2bn | S8 |
| SpaceX equity stake | $2.0bn bought in Q1 2026 plus $863m unrealised gain | about $2.9bn | S9 |
| Total, reported businesses | | $139-160bn, $35-40 a share | |
| Residual in the share price | $1,580.4bn less the total | $1,420-1,441bn, 90-91% | |

The split matters more than the point estimate. Energy, the segment with the best margin at 33.1% gross in Q3 2026, is 12% of trailing revenue and shrank 16% year on year as Megapack average selling prices fell; services grew 32% and reached a record $734m of gross profit in the quarter. Neither can be stretched to a trillion dollars without abandoning the multiples their peers earn. Even a generous automotive recovery — a 10% operating margin on $75bn at 25x earnings — lifts the whole total only to about $285bn, $72 a share, and still leaves 82% of the price unexplained.

### What the price requires by 2030

| Multiple applied to enterprise value | Enterprise value | Required adjusted EBITDA | Versus $15.0bn trailing | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 17.3x (BYD's multiple) | $1,544.2bn | $89.3bn | 6.0x | S131 |
| 25x | $1,544.2bn | $61.8bn | 4.1x | |
| 40x | $1,544.2bn | $38.6bn | 2.6x | |
| 80x (the multiple management's own $4.0tn tranche implies on $50bn) | $1,544.2bn | $19.3bn | 1.3x | S127 |

Inverting the price gives the same answer from the other side. If the residual $1,441bn is discounted at 10% and valued at 20x 2030 operating income, it requires $105bn of 2030 operating income; at 40x, $53bn. At a 25% robotaxi margin and $100,000 of revenue per vehicle-year, that is 2.1-4.2m vehicles in commercial service by 2030. The Texas registry showed 1,051 authorised robotaxis on 2026-10-27, and installed Cybercab capacity in Texas is 125,000 units a year [S125, S9]. The market is therefore discounting 17-34 years of current factory output, six to twelve times management's own one-million-robotaxi milestone, which the board paired with a $3.5tn market capitalisation [S127]. Note also the multiple: at the $4.0tn tranche management's plan implies 80x adjusted EBITDA, below the 103x the shares carry today, so the price is already ahead of the pay design built to reward the outcome it assumes.

| Company | P/E (TTM) | EV/sales | EV/EBITDA (XBRL basis) | FCF yield | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Tesla | 439.4x | 14.9x | 169.0x | 0.2% | S8, S11 |
| General Motors | 19.1x | n/m | n/m | 19.5% | S15, S16 |
| Ford | n/m | n/m | n/m | 11.3% | S17, S18 |
| Rivian | n/m | 2.6x | n/m | -23.8% | S19 |
| BYD | 21.2x | n/d | 17.3x | n/d | S132, S131 |
| CATL | 19.8x | n/d | n/d | n/d | S133 |
| Fluence Energy | n/m | n/m | n/m | -14.6% | S61, S62 |

Tesla's own history says the same thing as the peer table. The P/E was 34.0x at the end of 2022, 57.8x in 2023, 204.6x in 2024 and 420.8x in 2025 as diluted EPS fell from $4.90 to $1.08, and stands at 439.4x now [S11, S12, S1]. EV/sales is the more stable measure and is at 14.9x, mid-way in its 14.7-16.5x band of the past three years, because revenue doubled while the shares went nowhere: the five-year return to 2026-10-30 is -0.8%. The regime this multiple is priced in makes that harder to hold: the 10-year Treasury yields 4.93%, up 0.84 points in twelve months, the VIX is 19.42, in its 77th percentile, and high-yield spreads have widened from 276 to 326 basis points [S22, S21, S46].

### Consensus, guidance and the dates that reset the multiple

Sell-side consensus is Hold — 24 buy, 1 strong buy, 20 hold and 3 sell across 48 firms — with an average target of $408.61, 2.2% above the close; a wider 83-analyst sample puts it at $442.13, 10.6% above [S128]. Individual targets range from Jefferies at $400 to RBC at $480, and Q3 2026 was a beat on adjusted earnings, $0.48 against $0.45. Tesla publishes no numeric revenue or EPS guidance; its outlook commits only to maximum capacity utilisation, a strong balance sheet and "hardware-related profits accompanied by an acceleration of SI, software and fleet-based profits", and the capital-expenditure outlook was cut from more than $25bn to about $20bn after the quarter. The dates that can move the multiple inside twelve months are the fourth-quarter 2026 results, expected in the last week of January 2027 on the pattern of the FY2025 10-K filed 2026-01-29, the first Cybercab deployment outside Austin as Dallas is prepared, further FSD approvals in the nine European markets already live, and progress in the SpaceX combination study. The first 2025 award tranche crystallises at a $2,000bn market capitalisation, $506.05 a share and 26.6% above spot [S127].

The strongest counter-argument is that the premium is a fair price for an option that is visibly maturing: active FSD subscriptions reached 1.74m, up 67% year on year, the paid take rate in North America is above 75% of deliveries, unsupervised Robotaxi miles reached nearly 2m and the authorised fleet grew from 739 to 1,051 vehicles in eighteen days. If robotaxi unit economics are proven in 2027, 103x EBITDA on today's numbers is a discount to what the business would then earn. The arithmetic does not support the weaker version of that argument — energy alone caps out at $37bn — and no company in the comparison set earns Tesla's combination of a 30% energy gross margin and 32% services growth while trading above 30x earnings. Confidence in the valuation arithmetic is high; confidence in the durability of the multiple is low, because it rests on evidence the company has not disclosed. Three questions would settle it: revenue per robotaxi per week in Austin, the operating margin the energy segment earns at 130 GWh of installed capacity, and whether a buyback or dividend ever enters a capital-allocation policy that has never returned cash. Options-implied volatility and short interest were not retrieved and are not used here.
