arguments.markdown:
Tesla's ESG and policy position has already removed a material profit stream and leaves its highest-value product gated by permits and a live safety investigation, so ESG lowers, rather than raises, the multiple a twelve-month buyer should pay. Automotive regulatory credits earned $1,993 million in 2025 against $2,763 million in 2024, then $639 million in the first nine months of 2026 against $1,451 million a year earlier; the contracted credit backlog fell to $384 million at 2026-09-30 from $841 million at 2025-12-31, and $475 million of previously delivered credits were reversed [S1, S8]. Credits are earned against compliance shortfalls the rules create, so when the 2025 budget law narrowed the programmes both the shortfalls and the deliverable credits shrank — hence the reversal. On the 2026 run rate the line is worth roughly $850 million a year of near-pure gross margin; models that restore it toward the 2024 peak overstate revenue and automotive margin.

### Permits, not software, cap the paid robotaxi market

The California DMV's list, updated 2026-10-23, places TESLA ROBOTAXI LLC among holders of an autonomous-vehicle testing permit **with a safety driver**; Tesla appears on neither the driverless-testing list (2026-10-22) nor the deployment list, which names only Mercedes-Benz, Nuro and Waymo. The California Public Utilities Commission said in March 2026 that the state's Tesla "Robotaxi" runs on a limousine permit, outside autonomous-vehicle passenger-service rules. In Texas, Senate Bill 2807 — not 2809 — has required Texas DMV authorisation for commercial automated vehicles since 2026-05-28, and 1,051 vehicles held that authorisation on 2026-10-27; it is a registration regime, not a volume cap. Tesla's roughly 2.0 million unsupervised miles are 0.9% of Waymo's 220.6 million rider-only miles through March 2026. A testing permit with a driver cannot generate driverless revenue, so the twelve-month paid market is permissive states only, and California needs two more approvals against Waymo's multi-year precedent [S9, S89, S90, S91, S125, S151].

### Safety enforcement is the sharper exposure

NHTSA's Office of Defects Investigation opened Engineering Analysis EA26002 on 2026-03-18 into Tesla's FSD degradation-detection system in reduced-visibility conditions, escalating Preliminary Evaluation PE24031 and covering model years 2016 to 2026. An Engineering Analysis is the last administrative step before the agency can seek a mandatory recall. A software recall's direct cost is small because the remedy ships over the air, but agency findings become exhibits in the product-liability cases Tesla already defends, and a recall can interrupt the autonomy narrative carrying most of the equity value. Tesla discloses no NHTSA consent order, which would be the materially worse outcome. Separately, NHTSA records eight recall campaigns on the 2026 Model Y between 2025-05-30 and 2026-09-01, including front-suspension fasteners (26V558000) — high for one nameplate in sixteen months [S47, S87, S88].

### Governance: the tail shrank, the concentration did not

On 2025-12-19 the Delaware Supreme Court reversed the Chancery rescission of Mr Musk's 2018 pay award, reinstating it with $1 in nominal damages and a reduced fee award, after 72% of disinterested shares voted to ratify in 2024. That removes an overhang priced since January 2024. Concentration remains: Mr Musk holds 699,580,882 shares, 19.8% of 3,952,648,559 outstanding, of which 207,498,721 are pledged as loan collateral — a forced-selling channel in a drawdown. The 2025 CEO Performance Award covers 423,743,904 restricted shares, 10.7% of the total; unearned shares vote proportionally, so the control effect is smaller than the dilution. The 2026 escalation is capital allocation: Tesla agreed in January 2026 to invest approximately $2.00 billion in xAI Holdings, the right converted into SpaceX Class A stock when SpaceX acquired xAI Holdings on 2026-02-02, and Tesla completed the purchase on 2026-03-12. That is the governance item most likely to move institutional demand [S1, S10].

### Social: enforcement is mixed, workplace safety is unmeasured

The California Civil Rights Department's race-discrimination action ran its first, equitable-relief trial phase from 2026-09-21 to a scheduled close on 2026-10-30 in Alameda County Superior Court, while the EEOC's parallel race-harassment and retaliation suit, filed 2023-09-28, sits in discovery with no trial date. Against that, the National Labor Relations Board dismissed a complaint over Buffalo plant IT rules on 2026-10-29. The exposure is injunctive, not monetary: a finding would impose monitoring on plant management and raise the cost of state incentives, while cash damages are undisclosed and unlikely to be material. Workplace safety stays unmeasured: Tesla's total recordable case rate and days-away rate, and any comparison with GM, Ford or BYD, are not readable from the 2025 Impact Report, and establishment-level OSHA 300A data is outstanding. That gap is material because injury rates set state incentive conditions and insurer pricing at the plants Tesla is expanding, so the social judgement rests on litigation and labour relations alone [S8, S96, S97, S175].

### The environmental case does not price in twelve months

Tesla's 2025 Impact Report claims nearly 37 million tonnes of CO2e avoided by customers in 2025 and a 2040 net-zero commitment; both are company material and unverified, and its Scope 1-3 totals could not be read because the file would not load. The one environmental rule with a hard compliance cost for a battery maker has been deferred: Regulation (EU) 2025/1561 pushed supply-chain due diligence from 18 August 2025 to 18 August 2027, and the battery passport starts on 18 February 2027 — both outside the horizon [S95, S97].

rows.finding: Q3 2026 energy gross profit of $954M on $2,881M revenue (33.1%) falls to $428M, 14.8%, once the $526M IEEPA tariff refund credited to energy cost of revenue is removed; the separate $339M customer pass-through remains in revenue.
rows.mechanism: A one-off refund reduces cost without any operating improvement, while the contractual pass-through reduces revenue, so the reported margin overstates the segment's earning power.
rows.benchmark: Q2 2026 20.4% with no refund; nine-month 2026 24.0% ex-refund; Fluence FY2025 13.1% and June 2026 quarter 5.1%.
rows.implication: Do not underwrite a 30% storage margin: the base case normalises energy to 14-18%, worth $1.5bn of EBITDA less than the prior 25-30% assumption.
rows.weakens: The warranty true-up component is not quantified in any filing; Q2 2026's 20.4% shows the underlying margin can exceed 14.8%.

rows.confidence: High on the arithmetic; medium on the normalised level.

rows.mechanism: First-half IEEPA amounts were immaterial, so only Q3 carries the refund; the apparent Q3 improvement over Q2 is entirely the one-off.

rows.mechanism: Project integrators absorb liquidated damages and cost overruns; the June 2026 quarter carried both, so it is a trough not a benchmark.
rows.benchmark: Tesla Q3 2026 ex-refund 14.8%.

rows.finding: Sungrow's storage business earned 36.49% gross margin in FY2025 on RMB 37.29bn of revenue; CATL's storage battery gross margin was 23.96% in H1 2026.

rows.benchmark: Tesla energy 14.8% ex-refund; 24.0% nine-month ex-refund.

arguments.markdown:
Tesla's ESG and policy position has already removed a material profit stream and leaves its highest-value product gated by permits and a live safety investigation: ESG lowers, not raises, the multiple a twelve-month buyer should pay. Automotive regulatory credits earned $1,993 million in 2025 against $2,763 million in 2024, then $639 million in the first nine months of 2026 against $1,451 million a year earlier; the contracted credit backlog fell to $384 million at 2026-09-30 from $841 million at 2025-12-31, and $475 million of previously delivered credits were reversed [S1, S8]. Credits are earned against compliance shortfalls the rules create, so when the 2025 budget law narrowed the programmes, both shrank — hence the reversal. On the 2026 run rate the line is worth roughly $850 million a year of near-pure gross margin; models that restore it toward the 2024 peak overstate revenue and automotive margin.

### Permits, not software, cap the paid robotaxi market

The California DMV's list, updated 2026-10-23, places TESLA ROBOTAXI LLC among holders of an autonomous-vehicle testing permit **with a safety driver**; Tesla appears on neither the driverless-testing list (2026-10-22) nor the deployment list, which names only Mercedes-Benz, Nuro and Waymo. The California Public Utilities Commission said in March 2026 that the state's Tesla "Robotaxi" runs on a limousine permit, outside autonomous-vehicle passenger-service rules. In Texas, Senate Bill 2807 — not 2809 — has required Texas DMV authorisation for commercial automated vehicles since 2026-05-28, and 1,051 vehicles held that authorisation on 2026-10-27; it is a registration regime, not a volume cap. Tesla's roughly 2.0 million unsupervised miles are 0.9% of Waymo's 220.6 million rider-only miles through March 2026. A testing permit with a driver cannot generate driverless revenue, so the twelve-month paid market is permissive states only; California needs two more approvals against Waymo's multi-year precedent [S9, S89, S90, S91, S125, S151].

### Safety enforcement is the sharper exposure

NHTSA's Office of Defects Investigation opened Engineering Analysis EA26002 on 2026-03-18 into Tesla's FSD degradation-detection system in reduced-visibility conditions, escalating Preliminary Evaluation PE24031 and covering model years 2016 to 2026. An Engineering Analysis is the last administrative step before the agency can seek a mandatory recall. A software recall's direct cost is small — the remedy ships over the air — but agency findings become exhibits in product-liability cases and a recall can interrupt the autonomy narrative carrying most of the equity value. Tesla discloses no NHTSA consent order, which would be the materially worse outcome. Separately, NHTSA records eight recall campaigns on the 2026 Model Y between 2025-05-30 and 2026-09-01, including front-suspension fasteners (26V558000) — high for one nameplate in sixteen months [S47, S87, S88].

### Governance: the tail shrank, the concentration did not

On 2025-12-19 the Delaware Supreme Court reversed the Chancery rescission of Mr Musk's 2018 pay award, reinstating it with $1 nominal damages and reduced fees, after 72% of disinterested shares ratified it in 2024. That removes an overhang priced since January 2024. Concentration remains: Mr Musk holds 699,580,882 shares, 19.8% of 3,952,648,559 outstanding, of which 207,498,721 are pledged as loan collateral — a forced-selling channel in a drawdown. The 2025 CEO Performance Award covers 423,743,904 restricted shares, 10.7% of the total; unearned shares vote proportionally, so the control effect is smaller than the dilution. The 2026 escalation is capital allocation: Tesla agreed in January 2026 to invest approximately $2.00 billion in xAI Holdings, the right converted into SpaceX Class A stock when SpaceX acquired xAI Holdings on 2026-02-02, and Tesla completed the purchase on 2026-03-12. That is the item most likely to move institutional demand [S1, S10].

### Social: enforcement is mixed, workplace safety is unmeasured

The California Civil Rights Department's race-discrimination action ran its equitable-relief trial phase from 2026-09-21 to a close on 2026-10-30 in Alameda County Superior Court, while the EEOC's parallel race-harassment suit, filed 2023-09-28, sits in discovery with no trial date. Against that, the National Labor Relations Board dismissed a complaint over Buffalo plant IT rules on 2026-10-29. The exposure is injunctive, not monetary: a finding would impose monitoring on plant management and raise the cost of state incentives; cash damages are undisclosed and unlikely to be material. Workplace safety stays unmeasured: Tesla's total recordable case rate and days-away rate, and any comparison with GM, Ford or BYD, are not readable from the 2025 Impact Report, and establishment-level OSHA 300A data is outstanding. That gap is material because injury rates set state incentive conditions and insurer pricing at the plants Tesla is expanding; the social judgement rests on litigation and labour relations alone [S8, S96, S97, S175].

### The environmental case does not price in twelve months

Tesla's 2025 Impact Report claims nearly 37 million tonnes of CO2e avoided by customers in 2025 and a 2040 net-zero commitment; both are company material and unverified, and Scope 1-3 totals could not be read because the file would not load. The one environmental rule with a hard compliance cost for a battery maker has been deferred: Regulation (EU) 2025/1561 pushed supply-chain due diligence from 18 August 2025 to 18 August 2027, and the battery passport starts on 18 February 2027 — both outside the horizon [S95, S97].

| ESG issue | Why it is financially material | Evidence | Effect on the case | Source |

arguments.markdown:
Tesla's ESG and policy position has already removed a material profit stream and leaves its highest-value product gated by permits and a live safety investigation: ESG lowers, not raises, the multiple a twelve-month buyer should pay. Automotive regulatory credits earned $1,993 million in 2025 against $2,763 million in 2024, then $639 million in the first nine months of 2026 against $1,451 million a year earlier; the contracted credit backlog fell to $384 million at 2026-09-30 from $841 million at 2025-12-31, and $475 million of previously delivered credits were reversed [S1, S8]. Credits are earned against compliance shortfalls the rules create, so when the 2025 budget law narrowed the programmes, both shrank — hence the reversal. On the 2026 run rate the line is worth roughly $850 million a year of near-pure gross margin; models that restore it toward the 2024 peak overstate revenue and automotive margin.

### Permits, not software, cap the paid robotaxi market

The California DMV's list, updated 2026-10-23, places TESLA ROBOTAXI LLC among holders of an autonomous-vehicle testing permit **with a safety driver**; Tesla appears on neither the driverless-testing list (2026-10-22) nor the deployment list, which names only Mercedes-Benz, Nuro and Waymo. The California Public Utilities Commission said in March 2026 that the state's Tesla "Robotaxi" runs on a limousine permit, outside autonomous-vehicle passenger-service rules. In Texas, Senate Bill 2807 — not 2809 — has required Texas DMV authorisation for commercial automated vehicles since 2026-05-28, and 1,051 vehicles held that authorisation on 2026-10-27; it is a registration regime, not a volume cap. Tesla's roughly 2.0 million unsupervised miles are 0.9% of Waymo's 220.6 million rider-only miles through March 2026. A testing permit with a driver cannot generate driverless revenue, so the twelve-month paid market is permissive states only; California needs two more approvals against Waymo's multi-year precedent [S9, S89, S90, S91, S125, S151].

### Safety enforcement is the sharper exposure

NHTSA's Office of Defects Investigation opened Engineering Analysis EA26002 on 2026-03-18 into Tesla's FSD degradation-detection system in reduced-visibility conditions, escalating Preliminary Evaluation PE24031 and covering model years 2016 to 2026. An Engineering Analysis is the last administrative step before the agency can seek a mandatory recall. A software recall's direct cost is small — the remedy ships over the air — but agency findings become exhibits in product-liability cases and a recall can interrupt the autonomy narrative carrying most of the equity value. Tesla discloses no NHTSA consent order, which would be the materially worse outcome. Separately, NHTSA records eight recall campaigns on the 2026 Model Y between 2025-05-30 and 2026-09-01, including front-suspension fasteners (26V558000) — high for one nameplate in sixteen months [S47, S87, S88].

### Governance: the tail shrank, the concentration did not

On 2025-12-19 the Delaware Supreme Court reversed the Chancery rescission of Mr Musk's 2018 pay award, reinstating it with $1 nominal damages and reduced fees, after 72% of disinterested shares ratified it in 2024. That removes an overhang priced since January 2024. Concentration remains: Mr Musk holds 699,580,882 shares, 19.8% of 3,952,648,559 outstanding, of which 207,498,721 are pledged as loan collateral — a forced-selling channel in a drawdown. The 2025 CEO Performance Award covers 423,743,904 restricted shares, 10.7% of the total; unearned shares vote proportionally, so the control effect is smaller than the dilution. The 2026 escalation is capital allocation: Tesla agreed in January 2026 to invest approximately $2.00 billion in xAI Holdings, the right converted into SpaceX Class A stock when SpaceX acquired xAI Holdings on 2026-02-02, and Tesla completed the purchase on 2026-03-12. That is the item most likely to move institutional demand [S1, S10].

### Social: enforcement is mixed, workplace safety is unmeasured

The California Civil Rights Department's race-discrimination action ran its equitable-relief trial phase from 2026-09-21 to a close on 2026-10-30 in Alameda County Superior Court, while the EEOC's parallel race-harassment suit, filed 2023-09-28, sits in discovery with no trial date. Against that, the National Labor Relations Board dismissed a complaint over Buffalo plant IT rules on 2026-10-29. The exposure is injunctive, not monetary: a finding would impose monitoring on plant management and raise the cost of state incentives; cash damages are undisclosed and unlikely to be material. Workplace safety stays unmeasured: Tesla's total recordable case rate and days-away rate, and any comparison with GM, Ford or BYD, are not readable from the 2025 Impact Report, and establishment-level OSHA 300A data is outstanding. That gap is material because injury rates set state incentive conditions and insurer pricing at the plants Tesla is expanding; the social judgement rests on litigation and labour relations alone [S8, S96, S97, S175].

### The environmental case does not price in twelve months

Tesla's 2025 Impact Report claims nearly 37 million tonnes of CO2e avoided by customers in 2025 and a 2040 net-zero commitment; both are company material and unverified, and Scope 1-3 totals could not be read because the file would not load. The one environmental rule with a hard compliance cost for a battery maker has been deferred: Regulation (EU) 2025/1561 pushed supply-chain due diligence from 18 August 2025 to 18 August 2027, and the battery passport starts on 18 February 2027 — both outside the horizon [S95, S97].

plan.thesis_sentence: Tesla converted $1,531M of free cash flow in Q3 2026, but the statements no longer show it earning its cost of capital: a 5.5% trailing return on invested capital sits 57 basis points above the ten-year Treasury, $41,778M of capex since 2023 has coincided with a 61% fall in operating income, and the profit that remains leans on interest income, a payables build and $526M of one-off energy tariff refunds, so trailing adjusted EBITDA normalises to $14,469M and the 40% base case at 70x plus net cash is $266 a share.

plan.mechanism: Normalise adjusted EBITDA for one-offs, bridge EBITDA to free cash flow through working capital and capex, and compare ROIC with the risk-free rate and the cost of the capex programme.

Tesla's ESG and policy position has already removed a material profit stream and leaves its highest-value product gated by permits and a live safety investigation: ESG lowers, not raises, the multiple a twelve-month buyer should pay. On the 2026 run rate the line is worth roughly $850 million a year of near-pure gross margin; models that restore it toward the 2024 peak overstate revenue and automotive margin.

### Permits, not software, cap the paid robotaxi market

The California DMV's list, updated 2026-10-23, places TESLA ROBOTAXI LLC among holders of an autonomous-vehicle testing permit **with a safety driver**; Tesla appears on neither the driverless-testing list (2026-10-22) nor the deployment list, which names only Mercedes-Benz, Nuro and Waymo. The California Public Utilities Commission said in March 2026 that the state's Tesla "Robotaxi" runs on a limousine permit, outside autonomous-vehicle passenger-service rules. A testing permit with a driver cannot generate driverless revenue, so the twelve-month paid market is permissive states only; California needs two more approvals against Waymo's multi-year precedent [S9, S89, S90, S91, S125, S151].

NHTSA's Office of Defects Investigation opened Engineering Analysis EA26002 on 2026-03-18 into Tesla's FSD degradation-detection system in reduced-visibility conditions, escalating Preliminary Evaluation PE24031 and covering model years 2016 to 2026. An Engineering Analysis is the last administrative step before the agency can seek a mandatory recall. A software recall's direct cost is small — the remedy ships over the air — but agency findings become exhibits in product-liability cases and a recall can interrupt the autonomy narrative carrying most of the equity value. Tesla discloses no NHTSA consent order, which would be the materially worse outcome. Separately, NHTSA records eight recall campaigns on the 2026 Model Y between 2025-05-30 and 2026-09-01, including front-suspension fasteners (26V558000) — high for one nameplate in sixteen months [S47, S87, S88].

On 2025-12-19 the Delaware Supreme Court reversed the Chancery rescission of Mr Musk's 2018 pay award, reinstating it with $1 nominal damages and reduced fees, after 72% of disinterested shares ratified it in 2024. ### Social: enforcement is mixed, workplace safety is unmeasured

The California Civil Rights Department's race-discrimination action ran its equitable-relief trial phase from 2026-09-21 to a close on 2026-10-30 in Alameda County Superior Court, while the EEOC's parallel race-harassment suit, filed 2023-09-28, sits in discovery with no trial date. The exposure is injunctive, not monetary: a finding would impose monitoring on plant management and raise the cost of state incentives; cash damages are undisclosed and unlikely to be material. Workplace safety stays unmeasured: Tesla's total recordable case rate and days-away rate, and any comparison with GM, Ford or BYD, are not readable from the 2025 Impact Report, and establishment-level OSHA 300A data is outstanding. {"content":[{"type":"text","text":"## Competitive Landscape (competition, revision 5 by Market Analyst, 8,931 characters)
Tesla is winning the market that is shrinking and losing the one that is growing. It holds the US electric-vehicle market at a share no rival approaches while that market contracts, ranks fourth among China's new-energy brands in a pool that is itself shrinking, and its European recovery has come inside a pool growing faster than it. What Tesla owns is narrower than the narrative: the charging standard every major automaker has licensed, 1.74 million paid FSD subscriptions, and a storage business whose 33.1% reported gross margin falls to 14.8% once $526 million of tariff refunds and warranty true-ups are removed — mid-pack against CATL and Sungrow, not ahead of them [S8, S9, S167].

### In the United States, Tesla sets the price because it holds the pool

Tesla sold 144,094 US electric vehicles in Q3 2026 for 54% of the market, and 386,194 in nine months for 52.9%, with US volume down 14.4% against a market down 30.3%. Share gains in a contracting pool flatter the position. When a $7,500 credit disappears, the brand with the densest charging footprint keeps the remaining buyers. The question is whether Tesla can hold price, and it has — automotive gross margin rose to 18.5% in Q3 2026 from 17.0% [S145, S8].

### China is where Tesla is the price taker

BYD sold 456,713 passenger cars in September 2026, 273,143 of them battery-electric, and 3,078,490 in nine months — 2.3 times Tesla's 1,324,681. Geely sold 119,682 and Xiaomi 40,015 retail units in September. BYD earned 19.46% gross margin overseas against 16.66% at home in 2025, a domestic ceiling Tesla cannot price above; Tesla's China retail of 64,837 was 3.8 times smaller than BYD's in September while Chinese battery-electric wholesale grew 18.3%. In driver assistance, Huawei and Momenta together supply more than 80% of China's urban NOA systems, Momenta alone 65% [S138, S146, S149, S168].

### Europe: growth in units, no evidence of share

EU battery-electric registrations reached 1,931,465 in January-September 2026 at a 22.7% share, with September at 29.9%, so the pool expanded 49% while Tesla's European deliveries recovered from a 2025 slump. Tesla sells cars, storage projects and services, and the returns are lower and more borrowed than the segment headlines suggest: the car earned an 18.1% gross margin excluding regulatory credits in Q3 2026, not enough to cover group research and selling cost, storage's 33.1% quarter falls to 14.8% once the $526M IEEPA tariff refund is removed, and the group's pre-tax profit was small enough that interest income supplied 46.5% of it. The return is earned on a mixed gross-profit pool and on the cash pile, not on a structurally superior unit economic model.

### Three segments, three ways of getting paid

The automotive segment took 73.3% of third-quarter 2026 revenue ($20,560M of $28,046M), services and other 16.4% ($4,605M) and energy generation and storage 10.3% ($2,881M). The buyer differs in each: a retail or fleet customer pays cash or finances a car at transfer of control; an energy customer — a utility, developer or data-centre operator — pays on project milestones across quarters; a service customer pays per transaction for collision repair, maintenance or a Supercharging session; another automaker pays for regulatory credits at transfer of title. The mix has moved: energy was 6.2% of FY2023 revenue ($6,035M) and 13.5% in FY2025 ($12,771M), while automotive revenue fell from $82,419M to $69,526M. The only recurring software charge is FSD (Supervised) at $99 a month, with 1.74 million active subscriptions on 2026-09-30 against 1.04 million a year earlier [S8, S1, S121].

### The vehicle does not pay for the research budget

[table]

A delivered car carried $42,259 of automotive revenue and $34,436 of cost, leaving $7,823 of gross profit, $7,590 excluding credits; spreading $4,776M of group research and development and selling cost over 486,532 deliveries costs $9,817 a vehicle, so the automotive line alone runs at about -$1,994 a vehicle. Energy and services add $3,470 a vehicle and turn that into $1,476 of operating profit and, with $445M of interest income, $1,965 of pre-tax profit. Cost per vehicle was $33,666 in Q4 2025, $35,786 in Q1 2026 and $34,436 in Q3 2026, so unit cost is not falling; the rise in ex-credit automotive margin from 15.4% to 18.1% year on year arrived with a richer Asia-Pacific delivery mix in Q3 2026, not from the factory [S9, S8].

### Storage's 33% is a tariff refund, not a run-rate

Energy reported $954M of gross profit on $2,881M of revenue in Q3 2026, 33.1%, after 20.4% in Q2 2026. The 10-Q note says Tesla recognised $526M of IEEPA tariff refunds as a reduction to energy cost of revenue and $339M as a reduction to energy revenue for refunds owed to customers; first-half amounts were immaterial. Removing the $526M cost credit leaves $428M, or 14.8%, with the $339M customer pass-through still depressing revenue. The earnings call also attributed the margin to warranty true-ups, but no filing quantifies that piece, so the $526M cannot be split and 14.8% is the conservative ex-refund figure; adding the $339M back as well would give 23.8%, which assumes the customer price cuts reverse. Q1 2026's 39.5% and Q2's 20.4% carry no refund, so the apparent Q3 improvement is entirely the refund: ex-refund, Q3 is below Q2 [S8, S9, S117].

[table 1]

[table 2]

At 14.8%, Tesla is near Fluence's 13.1% fiscal-year margin, not six times Fluence's worst quarter — the 5.1% June 2026 print carried project liquidated damages and cost overruns, and is the wrong comparison. Sungrow's storage business earned 36.49% in FY2025 and CATL's storage batteries 23.96% in H1 2026, both as reported and both above Tesla; a vertically integrated Megapack should sit between the integrator and the cell maker, which is where 14.8-24.0% puts it, not at a structural premium. Revenue per kWh fell to $210 in Q3 2026 from $274 in Q1 2026, and ex-refund gross profit per kWh was $31 against $70 reported, so the segment is price- and volume-sensitive, not a fixed 30% annuity.

### Services is the quiet second engine, and robotaxi is the unpriced one

Services and other grew revenue 33% to $4,605M and gross profit to a record $734M, 15.9%, from 14.1% in Q2 2026 and 10.5% a year earlier; used vehicles, collision, maintenance and paid Supercharging are the lines, and Rivian's software and services segment earned 42% on $605M, so Tesla's margin is below the best comparable on 7.6 times the revenue. Robotaxi is the largest unpriced unit economic in the case and the least disclosed: Tesla reports nearly two million cumulative unsupervised miles, a 1,051-vehicle authorised Texas fleet and a Cybercab launch, but no revenue, no paid trips and no cost per paid mile. Insurance, remote supervision, vehicle depreciation, charging and maintenance are the cost lines; each is undisclosed. If total cost is 60% of the fare, a 2x cost per mile turns a 40% contribution margin into -20%; if cost is 50%, 2x leaves zero. A revenue line with positive contribution is the single fact that would move the valuation; without it the 15% autonomy branch of the bull case rests on miles, not money [S9, S120, S153].

### What breaks even, and what cannot be measured

[Pricing table]

At Q3 2026 unit economics, the automotive line covers its share of group cost only at about 629,000 deliveries a quarter excluding credits (611,000 including them), 29% above the 486,532 delivered. Tesla discloses no customer-acquisition cost — there is no marketing line in the statements — so SG&A at 7.2% of revenue is the nearest proxy and a CAC payback or LTV:CAC ratio cannot be computed from the filings; that limit matters, because the claim that Tesla acquires buyers more cheaply than Ford or GM is untested. Judged on operating margin, Tesla's 2.6% sits below GM's 8.2% EBIT-adjusted and Ford's 5.5%, while its 18.1% ex-credit gross margin is level with BYD's 18%: the difference is the operating cost line, not the car. The diligence question is what FSD subscription revenue and Megapack-only margin actually are, because those two numbers decide whether the group earns more than its cost of capital [S115, S116, S119].

Tesla converted $1,531M of free cash flow in Q3 2026, but the statements no longer show it earning its cost of capital: a 5.5% trailing return on invested capital sits 57 basis points above the ten-year Treasury, $41,778M of capex since 2023 has coincided with a 61% fall in operating income, and the profit that remains leans on interest income, a payables build and $526M of one-off energy tariff refunds. Normalising those refunds puts trailing adjusted EBITDA at $14,469M, and at 70x that plus net cash the report's 40% base case is $266 a share.

### Revenue recovered, operating profit did not

[table with Q3 2026 column]

Revenue fell for two years before the 2026 rebound while operating income fell throughout, from $8,891M in FY2023 to $3,466M trailing, because research and development rose from $3,969M to $8,861M and selling and administrative cost from $4,800M to $7,485M against gross profit that stayed between $17.1B and $20.0B. Q3 2026 revenue was $28,046M, gross profit $5,494M (19.6%), operating income $718M (2.6%), net income $787M and diluted EPS $0.22, on deliveries down 2% to 486,532 from 497,099, so price, mix and a weaker dollar carried the top line. Reported against adjusted: GAAP net income of $787M against non-GAAP of $1,697M, and diluted EPS of $0.22 against $0.48. The quarter also absorbed a $475M reversal of previously recognised regulatory credit revenue for returned credits, so the 2.6% operating margin understates the underlying figure by 1.7 points [S12, S13, S1, S8].

### Free cash flow is a payables loan and a capex pause

Nine-month operating cash flow of $14,897M exceeded the $13,014M of capital expenditure to leave $1,883M of free cash flow, against $6,220M for FY2025. Management attributes $3.51 billion of the $3.96 billion year-on-year operating-cash-flow increase to working capital, and in Q3 2026 alone free cash flow of $1,531M rested on a $2,590M working-capital inflow, of which accounts payable supplied $1,920M and accrued liabilities $1,950M; stripping it out, quarterly free cash flow was -$1,059M, and $3,670M of capex sat in liabilities at 2026-09-30. Across nine months, payables rose $3,868M to $17,239M and the cash conversion cycle fell to 2.6 days from 13.0, so without the payables build nine-month free cash flow would have been -$1,985M. Capital expenditure nearly doubled from $6,134M a year earlier, and the 2026 plan was restated between filings — "in excess of $25 billion" in July 2026, "in excess of $20 billion" in October 2026 — leaving full-year 2026 free cash flow between -$1,290M and +$1,160M depending on whether Q4 operating cash flow matches Q4 2025's $3,813M or Q3 2026's $6,263M [S8, S9, S83, S102].

### The balance sheet carries the plan; the capital does not earn its keep

[returns table]

Cash of $17,853M and short-term investments of $27,594M against $9,267M of debt gave $36,180M of net cash at 2026-09-30, and three credit agreements signed in September 2026 lifted unused committed facilities to $30.00B from $6.43B at 2025-12-31, so the $20B capex year is funded several times over without equity. The obligations outside the debt line matter more: $7,955M of minimum lease payments at 2025-12-31, of which $1,320M falls due within twelve months; an accrued warranty reserve of $7,414M that grew 20.9% in nine months against 10% delivery growth; and $7,055M of deferred revenue. Goodwill and intangibles of $381M are 0.2% of assets, and interest coverage of 9.96x is ample but has fallen from 56.99x in FY2023. Returns have fallen faster than margins: return on invested capital went from 28.3% in FY2023 to 13.7%, 7.0% and 5.5% trailing, and return on equity from 27.9% to 3.8%; the 5.5% compares with a 4.93% ten-year Treasury yield on 2026-10-30, leaving 57 basis points for equity risk. The capex record explains it: $41,778M spent in FY2023 through the first nine months of 2026 against a $5,425M fall in operating income over the same span, an incremental return that is negative at group level. Nothing has been returned to shareholders: no dividend and no repurchase from FY2021 to Q3 2026, while $2,000M of cash went into the xAI investment agreed in January 2026 and converted into SpaceX Class A stock on 2026-03-12 [S8, S1, S10, S115, S104].

### The EBITDA bridge and the price it supports

[bridge table]

Trailing adjusted EBITDA of $14,995M is the sum of four quarters; subtracting the $526M Q3 2026 IEEPA energy refund gives $14,469M, held at $14.5bn in the base case with no credit recovery, no robotaxi line and energy at 15%. The bull case's $506.05 is not an EBITDA output: 3,952.6M shares × $506.05 = $2,000bn, exactly the first market-capitalisation gate of the 2025 CEO award, and 131 times the $15.3bn of EBITDA the same case assumes. A 70x multiple on $14.5bn plus $36.18bn of net cash gives $266, the 40% base case; the report's distribution — 30% bull at $506.05, 40% base at $266, 22% bear at $156 and 8% full de-rating at $64-101 — produces a -25.2% expected return [S8, S9, S10].

### What flatters the number, and what would change it

Interest income of $1,301M was 42.9% of nine-month pre-tax income and $445M was 46.5% of the Q3 2026 figure, against 17.5% in FY2024. Stock-based compensation of $3,346M in nine months is 4.3% of revenue and the main reason non-GAAP profit more than doubles GAAP profit; EPS is struck on 3,240M basic and 3,541M diluted weighted-average shares against 3,952,648,559 shares outstanding at 2026-09-30, and the 710M difference is the 423.7M unearned shares of the 2025 CEO award plus 286.4M unvested 2018 restricted shares, both already inside the issued count, while the diluted count adds about 301M options and RSUs. An effective tax rate of 20% against 27% was helped by a smaller valuation-allowance release in Q2 2026, and cost of automotive sales benefited from what management calls warranty adjustments while the warranty reserve rose 20.9%. Sensitivity: a percentage point of ex-credit automotive margin is worth $800M a year on $80,000M of automotive revenue, 6.4 times a point of energy margin at $12,300M, and each $1B of capex is $1B of free cash flow. The $1.5bn cut from the earlier $16.0bn base is 12 points of energy margin on $12.3bn of trailing energy revenue (27% to 15%); at 14-18% energy margin, $14.5bn of adjusted EBITDA and $20B of capex, free cash flow is roughly $0 to +$0.5bn, not the $2.0bn the 30% energy assumption implied. The variable that moves the outcome most is capex, a management decision worth $5B in a single restatement between July and October 2026 — more than six points of automotive margin. The diligence question is what the 2027 capex number is and whether the payables build reflects renegotiated terms or deferred payments [S8, S83, S1, S117, S102].

arguments.markdown:
Tesla sells cars, storage projects and services, and the returns are lower and more borrowed than the segment headlines suggest: the car earned an 18.1% gross margin excluding regulatory credits in Q3 2026, not enough to cover group research and selling cost, storage's 33.1% quarter falls to 14.8% once the $526M IEEPA tariff refund is removed, and the group's pre-tax profit was small enough that interest income supplied 46.5% of it. The return is earned on a mixed gross-profit pool and on the cash pile, not on a structurally superior unit economic model.

### Three segments, three ways of getting paid

The automotive segment took 73.3% of third-quarter 2026 revenue ($20,560M of $28,046M), services and other 16.4% ($4,605M) and energy generation and storage 10.3% ($2,881M). The buyer differs in each: a retail or fleet customer pays cash or finances a car at transfer of control; an energy customer — a utility, developer or data-centre operator — pays on project milestones across quarters; a service customer pays per transaction for collision repair, maintenance or a Supercharging session; another automaker pays for regulatory credits at transfer of title. The mix has moved: energy was 6.2% of FY2023 revenue ($6,035M) and 13.5% in FY2025 ($12,771M), while automotive revenue fell from $82,419M to $69,526M. The only recurring software charge is FSD (Supervised) at $99 a month, with 1.74 million active subscriptions on 2026-09-30 against 1.04 million a year earlier [S8, S1, S121].

### The vehicle does not pay for the research budget

| Per unit (one vehicle delivered), Q3 2026 | USD per unit | Note | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| Automotive revenue | 42,259 | $20,560M ÷ 486,532 deliveries | S9 |
| Cost of automotive revenue | (34,436) | materials, labour, overhead, warranty, tariffs | S8 |
| Automotive gross profit | 7,823 | 18.5% margin | S8 |
| Regulatory credits inside that profit | 232 | $113M ÷ 486,532; no matching cost | S8 |
| Automotive gross profit excluding credits | 7,590 | 18.1% of $20,447M ex-credit revenue | S8 |
| Group R&D and SG&A per unit | (9,817) | $4,776M ÷ 486,532, all charged to the car | S9 |
| Automotive-only operating contribution | (1,994) | a loss before energy and services | derived |
| Energy and services gross profit per unit | 3,470 | $1,688M ÷ 486,532 | S8 |
| Group operating profit per unit | 1,476 | $718M ÷ 486,532 | S9 |
| Interest income per unit | 915 | $445M ÷ 486,532 | S8 |
| Pre-tax profit per unit | 1,965 | $956M ÷ 486,532 | S8 |

A delivered car carried $42,259 of automotive revenue and $34,436 of cost, leaving $7,823 of gross profit, $7,590 excluding credits; spreading $4,776M of group research and development and selling cost over 486,532 deliveries costs $9,817 a vehicle, so the automotive line alone runs at about -$1,994 a vehicle. Energy and services add $3,470 a vehicle and turn that into $1,476 of operating profit and, with $445M of interest income, $1,965 of pre-tax profit. Cost per vehicle was $33,666 in Q4 2025, $35,786 in Q1 2026 and $34,436 in Q3 2026, so unit cost is not falling; the rise in ex-credit automotive margin from 15.4% to 18.1% year on year arrived with a richer Asia-Pacific delivery mix in Q3 2026, not from the factory [S9, S8].

::: evidence
**The reported credit collapse is a clawback of past revenue, not yet a collapse in current demand — but the contracted backlog says it is coming.**

Reported credit revenue fell from $542M in Q4 2025 to $380M in Q1 2026, $146M in Q2 2026 and $113M in Q3 2026, after $1,993M in FY2025. The Q3 figure is net of a $475M reversal of previously recognised credits for contractual returns, so gross sales were about $588M — higher than Q4 2025 — and the reported line overstates the decline. The forward indicator is worse: contracted obligations with original terms over one year fell to $384M at 2026-09-30 from $841M at 2025-12-31, only $201M due within twelve months. Toyota and Stellantis left Tesla's European CO2 pool for 2026, with Subaru also reported out; Tesla names no credit buyer [S8, S83, S1, S123].
:::

### Storage's 33% is a tariff refund, not a run-rate

Energy reported $954M of gross profit on $2,881M of revenue in Q3 2026, 33.1%, after 20.4% in Q2 2026. The 10-Q note says Tesla recognised $526M of IEEPA tariff refunds as a reduction to energy cost of revenue and $339M as a reduction to energy revenue for refunds owed to customers; first-half amounts were immaterial. Removing the $526M cost credit leaves $428M, or 14.8%, with the $339M customer pass-through still depressing revenue. The earnings call also attributed the margin to warranty true-ups, but no filing quantifies that piece, so the $526M cannot be split and 14.8% is the conservative ex-refund figure; adding the $339M back as well would give 23.8%, which assumes the customer price cuts reverse. Q1 2026's 39.5% and Q2's 20.4% carry no refund, so the apparent Q3 improvement is entirely the refund: ex-refund, Q3 is below Q2 [S8, S9, S117].

| Energy segment, $M unless stated | Q1 2026 | Q2 2026 | Q3 2026 | 9M 2026 | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Revenue | 2,408 | 3,139 | 2,881 | 8,428 | S9 |
| Gross profit as reported | 952 | 640 | 954 | 2,546 | S9 |
| Gross margin as reported | 39.5% | 20.4% | 33.1% | 30.2% | S9 |
| IEEPA refund to cost of revenue | — | — | 526 | 526 | S8 |
| Gross profit ex-refund | 952 | 640 | 428 | 2,020 | derived |
| Gross margin ex-refund | 39.5% | 20.4% | 14.8% | 24.0% | derived |

| Storage benchmark | Gross margin | Period | Basis | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Tesla energy | 33.1% / 14.8% | Q3 2026 | as reported / ex-IEEPA refund | S8, S9 |
| Fluence | 13.1%; 5.1% | FY2025; June 2026 quarter | as reported | S174, S61 |
| Sungrow storage | 36.49% | FY2025 | as reported | S176 |
| CATL storage batteries | 23.96% | H1 2026 | as reported | S177 |

At 14.8%, Tesla is near Fluence's 13.1% fiscal-year margin, not six times Fluence's worst quarter — the 5.1% June 2026 print carried project liquidated damages and cost overruns, and is the wrong comparison. Sungrow's storage business earned 36.49% in FY2025 and CATL's storage batteries 23.96% in H1 2026, both as reported and both above Tesla; a vertically integrated Megapack should sit between the integrator and the cell maker, which is where 14.8-24.0% puts it, not at a structural premium. Revenue per kWh fell to $210 in Q3 2026 from $274 in Q1 2026, and ex-refund gross profit per kWh was $31 against $70 reported, so the segment is price- and volume-sensitive, not a fixed 30% annuity.

### Services is the quiet second engine, and robotaxi is the unpriced one

Services and other grew revenue 33% to $4,605M and gross profit to a record $734M, 15.9%, from 14.1% in Q2 2026 and 10.5% a year earlier; used vehicles, collision, maintenance and paid Supercharging are the lines, and Rivian's software and services segment earned 42% on $605M, so Tesla's margin is below the best comparable on 7.6 times the revenue. Robotaxi is the largest unpriced unit economic in the case and the least disclosed: Tesla reports nearly two million cumulative unsupervised miles, a 1,051-vehicle authorised Texas fleet and a Cybercab launch, but no revenue, no paid trips and no cost per paid mile. Insurance, remote supervision, vehicle depreciation, charging and maintenance are the cost lines; each is undisclosed. If total cost is 60% of the fare, a 2x cost per mile turns a 40% contribution margin into -20%; if cost is 50%, 2x leaves zero. A revenue line with positive contribution is the single fact that would move the valuation; without it the 15% autonomy branch of the bull case rests on miles, not money [S9, S120, S153].

### What breaks even, and what cannot be measured

| Line of business | Pricing metric | Price per unit | Period | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Vehicles | per vehicle delivered, blended across models | $42,259 revenue, $34,436 cost | Q3 2026 | S9 |
| Regulatory credits | per credit sold to another automaker | not disclosed; $113M net of a $475M reversal | Q3 2026 | S8 |
| Energy storage | per kWh deployed, Megapack and Powerwall blended | $210/kWh revenue, $70/kWh gross profit | Q3 2026 | S9 |
| FSD (Supervised) | per vehicle per month | $99 | 2026-10 | S121 |
| Megapack to SpaceX | per project, milestone billed | not disclosed; $626M of revenue | 9M 2026 | S8 |
| Vehicle leasing | per vehicle per month | not disclosed; $353M leasing revenue | Q3 2026 | S8 |
| Supercharging | per session or per kWh | not disclosed | Q3 2026 | S8 |
| Robotaxi and Cybercab | per ride | not disclosed | Q3 2026 | S9 |

At Q3 2026 unit economics, the automotive line covers its share of group cost only at about 629,000 deliveries a quarter excluding credits (611,000 including them), 29% above the 486,532 delivered. Tesla discloses no customer-acquisition cost — there is no marketing line in the statements — so SG&A at 7.2% of revenue is the nearest proxy and a CAC payback or LTV:CAC ratio cannot be computed from the filings; that limit matters, because the claim that Tesla acquires buyers more cheaply than Ford or GM is untested. Judged on operating margin, Tesla's 2.6% sits below GM's 8.2% EBIT-adjusted and Ford's 5.5%, while its 18.1% ex-credit gross margin is level with BYD's 18%: the difference is the operating cost line, not the car. The diligence question is what FSD subscription revenue and Megapack-only margin actually are, because those two numbers decide whether the group earns more than its cost of capital [S115, S116, S119].

arguments.markdown:
Tesla sells cars, storage and services, and the returns are lower and more borrowed than the headlines suggest: the car earned an 18.1% ex-credit gross margin in Q3 2026, short of group research and selling cost; storage's 33.1% falls to 14.8% without the $526M IEEPA tariff refund; and interest income supplied 46.5% of pre-tax profit. The return is earned on a mixed gross-profit pool and the cash pile, not a structurally superior unit economic model.

### Three segments, three ways of getting paid

The automotive segment took 73.3% of third-quarter 2026 revenue ($20,560M of $28,046M), services and other 16.4% ($4,605M) and energy generation and storage 10.3% ($2,881M). The buyer differs in each: a retail or fleet customer pays cash or finances a car at transfer of control; an energy customer — a utility, developer or data-centre operator — pays on project milestones across quarters; a service customer pays per transaction for repair, maintenance or charging; another automaker pays for regulatory credits at transfer of title. The mix has moved: energy was 6.2% of FY2023 revenue ($6,035M) and 13.5% in FY2025 ($12,771M), while automotive revenue fell from $82,419M to $69,526M. The only recurring software charge is FSD (Supervised) at $99 a month, with 1.74 million active subscriptions at 2026-09-30, up from 1.04 million [S8, S1, S121].

### The vehicle does not pay for the research budget

| Per unit (one vehicle delivered), Q3 2026 | USD per unit | Note | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| Automotive revenue | 42,259 | $20,560M ÷ 486,532 deliveries | S9 |
| Cost of automotive revenue | (34,436) | materials, labour, overhead, warranty, tariffs | S8 |
| Automotive gross profit | 7,823 | 18.5% margin | S8 |
| Regulatory credits inside that profit | 232 | $113M ÷ 486,532; no matching cost | S8 |
| Automotive gross profit excluding credits | 7,590 | 18.1% of $20,447M ex-credit revenue | S8 |
| Group R&D and SG&A per unit | (9,817) | $4,776M ÷ 486,532, all charged to the car | S9 |
| Automotive-only operating contribution | (1,994) | a loss before energy and services | derived |
| Energy and services gross profit per unit | 3,470 | $1,688M ÷ 486,532 | S8 |
| Group operating profit per unit | 1,476 | $718M ÷ 486,532 | S9 |
| Interest income per unit | 915 | $445M ÷ 486,532 | S8 |
| Pre-tax profit per unit | 1,965 | $956M ÷ 486,532 | S8 |

A delivered car carried $42,259 of automotive revenue and $34,436 of cost, leaving $7,823 of gross profit, $7,590 excluding credits; spreading $4,776M of group research and development and selling cost over 486,532 deliveries costs $9,817 a vehicle, so the automotive line alone runs at about -$1,994 a vehicle. Energy and services add $3,470 a vehicle and turn that into $1,476 of operating profit and, with $445M of interest income, $1,965 of pre-tax profit. Cost per vehicle was $33,666 in Q4 2025 and $34,436 in Q3 2026, so unit cost is not falling; the rise in ex-credit margin from 15.4% to 18.1% came with a richer Asia-Pacific mix, not from the factory [S9, S8].

::: evidence
**The reported credit collapse is a clawback of past revenue, not yet a collapse in current demand — but the contracted backlog says it is coming.**

Reported credit revenue fell from $542M in Q4 2025 to $380M in Q1 2026, $146M in Q2 2026 and $113M in Q3 2026, after $1,993M in FY2025. The Q3 figure is net of a $475M reversal of previously recognised credits for contractual returns, so gross sales were about $588M — higher than Q4 2025 — and the reported line overstates the decline. The forward indicator is worse: contracted obligations with original terms over one year fell to $384M at 2026-09-30 from $841M at 2025-12-31. Toyota and Stellantis left Tesla's European CO2 pool for 2026; Tesla names no credit buyer [S8, S83, S1, S123].
:::

### Storage's 33% is a tariff refund, not a run-rate

Energy reported $954M of gross profit on $2,881M of revenue in Q3 2026, 33.1%, after 20.4% in Q2 2026. The 10-Q note says Tesla recognised $526M of IEEPA tariff refunds as a reduction to energy cost of revenue and $339M as a reduction to energy revenue for refunds owed to customers; first-half amounts were immaterial. Removing the $526M cost credit leaves $428M, or 14.8%, with the $339M customer pass-through still depressing revenue. The earnings call also attributed the margin to warranty true-ups, but no filing quantifies that piece, so the $526M cannot be split and 14.8% is the conservative ex-refund figure; adding the $339M back as well would give 23.8%, but that assumes the customer price cuts reverse. Q1's 39.5% and Q2's 20.4% carry no refund, so the Q3 improvement is entirely the refund: ex-refund, Q3 is below Q2 [S8, S9, S117].

| Energy segment, $M unless stated | Q1 2026 | Q2 2026 | Q3 2026 | 9M 2026 | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Revenue | 2,408 | 3,139 | 2,881 | 8,428 | S9 |
| Gross profit as reported | 952 | 640 | 954 | 2,546 | S9 |
| Gross margin as reported | 39.5% | 20.4% | 33.1% | 30.2% | S9 |
| IEEPA refund to cost of revenue | — | — | 526 | 526 | S8 |
| Gross profit ex-refund | 952 | 640 | 428 | 2,020 | derived |
| Gross margin ex-refund | 39.5% | 20.4% | 14.8% | 24.0% | derived |

| Storage benchmark | Gross margin | Period | Basis | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Tesla energy | 33.1% / 14.8% | Q3 2026 | as reported / ex-IEEPA refund | S8, S9 |
| Fluence | 13.1%; 5.1% | FY2025; June 2026 quarter | as reported | S174, S61 |
| Sungrow storage | 36.49% | FY2025 | as reported | S176 |
| CATL storage batteries | 23.96% | H1 2026 | as reported | S177 |

At 14.8%, Tesla is near Fluence's 13.1% fiscal-year margin, not six times Fluence's worst quarter — the 5.1% June 2026 print carried project liquidated damages and cost overruns, and is the wrong comparison. Sungrow's storage business earned 36.49% in FY2025 and CATL's storage batteries 23.96% in H1 2026; a vertically integrated Megapack should sit between the integrator and the cell maker, which is where 14.8-24.0% puts it, not at a structural premium. Revenue per kWh fell to $210 in Q3 2026 from $274 in Q1 2026, and ex-refund gross profit per kWh was $31 against $70 reported, so the segment is price- and volume-sensitive, not a fixed 30% annuity.

### Services is the quiet second engine, and robotaxi is the unpriced one

Services and other grew revenue 33% to $4,605M and gross profit to a record $734M, 15.9%, from 14.1% in Q2 2026 and 10.5% a year earlier; used vehicles, collision, maintenance and paid Supercharging are the lines, and Rivian's software and services segment earned 42% on $605M, so Tesla's margin is below the best comparable on 7.6 times the revenue. Robotaxi is the largest unpriced unit economic in the case: Tesla reports nearly two million cumulative unsupervised miles, a 1,051-vehicle authorised Texas fleet and a Cybercab launch, but no revenue, no paid trips and no cost per paid mile. Insurance, remote supervision, vehicle depreciation, charging and maintenance are the cost lines; each is undisclosed. If total cost is 60% of the fare, a 2x cost per mile turns a 40% contribution margin into -20%; if cost is 50%, 2x leaves zero. A revenue line with positive contribution is the fact that would move the valuation; without it the 15% autonomy branch of the bull case rests on miles, not money [S9, S120, S153].

### What breaks even, and what cannot be measured

| Line of business | Pricing metric | Price per unit | Period | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Vehicles | per vehicle delivered, blended across models | $42,259 revenue, $34,436 cost | Q3 2026 | S9 |
| Regulatory credits | per credit sold to another automaker | not disclosed; $113M net of a $475M reversal | Q3 2026 | S8 |
| Energy storage | per kWh deployed, Megapack and Powerwall blended | $210/kWh revenue, $70/kWh gross profit | Q3 2026 | S9 |
| FSD (Supervised) | per vehicle per month | $99 | 2026-10 | S121 |
| Megapack to SpaceX | per project, milestone billed | not disclosed; $626M of revenue | 9M 2026 | S8 |
| Vehicle leasing | per vehicle per month | not disclosed; $353M leasing revenue | Q3 2026 | S8 |
| Robotaxi and Cybercab | per ride | not disclosed | Q3 2026 | S9 |

At Q3 2026 unit economics, the automotive line covers its share of group cost only at about 629,000 deliveries a quarter excluding credits (611,000 including them), 29% above the 486,532 delivered. Tesla discloses no customer-acquisition cost — there is no marketing line in the statements — so SG&A at 7.2% of revenue is the nearest proxy and a CAC payback or LTV:CAC ratio cannot be computed from the filings; the claim that Tesla acquires buyers more cheaply than Ford or GM is therefore untested. Judged on operating margin, Tesla's 2.6% sits below GM's 8.2% EBIT-adjusted and Ford's 5.5%, while its 18.1% ex-credit gross margin is level with BYD's 18%: the difference is the operating cost line, not the car. The diligence question is what FSD subscription revenue and Megapack-only margin actually are, because those two numbers decide whether the group earns more than its cost of capital [S115, S116, S119].

{"content":[{"type":"text","text":"## Competitive Landscape (competition, revision 5 by Market Analyst, 8,931 characters)
Tesla is winning the market that is shrinking and losing the one that is growing. It holds the US electric-vehicle market at a share no rival approaches while that market contracts, ranks fourth among China's new-energy brands in a pool that is itself shrinking, and its European recovery has come inside a pool growing faster than it. What Tesla owns is narrower than the narrative: the charging standard every major automaker has licensed, 1.74 million paid FSD subscriptions, and a storage business whose 33.1% reported gross margin falls to 14.8% once $526 million of tariff refunds and warranty true-ups are removed — mid-pack against CATL and Sungrow, not ahead of them [S8, S9, S167].

### In the United States, Tesla sets the price because it holds the pool

Tesla sold 144,094 US electric vehicles in Q3 2026 for 54% of the market, and 386,194 in nine months for 52.9%, with US volume down 14.4% against a market down 30.3%. Share gains in a contracting pool flatter the position. When a $7,500 credit disappears, the brand with the densest charging footprint keeps the remaining buyers. The question is whether Tesla can hold price, and it has — automotive gross margin rose to 18.5% in Q3 2026 from 17.0% [S145, S8].

### China is where Tesla is the price taker

BYD sold 456,713 passenger cars in September 2026, 273,143 of them battery-electric, and 3,078,490 in nine months — 2.3 times Tesla's 1,324,681. Geely sold 119,682 and Xiaomi 40,015 retail units in September. BYD earned 19.46% gross margin overseas against 16.66% at home in 2025, a domestic ceiling Tesla cannot price above; Tesla's China retail of 64,837 was 3.8 times smaller than BYD's in September while Chinese battery-electric wholesale grew 18.3%. In driver assistance, Huawei and Momenta together supply more than 80% of China's urban NOA systems, Momenta alone 65% [S138, S146, S149, S168].

### Europe: growth in units, no evidence of share

EU battery-electric registrations reached 1,931,465 in January-September 2026 at a 22.7% share, with September at 29.9%, so the pool expanded 49% while Tesla's European deliveries recovered from a 2025 slump. A recovery off a collapsed base inside a pool growing that fast is not share gain; Tesla discloses no EU unit count, and ACEA's manufacturer table would settle it. Volkswagen, Renault, Stellantis and Hyundai-Kia sell compliance models; tariffed Chinese BEVs undercut. Tesla's handicap is a two-model line-up: Model 3/Y were 478,237 of 486,532 deliveries in Q3 2026 [S140, S147].

### Storage: integration, not a cost moat

The 33.1% energy gross margin Tesla reported for Q3 2026 is not comparable with an integrator's clean number: $526 million of IEEPA tariff refunds and warranty true-ups sit inside cost of revenue, so the underlying margin is $428 million on $2,881 million, or 14.8%. On that basis Tesla is mid-pack: Fluence earned 13.1% in fiscal 2025 and 5.1% in the June 2026 quarter, CATL's energy-storage segment 23.96% in H1 2026, Sungrow's storage segment 32.43%, and LG Energy Solution a 1.5% operating margin in Q2 2026 [S8, S9, S61, S66, S167, S166, S172, S169]. Integration does not show up as a margin outlier, and revenue per GWh fell 23% to $210 million from $273 million as system prices deflated. The counter-evidence is scale: 36.0 GWh in nine months and Autobidder may still give Tesla the lowest installed cost per project even at a mid-teens margin.

### In paid autonomy Tesla trails, and in driver assistance it is no longer alone

Waymo ran 500,000 paid rides a week across 10 US cities by March 2026 with about 3,700 vehicles and had logged 220.6 million rider-only miles through March 2026. Tesla began Cybercab rides in Austin on 2026-09-03 and stood at 1,051 vehicles on the Texas authorisation list on 2026-10-27 (544 Cybercab, 507 Model Y); it reports 2.0 million cumulative unsupervised miles, 0.9% of Waymo's rider-only total, is absent from California's driverless deployment permits, and discloses no ride count or fare. Baidu's Apollo Go ran 3.4 million trips in Q4 2025; Pony.ai passed 1,400 vehicles in March 2026. Insurance, teleoperation and cost per paid mile are undisclosed; a 10-20% swing in autonomy value turns on them. The supervised market is not Tesla's either: GM's Super Cruise is hands-free on about 750,000 compatible miles in the US and Canada, Ford's BlueCruise on more than 130,000 Blue Zone miles, and comma.ai's openpilot sells aftermarket kits with no OEM fleet. FSD's 1.74 million subscriptions are the largest single pool, but hands-free highway driving is now a $40-50 a month OEM feature, which caps what Tesla can charge and explains a 17.1% attach rate [S151, S125, S142, S171, S130, S170].

{"content":[{"type":"text","text":"## Market & Industry Analysis (market, revision 5 by Market Analyst, 8,952 characters)
Tesla's problem is not that its markets are small; it is that the two that made it are contracting while the two that grow are priced per unit, not per promise. Global electric-car sales are expected to reach 23.0 million units in 2026, 28% of all car sales, from more than 20 million in 2025, and the IEA projects half of global sales by 2035 [S9, S137]. Dividing 23.0 million by 28% implies 82 million light vehicles, so the electric pool is the whole case: Tesla delivered 1,324,681 vehicles in the first nine months of 2026 (358,023; 480,126; 486,532) — a run-rate of 1.77 million, or 7.7% of the 2026 electric pool and 2.2% of all cars. Unit growth of 15% in 2026 slows to a 7.7% CAGR to 2035 on the IEA's own 50%-share projection, while Tesla's third quarter fell 2% year on year. That is a share problem inside a decelerating market: what an investor buys is not category growth but the price Tesla can hold for a differentiated slice of it.

**Market size, top-down and bottom-up**

| Layer | 2026 size | How derived | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| TAM — global light vehicles | 82m units | 23.0m electric ÷ 28% share | S137 |
| SAM — global electric cars (BEV+PHEV) | 23.0m units | IEA forecast, 28% of sales | S137 |
| SOM — Tesla deliveries | 1.32m in 9M 2026; 1.77m run-rate (7.7% of SAM) | Quarterly delivery table | S9 |
| TAM — global storage deployments | 158 GW / 459 GWh | BloombergNEF 2026 forecast | S141 |
| SOM — Tesla storage | 36.0 GWh in 9M 2026 (7.8% of 2026E) | 10-Q plus deployment table | S8, S9 |
| TAM — paid robotaxi revenue | $0.3-0.5bn fare-based, against $3.5-5.5bn third-party | 500,000 Waymo rides/week × 52 × $12-18 assumed fare; ~3,700 Waymo vehicles at 2026-03 | S142, S144, S151 |

### The two largest pools shrank by policy, not by demand

Removing the $7,500 federal credit on 2025-09-30 cut the US electric pool by 30.3% year to date: sales fell 36% year on year in Q4 2025, and were 30.3% below the prior year through September 2026 after a 7.7% sequential rebound to 266,630 in Q3, when electric cars were 6.4% of US new-vehicle sales and Tesla's own US volume fell 14.4%. China's new-energy retail fell 16.7% year on year to 1.084 million in September 2026, the ninth consecutive decline, and 12.8% to 7.758 million in nine months, while penetration hit a record 67.0% only because total passenger-car retail fell 28.0%; battery-electric retail fell 7.4%, plug-in hybrid retail 35.6% and range-extended electric 19.3%, while battery-electric wholesale rose 18.3% and NEV exports 163.5% to 558,000. Tightening China's purchase-tax preference and withdrawing local subsidies raised the cash price of the cheapest cars first and pushed production abroad. Tesla held 52.9% of the smaller US pool and was China's fourth-largest NEV brand by retail at 64,837 units: US equity value is now a bet on a 6-7% electric share of the US market in 2027, and China is a capped, price-deflationary market whose growth reaches Tesla through exports that carry tariffs [S138, S139, S145].

### Europe is the only vehicle market growing fast enough to matter

EU battery-electric registrations reached 1,931,465 in January-September 2026, a 22.7% share against 16.1% a year earlier, and September alone ran at 290,117 units and a 29.9% share, up 72.9% year on year on a total market up 5.7%. On those two shares the electric pool grew 49% in units, the only large market where Tesla can add volume without cutting price. EU demand is regulation-created: the 2025-2027 CO2 step forces fleet averages down, and the Commission's 2025-12-16 proposal to replace the 100% 2035 target with a 90% cut has moved the long-dated backstop into Parliament and Council, where ministers remain split. Europe carries Tesla's 2026 volume growth (Berlin posted record production in Q3 2026), and that growth is capped by a policy being renegotiated while it is relied upon [S140, S147].

### Storage compounds in volume and deflates in price

Global storage installations reached 112 GW in 2025 and are forecast at 158 GW and 459 GWh in 2026, a 41% annual increase, with BloombergNEF seeing 3.1 TW cumulative by 2036. Tesla deployed 36.0 GWh in the first nine months of 2026, 7.8% of the forecast pool, but revenue per GWh fell to $210 million from $273 million — 23% — because Q3 energy revenue fell 16% while deployments rose 9.6%. The reported 33.1% energy gross margin is not the underlying one: $526 million of IEEPA tariff refunds and warranty true-ups sit in cost of revenue, leaving $428 million on $2,881 million, or 14.8%, below CATL's 23.96% energy-storage segment and Sungrow's 32.43% storage margin in H1 2026 and only just above Fluence's 13.1% fiscal-2025 margin. Demand is structural in that Tesla reports its highest-ever order rate and ties backlog to data-centre load growth, not subsidies; but model the segment on revenue per GWh falling faster than volume rises, at a mid-teens clean margin rather than the as-reported figure [S8, S9, S141, S167, S166, S172, S66].

### Paid robotaxi is a Waymo-sized business, not a market yet

The only scaled paid autonomous service is Waymo's: 500,000 paid rides a week across 10 US cities as of 2026-03-27, which is 26 million a year and, at an assumed $12-18 average fare, a $0.3-0.5 billion business; Waymo had logged 220.6 million rider-only miles through March 2026 with about 3,700 vehicles. Third-party research puts the 2026 robotaxi market at $3.5-5.5 billion and 2030 estimates span $27-204 billion, a 7.3x spread that marks sizes built from ride-hailing spend rather than observed fares. Tesla is scaling from a smaller base: the Texas authorisation list showed 1,051 Robotaxi vehicles on 2026-10-27 (544 Cybercab, 507 Model Y), up from 739 on 2026-10-09 on the same list, against Waymo's 3,700, and Tesla reports about 2.0 million cumulative unsupervised miles, 0.9% of Waymo's rider-only total. Tesla discloses no ride count, fare or robotaxi revenue, and no operator discloses insurance, remote supervision or cost per paid mile — the three numbers that decide whether a fare business earns a margin. The serviceable market by 2028 is therefore set by permits and per-mile safety evidence, not TAM studies: a $50 billion 2028 robotaxi line would require Tesla to overtake the incumbent and multiply the 2026 paid market more than twenty-fold [S142, S144, S125, S151, S9, S153].

**Where the growth is, and where Tesla stands**

| Region | Market size (2026) | Growth | Tesla's position | Barriers | Key competitors | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| United States | 266,630 EVs in Q3; 6.4% of sales | −30.3% YTD; +7.7% QoQ | Entered; 52.9% of EV pool; own volume −14.4% | Credit repealed 2025-09-30; OBBBA content rules | Ford, GM, Hyundai-Kia, Rivian | S139, S145 |
| China | 7.758m NEV retail 9M; 67.0% September penetration | −12.8% 9M; BEV retail −7.4% | Entered; fourth-largest brand at 64,837 in September | Purchase-tax preference tightened; local cost advantage | BYD, Geely, Leapmotor, Xiaomi | S138 |
| European Union | 1.93m BEVs in 9M; 22.7% share (29.9% September) | +49% BEV units; total market +5.7% | Entered; recovery off a weak 2025 | CO2 2035 target under review; national incentives | Volkswagen, Renault, Stellantis, Hyundai-Kia, BYD | S140, S147 |
| Rest of world | Not disclosed by Tesla; Chinese NEV exports 3.887m in 9M (+138.8%) | Exports +163.5% in September | Entered; records in Canada, Australia, Japan, Taiwan | Tariffs on Chinese-built cars; charging build-out | BYD, Geely, Toyota | S138, S9 |
| Storage (global) | 158 GW / 459 GWh in 2026E | +41% GW after +48% in 2025 | Entered; 36.0 GWh in 9M, 7.8% of 2026E | Cell supply, tariffs on Chinese cells, interconnection queues | CATL, Sungrow, Fluence, BYD | S141, S8 |

::: evidence
**The demand Tesla is priced for grows everywhere except where it sells most.**

The IEA's 23 million-unit 2026 forecast is carried by Europe (49% BEV unit growth) and by Chinese exports (163.5% in September), while the United States and China — the sources of most of Tesla's 2024-2025 revenue — are down 30.3% and 12.8% year to date. The counterweight is Tesla's own disclosure that battery availability, not orders, limited Q3 2026 volume: the next two quarters may be supply-constrained rather than demand-constrained. [S137, S138, S145]
:::

The implication is allocation, not enthusiasm: Europe and storage are the only growing pools, but storage's clean margin is mid-teens and paid autonomy remains small in fare terms, so neither supports the bull branch that rests on an autonomy proof and a SpaceX combination. Treat US vehicle revenue as share defence at a lower market level, value paid autonomy at zero until rides and fares are disclosed, and let the base and bear branches carry the weight the scenarios already give them. arguments.markdown:
Tesla sells cars, storage and services, and the returns are lower and more borrowed than the headlines suggest: the car earned an 18.1% ex-credit gross margin in Q3 2026, short of group research and selling cost; storage's 33.1% falls to 14.8% without the $526M IEEPA tariff refund; and interest income supplied 46.5% of pre-tax profit. The return is earned on a mixed gross-profit pool and the cash pile, not a structurally superior unit economic model.

### Three segments, three ways of getting paid

The automotive segment took 73.3% of third-quarter 2026 revenue ($20,560M of $28,046M), services and other 16.4% ($4,605M) and energy generation and storage 10.3% ($2,881M). The buyer differs in each: a retail or fleet customer pays cash or finances a car at transfer of control; an energy customer — a utility, developer or data-centre operator — pays on project milestones across quarters; a service customer pays per transaction for repair, maintenance or charging; another automaker pays for regulatory credits at transfer of title. The mix has moved: energy was 6.2% of FY2023 revenue ($6,035M) and 13.5% in FY2025 ($12,771M), while automotive revenue fell from $82,419M to $69,526M. The only recurring software charge is FSD (Supervised) at $99 a month, with 1.74 million active subscriptions at 2026-09-30 [S8, S1, S121].

### The vehicle does not pay for the research budget

| Per unit (one vehicle delivered), Q3 2026 | USD per unit | Note | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| Automotive revenue | 42,259 | $20,560M ÷ 486,532 deliveries | S9 |
| Cost of automotive revenue | (34,436) | materials, labour, overhead, warranty, tariffs | S8 |
| Automotive gross profit | 7,823 | 18.5% margin | S8 |
| Regulatory credits inside that profit | 232 | $113M ÷ 486,532; no matching cost | S8 |
| Automotive gross profit excluding credits | 7,590 | 18.1% of $20,447M ex-credit revenue | S8 |
| Group R&D and SG&A per unit | (9,817) | $4,776M ÷ 486,532, all charged to the car | S9 |
| Automotive-only operating contribution | (1,994) | a loss before energy and services | derived |
| Energy and services gross profit per unit | 3,470 | $1,688M ÷ 486,532 | S8 |
| Group operating profit per unit | 1,476 | $718M ÷ 486,532 | S9 |
| Interest income per unit | 915 | $445M ÷ 486,532 | S8 |
| Pre-tax profit per unit | 1,965 | $956M ÷ 486,532 | S8 |

A delivered car carried $42,259 of automotive revenue and $34,436 of cost, leaving $7,823 of gross profit, $7,590 excluding credits; spreading $4,776M of group research and development and selling cost over 486,532 deliveries costs $9,817 a vehicle, so the automotive line alone runs at about -$1,994 a vehicle. Energy and services add $3,470 a vehicle and turn that into $1,476 of operating profit and, with $445M of interest income, $1,965 of pre-tax profit. Cost per vehicle was $33,666 in Q4 2025 and $34,436 in Q3 2026, so unit cost is not falling; the rise in ex-credit margin from 15.4% to 18.1% came with a richer Asia-Pacific mix, not from the factory [S9, S8].

::: evidence
**The reported credit collapse is a clawback of past revenue, not yet a collapse in current demand — but the contracted backlog says it is coming.**

Reported credit revenue fell from $542M in Q4 2025 to $380M in Q1 2026, $146M in Q2 2026 and $113M in Q3 2026, after $1,993M in FY2025. The Q3 figure is net of a $475M reversal of previously recognised credits for contractual returns, so gross sales were about $588M — higher than Q4 2025 — and the reported line overstates the decline. The forward indicator is worse: contracted obligations with original terms over one year fell to $384M at 2026-09-30 from $841M at 2025-12-31. Toyota and Stellantis left Tesla's European CO2 pool for 2026; Tesla names no credit buyer [S8, S83, S1, S123].
:::

### Storage's 33% is a tariff refund, not a run-rate

Energy reported $954M of gross profit on $2,881M of revenue in Q3 2026, 33.1%, after 20.4% in Q2 2026. The 10-Q note says Tesla recognised $526M of IEEPA tariff refunds as a reduction to energy cost of revenue and $339M as a reduction to energy revenue for refunds owed to customers; first-half amounts were immaterial. Removing the $526M cost credit leaves $428M, or 14.8%, with the $339M customer pass-through still depressing revenue. The earnings call also attributed the margin to warranty true-ups, but no filing quantifies that piece, so the $526M cannot be split and 14.8% is the conservative ex-refund figure; adding the $339M back as well would give 23.8%, but that assumes the customer price cuts reverse. Q1's 39.5% and Q2's 20.4% carry no refund, so the Q3 improvement is entirely the refund: ex-refund, Q3 is below Q2 [S8, S9, S117].

| Energy segment, $M unless stated | Q1 2026 | Q2 2026 | Q3 2026 | 9M 2026 | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Revenue | 2,408 | 3,139 | 2,881 | 8,428 | S9 |
| Gross profit as reported | 952 | 640 | 954 | 2,546 | S9 |
| Gross margin as reported | 39.5% | 20.4% | 33.1% | 30.2% | S9 |
| IEEPA refund to cost of revenue | — | — | 526 | 526 | S8 |
| Gross profit ex-refund | 952 | 640 | 428 | 2,020 | derived |
| Gross margin ex-refund | 39.5% | 20.4% | 14.8% | 24.0% | derived |

| Storage benchmark | Gross margin | Period | Basis | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Tesla energy | 33.1% / 14.8% | Q3 2026 | as reported / ex-IEEPA refund | S8, S9 |
| Fluence | 13.1%; 5.1% | FY2025; June 2026 quarter | as reported | S174, S61 |
| Sungrow storage | 36.49% | FY2025 | as reported | S176 |
| CATL storage batteries | 23.96% | H1 2026 | as reported | S177 |

At 14.8%, Tesla is near Fluence's 13.1% fiscal-year margin, not six times Fluence's worst quarter — the 5.1% June 2026 print carried liquidated damages and cost overruns. Sungrow's storage business earned 36.49% in FY2025 and CATL's storage batteries 23.96% in H1 2026; a vertically integrated Megapack should sit between the integrator and the cell maker, which is where 14.8-24.0% puts it, not at a structural premium. Revenue per kWh fell to $210 in Q3 2026 from $274 in Q1 2026, and ex-refund gross profit per kWh was $31 against $70 reported, so the segment is price- and volume-sensitive, not a fixed 30% annuity.

### Services is the quiet second engine, and robotaxi is the unpriced one

Services and other grew revenue 33% to $4,605M and gross profit to a record $734M, 15.9%, from 14.1% in Q2 2026 and 10.5% a year earlier; used vehicles, collision, maintenance and Supercharging are the lines, and Rivian's software and services segment earned 42% on $605M, so Tesla's margin is below the best comparable on 7.6 times the revenue. Robotaxi is the largest unpriced unit economic in the case: Tesla reports nearly two million cumulative unsupervised miles, a 1,051-vehicle authorised Texas fleet and a Cybercab launch, but no revenue, no paid trips and no cost per paid mile. Insurance, remote supervision, vehicle depreciation, charging and maintenance are the cost lines; each is undisclosed. If total cost is 60% of the fare, a 2x cost per mile turns a 40% contribution margin into -20%; if cost is 50%, 2x leaves zero. A revenue line with positive contribution is the fact that would move the valuation; without it the 15% autonomy branch of the bull case rests on miles, not money [S9, S120, S153].

### What breaks even, and what cannot be measured

| Line of business | Pricing metric | Price per unit | Period | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Vehicles | per vehicle delivered, blended across models | $42,259 revenue, $34,436 cost | Q3 2026 | S9 |
| Regulatory credits | per credit sold to another automaker | not disclosed; $113M net of a $475M reversal | Q3 2026 | S8 |
| Energy storage | per kWh deployed, Megapack and Powerwall blended | $210/kWh revenue, $70/kWh gross profit | Q3 2026 | S9 |
| FSD (Supervised) | per vehicle per month | $99 | 2026-10 | S121 |
| Megapack to SpaceX | per project, milestone billed | not disclosed; $626M of revenue | 9M 2026 | S8 |
| Vehicle leasing | per vehicle per month | not disclosed; $353M leasing revenue | Q3 2026 | S8 |
| Robotaxi and Cybercab | per ride | not disclosed | Q3 2026 | S9 |

At Q3 2026 unit economics, the automotive line covers its share of group cost only at about 629,000 deliveries a quarter excluding credits (611,000 including them), 29% above the 486,532 delivered. Tesla discloses no customer-acquisition cost — there is no marketing line in the statements — so SG&A at 7.2% of revenue is the nearest proxy and a CAC payback or LTV:CAC ratio cannot be computed from the filings; the claim that Tesla acquires buyers more cheaply than Ford or GM is therefore untested. Judged on operating margin, Tesla's 2.6% sits below GM's 8.2% EBIT-adjusted and Ford's 5.5%, while its 18.1% ex-credit gross margin is level with BYD's 18%: the difference is the operating cost line, not the car. The diligence question is what FSD subscription revenue and Megapack-only margin actually are, because those two numbers decide whether the group earns more than its cost of capital [S115, S116, S119].
