arguments.markdown:
Tesla sells cars, storage and services, and the returns are lower and more borrowed than the headlines suggest: the car earned an 18.1% ex-credit gross margin in Q3 2026, short of group research and selling cost; storage's 33.1% falls to 14.8% without the $526M IEEPA tariff refund; and interest income supplied 46.5% of pre-tax profit. The return is earned on a mixed gross-profit pool and the cash pile, not a structurally superior unit economic model.

### Three segments, three ways of getting paid

The automotive segment took 73.3% of third-quarter 2026 revenue ($20,560M of $28,046M), services and other 16.4% ($4,605M) and energy generation and storage 10.3% ($2,881M). The buyer differs in each: a retail or fleet customer pays cash or finances a car at transfer of control; an energy customer — a utility, developer or data-centre operator — pays on project milestones across quarters; a service customer pays per transaction for repair, maintenance or charging; another automaker pays for regulatory credits at transfer of title. The mix has moved: energy was 6.2% of FY2023 revenue ($6,035M) and 13.5% in FY2025 ($12,771M), while automotive revenue fell from $82,419M to $69,526M. The recurring software charge is FSD (Supervised) at $99 a month, with 1.74 million active subscriptions at 2026-09-30 [S8, S1, S121].

### The vehicle does not pay for the research budget

| Per unit (one vehicle delivered), Q3 2026 | USD per unit | Note | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| Automotive revenue | 42,259 | $20,560M ÷ 486,532 deliveries | S9 |
| Cost of automotive revenue | (34,436) | materials, labour, overhead, warranty, tariffs | S8 |
| Automotive gross profit | 7,823 | 18.5% margin | S8 |
| Regulatory credits inside that profit | 232 | $113M ÷ 486,532; no matching cost | S8 |
| Automotive gross profit excluding credits | 7,590 | 18.1% of $20,447M ex-credit revenue | S8 |
| Group R&D and SG&A per unit | (9,817) | $4,776M ÷ 486,532, all charged to the car | S9 |
| Automotive-only operating contribution | (1,994) | a loss before energy and services | derived |
| Energy and services gross profit per unit | 3,470 | $1,688M ÷ 486,532 | S8 |
| Group operating profit per unit | 1,476 | $718M ÷ 486,532 | S9 |
| Interest income per unit | 915 | $445M ÷ 486,532 | S8 |
| Pre-tax profit per unit | 1,965 | $956M ÷ 486,532 | S8 |

A delivered car carried $42,259 of automotive revenue and $34,436 of cost, leaving $7,823 of gross profit, $7,590 excluding credits; spreading $4,776M of group research and development and selling cost over 486,532 deliveries costs $9,817 a vehicle, so the automotive line alone runs at about -$1,994 a vehicle. Energy and services add $3,470 a vehicle and turn that into $1,476 of operating profit and, with $445M of interest income, $1,965 of pre-tax profit. Cost per vehicle was $33,666 in Q4 2025 and $34,436 in Q3 2026, so unit cost is not falling; the rise in ex-credit margin from 15.4% to 18.1% came with a richer Asia-Pacific mix, not from the factory [S9, S8].

::: evidence
**The reported credit collapse is a clawback of past revenue, not yet a collapse in current demand — but the contracted backlog says it is coming.**

Reported credit revenue fell from $542M in Q4 2025 to $380M in Q1 2026, $146M in Q2 2026 and $113M in Q3 2026, after $1,993M in FY2025. The Q3 figure is net of a $475M reversal of previously recognised credits for contractual returns, so gross sales were about $588M — higher than Q4 2025 — and the reported line overstates the decline. The forward indicator is worse: contracted obligations with original terms over one year fell to $384M at 2026-09-30 from $841M at 2025-12-31. Toyota and Stellantis left Tesla's European CO2 pool for 2026; Tesla names no credit buyer [S8, S83, S1, S123].
:::

### Storage's 33% is a tariff refund, not a run-rate

Energy reported $954M of gross profit on $2,881M of revenue in Q3 2026, 33.1%, after 20.4% in Q2 2026. The 10-Q note says Tesla recognised $526M of IEEPA tariff refunds as a reduction to energy cost of revenue and $339M as a reduction to energy revenue for refunds owed to customers; first-half amounts were immaterial. Removing the $526M cost credit leaves $428M, or 14.8%, with the $339M customer pass-through still depressing revenue. The earnings call also attributed the margin to warranty true-ups, but no filing quantifies that piece, so the $526M cannot be split and 14.8% is the conservative ex-refund figure; adding the $339M back as well would give 23.8%, but that assumes the customer price cuts reverse. Q1's 39.5% and Q2's 20.4% carry no refund, so the Q3 improvement is entirely the refund: ex-refund, Q3 is below Q2 [S8, S9, S117].

| Energy segment, $M unless stated | Q1 2026 | Q2 2026 | Q3 2026 | 9M 2026 | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Revenue | 2,408 | 3,139 | 2,881 | 8,428 | S9 |
| Gross profit as reported | 952 | 640 | 954 | 2,546 | S9 |
| Gross margin as reported | 39.5% | 20.4% | 33.1% | 30.2% | S9 |
| IEEPA refund to cost of revenue | — | — | 526 | 526 | S8 |
| Gross profit ex-refund | 952 | 640 | 428 | 2,020 | derived |
| Gross margin ex-refund | 39.5% | 20.4% | 14.8% | 24.0% | derived |

| Storage benchmark | Gross margin | Period | Basis | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Tesla energy | 33.1% / 14.8% | Q3 2026 | as reported / ex-IEEPA refund | S8, S9 |
| Fluence | 13.1%; 5.1% | FY2025; June 2026 quarter | as reported | S174, S61 |
| Sungrow storage | 36.49% | FY2025 | as reported | S176 |
| CATL storage batteries | 23.96% | H1 2026 | as reported | S177 |

At 14.8%, Tesla is near Fluence's 13.1% fiscal-year margin, not six times Fluence's worst quarter — the 5.1% June 2026 print carried liquidated damages and cost overruns. Sungrow's storage business earned 36.49% in FY2025 and CATL's storage batteries 23.96% in H1 2026; a vertically integrated Megapack should sit between the integrator and the cell maker, which is where 14.8-24.0% puts it, not at a structural premium. Revenue per kWh fell to $210 in Q3 2026 from $274 in Q1 2026, and ex-refund gross profit per kWh was $31 against $70 reported, so the segment is price- and volume-sensitive, not a fixed 30% annuity.

### Services is the quiet second engine, and robotaxi is the unpriced one

Services and other grew revenue 33% to $4,605M and gross profit to a record $734M, 15.9%, from 14.1% in Q2 2026 and 10.5% a year earlier; used vehicles, collision, maintenance and Supercharging are the lines, and Rivian's software and services segment earned 42% on $605M, so Tesla's margin is below the best comparable on 7.6 times the revenue. Robotaxi is the largest unpriced unit economic in the case: Tesla reports nearly two million cumulative unsupervised miles, a 1,051-vehicle authorised Texas fleet and a Cybercab launch, but no revenue, no paid trips and no cost per paid mile. Insurance, remote supervision, vehicle depreciation, charging and maintenance are the cost lines; each is undisclosed. If total cost is 60% of the fare, a 2x cost per mile turns a 40% contribution margin into -20%; if cost is 50%, 2x leaves zero. A revenue line with positive contribution is the fact that would move the valuation; without it the 15% autonomy branch of the bull case rests on miles, not money [S9, S120, S153].

### What breaks even, and what cannot be measured

| Line of business | Pricing metric | Price per unit | Period | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Vehicles | per vehicle delivered, blended across models | $42,259 revenue, $34,436 cost | Q3 2026 | S9 |
| Regulatory credits | per credit sold to another automaker | not disclosed; $113M net of a $475M reversal | Q3 2026 | S8 |
| Energy storage | per kWh deployed, Megapack and Powerwall blended | $210/kWh revenue, $70/kWh gross profit | Q3 2026 | S9 |
| FSD (Supervised) | per vehicle per month | $99 | 2026-10 | S121 |
| Megapack to SpaceX | per project, milestone billed | not disclosed; $626M of revenue | 9M 2026 | S8 |
| Vehicle leasing | per vehicle per month | not disclosed; $353M leasing revenue | Q3 2026 | S8 |
| Robotaxi and Cybercab | per ride | not disclosed | Q3 2026 | S9 |

At Q3 2026 unit economics, the automotive line covers its share of group cost only at 629,000 deliveries a quarter excluding credits (611,000 including them), 29% above the 486,532 delivered. Tesla discloses no customer-acquisition cost — there is no marketing line in the statements — so SG&A at 7.2% of revenue is the nearest proxy and a CAC payback or LTV:CAC ratio cannot be computed from the filings; the claim that Tesla acquires buyers more cheaply than Ford or GM is therefore untested. Judged on operating margin, Tesla's 2.6% sits below GM's 8.2% EBIT-adjusted and Ford's 5.5%, while its 18.1% ex-credit gross margin is level with BYD's 18%: the difference is the operating cost line, not the car. The diligence question is what FSD subscription revenue and Megapack-only margin actually are, because those two numbers decide whether the group earns more than its cost of capital [S115, S116, S119].

One buyer can pay $1,580.4bn, and since 2026-06-12 it has been listed. SpaceX, ticker SPCX on Nasdaq, quoted $147.79 for a $2.01tn market value on 2026-10-20, against Tesla at $373.71 and $1.48tn. At the 20-35% premium RBC Capital Markets and JPMorgan expect, a share-for-share combination values Tesla at $480-540 a share, 20-35% above the $399.81 close on 2026-10-30. The 12-month exit is therefore two-sided: a sale into a 103x multiple, and a minority-probability bid that pays a premium in another listed stock. On the report's single distribution — a 30% bull split evenly between autonomy proof and the combination, a 40% base at $266, a 22% bear at $156 and an 8% full de-rating at $82 — the expected 12-month return is -25.2%, and the live bid is worth about nine points of it [S154, S156, S8, S9].

|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Market sale | NasdaqGS, $13.8bn traded a day | the only certain route; 20-day average 36.30m shares | any session | certain | S11 |
| Share-for-share combination | SpaceX (Nasdaq: SPCX), $2.01tn on 2026-10-20 | listed currency; a 20-35% broker premium implies $480-540 a share | no terms; no merger vote at the 2026-12-03 meeting | 15% weight in the 12-month distribution; 18% on the prediction market by 2026-12-31 | S154, S156, S158, S159 |
| Re-rating to the first award gate | public market, $2,000bn capitalisation | the first 2025 award tranche crystallises at $506.05 a share | 12-36 months | 15% weight, the other half of the 30% bull case | S10, S127 |
| Trade sale | General Motors, Ford, Rivian, BYD | the three US peers are worth $137.0bn together, 8.7% of Tesla | none | very low | S15, S17, S19 |
| Capital return | Tesla's board | no dividend ever declared, no repurchase programme disclosed | none | very low | S1 |
| Separation of robotaxi or energy | not disclosed | no filed plan, no registration statement | none | not disclosed | S1 |

The acquirer arithmetic has changed; the carmakers' indifference has not. General Motors at $73.7bn, Ford at $45.7bn and Rivian at $17.6bn are worth $137.0bn between them, 8.7% of Tesla, and BYD earns 21.2x trailing, so none can finance $1.58tn at any premium. SpaceX can because its paper is the currency: Q3 2026 revenue of $14.58bn, up 161% with $7.56bn from AI, and capital expenditure of $19.6bn in the quarter against a $35-40bn guide for the fourth, give it the scale and the growth to issue shares. No cash has to be found, which is why the binding constraint is governance rather than financing [S15, S17, S19, S156].

At parity Tesla holders would own 42-43% of the combined company and 47-50% with the premium. Musk holds 20% of Tesla's voting power against 85% at SpaceX and would hold 57-58% of the combined votes, so a Tesla holder would exchange economic ownership for a minority stake in a controlled company. Approval is the harder gate: Musk has said Tesla needs a majority of all shares outstanding rather than of votes cast, so abstentions count against the deal, and the 2026-12-03 annual meeting carries three proposals, the director elections, say-on-pay and auditor ratification, with no merger on the ballot. The structures under study, SpaceX buying Tesla or a new holding company owning both, are at committee stage with advisers and no exchange ratio, and the 2016 SolarCity acquisition is the reference for how a related-party deal of this kind is litigated [S154, S156, S159].

| Transaction | Year | Value | Multiple | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| SpaceX IPO and current mark (SPCX) | 2026 | $135 a share at the 2026-06-12 IPO; $147.79 and $2.01tn on 2026-10-20 | 143x annualised Q2 2026 adjusted EBITDA of $3.5bn | S154, S157 |
| Waymo funding round | 2026 | $126bn post-money | not disclosed; 11.3x below Tesla's implied autonomy value of $1,420-1,441bn | S130 |
| Tesla initial public offering | 2010 | $1.13 a share, split-adjusted | not disclosed | S1 |
| First 2025 award tranche | 2025 design | $2,000bn capitalisation | 80x adjusted EBITDA at the $4.0tn step | S127 |

SpaceX's own mark is the comparison that matters, and it cuts both ways. At $2.01tn on $3.5bn of Q2 2026 adjusted EBITDA, or $14bn annualised, SPCX trades at 143x, above Tesla's 103x. That is what makes a share exchange feasible: the premium is paid in the most expensive listed currency available. It is not a de-risking. A Tesla holder who accepts a 35% premium would own half of a company at 120-140x EBITDA with negative free cash flow after $19.6bn of quarterly capital expenditure, and would have converted one crowded multiple into another. The branch is real and priced; it is not cash [S154, S157].

Announcement truncates the left tail because the stock trades toward the exchange ratio, and caps the right tail at deal value unless a competing bid appears. arguments.markdown:
Tesla sells cars, storage and services, and the returns are lower and more borrowed than the headlines suggest: the car earned an 18.1% ex-credit gross margin in Q3 2026, short of group research and selling cost; storage's 33.1% falls to 14.8% without the $526M IEEPA tariff refund; and interest income supplied 46.5% of pre-tax profit. The return is earned on a mixed gross-profit pool and cash pile, not a structurally superior unit economic model [S8, S9].

### Three segments, three ways of getting paid

The automotive segment took 73.3% of third-quarter 2026 revenue ($20,560M of $28,046M), services and other 16.4% ($4,605M) and energy generation and storage 10.3% ($2,881M). The buyer differs in each: a retail or fleet customer pays cash or finances a car at transfer of control; an energy customer — a utility, developer or data-centre operator — pays on project milestones across quarters; a service customer pays per transaction for repair, maintenance or charging; another automaker pays for regulatory credits at transfer of title. The mix has moved: energy was 6.2% of FY2023 revenue ($6,035M) and 13.5% in FY2025 ($12,771M), while automotive revenue fell from $82,419M to $69,526M. The recurring software charge is FSD (Supervised) at $99 a month, with 1.74 million active subscriptions at 2026-09-30 [S8, S1, S121].

### The vehicle does not pay for the research budget

| Per unit (one vehicle delivered), Q3 2026 | USD per unit | Note | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| Automotive revenue | 42,259 | $20,560M ÷ 486,532 deliveries | S9 |
| Cost of automotive revenue | (34,436) | materials, labour, overhead, warranty, tariffs | S8 |
| Automotive gross profit | 7,823 | 18.5% margin | S8 |
| Regulatory credits inside that profit | 232 | $113M ÷ 486,532; no matching cost | S8 |
| Automotive gross profit excluding credits | 7,590 | 18.1% of $20,447M ex-credit revenue | S8 |
| Group R&D and SG&A per unit | (9,817) | $4,776M ÷ 486,532, all charged to the car | S9 |
| Automotive-only operating contribution | (1,994) | a loss before energy and services | derived |
| Energy and services gross profit per unit | 3,470 | $1,688M ÷ 486,532 | S8 |
| Group operating profit per unit | 1,476 | $718M ÷ 486,532 | S9 |
| Interest income per unit | 915 | $445M ÷ 486,532 | S8 |
| Pre-tax profit per unit | 1,965 | $956M ÷ 486,532 | S8 |

A delivered car carried $42,259 of automotive revenue and $34,436 of cost, leaving $7,823 of gross profit, $7,590 excluding credits; spreading $4,776M of group research and development and selling cost over 486,532 deliveries costs $9,817 a vehicle, so the automotive line alone runs at -$1,994 a vehicle. Energy and services add $3,470 a vehicle, turning it into $1,476 of operating profit and $1,965 of pre-tax profit with interest income. Cost per vehicle was $33,666 in Q4 2025 and $34,436 in Q3 2026, so unit cost is not falling; the rise in ex-credit margin from 15.4% to 18.1% came with a richer Asia-Pacific mix, not from the factory [S9, S8].

::: evidence
**The reported credit collapse is a clawback of past revenue, not yet a collapse in current demand — but the contracted backlog says it is coming.**

Reported credit revenue fell from $542M in Q4 2025 to $380M in Q1 2026, $146M in Q2 2026 and $113M in Q3 2026, after $1,993M in FY2025. The Q3 figure is net of a $475M reversal of previously recognised credits for contractual returns, so gross sales were about $588M, higher than Q4 2025. The forward indicator is worse: contracted obligations with original terms over one year fell to $384M at 2026-09-30 from $841M at 2025-12-31. Toyota and Stellantis left Tesla's European CO2 pool for 2026; Tesla names no credit buyer [S8, S83, S1, S123].
:::

### Storage's 33% is a tariff refund, not a run-rate

Energy reported $954M of gross profit on $2,881M of revenue in Q3 2026, 33.1%, after 20.4% in Q2 2026. The 10-Q note says Tesla recognised $526M of IEEPA tariff refunds as a reduction to energy cost of revenue and $339M as a reduction to energy revenue for refunds owed to customers; first-half amounts were immaterial. Removing the $526M cost credit leaves $428M, or 14.8%, with the $339M customer pass-through still depressing revenue. The earnings call also cited warranty true-ups, but no filing quantifies that piece, so the $526M cannot be split and 14.8% is the conservative ex-refund figure; adding the $339M back as well would give 23.8%, but that assumes the customer price cuts reverse. Q1's 39.5% and Q2's 20.4% carry no refund, so the Q3 improvement is entirely the refund: ex-refund, Q3 is below Q2 [S8, S9, S117].

| Energy segment, $M unless stated | Q1 2026 | Q2 2026 | Q3 2026 | 9M 2026 | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Revenue | 2,408 | 3,139 | 2,881 | 8,428 | S9 |
| Gross profit as reported | 952 | 640 | 954 | 2,546 | S9 |
| Gross margin as reported | 39.5% | 20.4% | 33.1% | 30.2% | S9 |
| IEEPA refund to cost of revenue | — | — | 526 | 526 | S8 |
| Gross profit ex-refund | 952 | 640 | 428 | 2,020 | S8, S9 (derived) |
| Gross margin ex-refund | 39.5% | 20.4% | 14.8% | 24.0% | S8, S9 (derived) |

| Storage benchmark | Gross margin | Period | Basis | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Tesla energy | 33.1% / 14.8% | Q3 2026 | as reported / ex-IEEPA refund | S8, S9 |
| Fluence | 13.1%; 5.1% | FY2025; June 2026 quarter | as reported | S174, S61 |
| Sungrow storage | 36.49% | FY2025 | as reported | S176 |
| CATL storage batteries | 23.96% | H1 2026 | as reported | S177 |

At 14.8%, Tesla is near Fluence's 13.1% fiscal-year margin, not six times Fluence's 5.1% June 2026 quarter, which carried liquidated damages and cost overruns. Sungrow's storage business earned 36.49% in FY2025 and CATL's storage batteries 23.96% in H1 2026; a vertically integrated Megapack should sit between the integrator and the cell maker, not at a structural premium. Revenue per kWh fell to $210 in Q3 2026 from $274 in Q1, and ex-refund gross profit per kWh was $31 against $70 reported. The counter-case is that Q2 2026's 20.4% needed no refund, Megapack is nearly sold out through 2027, services earned a record 15.9% and the ex-credit automotive margin rose to 18.1%; if those hold, 14.8% is a trough, not a run-rate [S8, S9, S117].

### Services is the quiet second engine, and robotaxi is the unpriced one

Services and other grew revenue 33% to $4,605M and gross profit to a record $734M, 15.9%, from 14.1% in Q2 2026 and 10.5% a year earlier; used vehicles, collision, maintenance and Supercharging are the lines, and Rivian's software and services segment earned 42% on $605M, so Tesla's margin is below the best comparable on 7.6 times the revenue. Robotaxi is the largest unpriced unit economic in the case: Tesla reports nearly two million cumulative unsupervised miles, a 1,051-vehicle authorised Texas fleet and a Cybercab launch, but no revenue, no paid trips and no cost per paid mile. Insurance, remote supervision, vehicle depreciation, charging and maintenance are the cost lines; each is undisclosed. If total cost is 60% of the fare, a 2x cost per mile turns a 40% contribution margin into -20%; if cost is 50%, 2x leaves zero. A revenue line with positive contribution is the fact that would move the valuation; without it the 15% autonomy branch of the bull case rests on miles, not money [S9, S120, S153].

### What breaks even, and what cannot be measured

| Line of business | Pricing metric | Price per unit | Period | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Vehicles | per vehicle delivered, blended across models | $42,259 revenue, $34,436 cost | Q3 2026 | S9 |
| Regulatory credits | per credit sold to another automaker | not disclosed; $113M net of a $475M reversal | Q3 2026 | S8 |
| Energy storage | per kWh deployed, Megapack and Powerwall blended | $210/kWh revenue, $70/kWh gross profit | Q3 2026 | S9 |
| FSD (Supervised) | per vehicle per month | $99 | 2026-10 | S121 |
| Megapack to SpaceX | per project, milestone billed | not disclosed; $626M of revenue | 9M 2026 | S8 |
| Vehicle leasing | per vehicle per month | not disclosed; $353M leasing revenue | Q3 2026 | S8 |
| Robotaxi and Cybercab | per ride | not disclosed | Q3 2026 | S9 |

At Q3 2026 unit economics, the automotive line covers its share of group cost only at 629,000 deliveries a quarter excluding credits (611,000 including them), 29% above the 486,532 delivered. Tesla discloses no customer-acquisition cost — there is no marketing line in the statements — so SG&A at 7.2% of revenue is the nearest proxy and CAC payback and LTV:CAC cannot be computed from the filings; the claim that Tesla acquires buyers more cheaply than Ford or GM is therefore untested. Judged on operating margin, Tesla's 2.6% sits below GM's 8.2% EBIT-adjusted and Ford's 5.5%, while its 18.1% ex-credit gross margin is level with BYD's 18%: the difference is the operating cost line, not the car. The diligence question is what FSD subscription revenue and Megapack-only margin actually are, because those two numbers decide whether the group earns more than its cost of capital [S115, S116, S119].

### The safety file is the binding constraint

NHTSA's Office of Defects Investigation opened Engineering Analysis EA26002 on 18 March 2026 into whether FSD detects degraded visibility — glare, fog, dust — and warns the driver in time, covering an estimated 3,203,754 vehicles from model years 2016-2026, after nine confirmed incidents including one pedestrian fatality; two further FSD probes remain open, one on traffic-law violations across 2,882,566 vehicles with 80 incidents. arguments.markdown:
Tesla sells cars, storage and services, and the returns are lower and more borrowed than the headlines suggest: the car earned an 18.1% ex-credit gross margin in Q3 2026, short of group research and selling cost; storage's 33.1% falls to 14.8% without the $526M IEEPA tariff refund; and interest income supplied 46.5% of pre-tax profit. The return is earned on a mixed gross-profit pool and cash pile, not a structurally superior unit economic model [S8, S9].

### Three segments, three ways of getting paid

The automotive segment took 73.3% of third-quarter 2026 revenue ($20,560M of $28,046M), services and other 16.4% ($4,605M) and energy generation and storage 10.3% ($2,881M). The buyer differs in each: a retail or fleet customer pays cash or finances a car at transfer of control; an energy customer — a utility, developer or data-centre operator — pays on project milestones across quarters; a service customer pays per transaction for repair, maintenance or charging; another automaker pays for regulatory credits at transfer of title. The mix has moved: energy was 6.2% of FY2023 revenue ($6,035M) and 13.5% in FY2025 ($12,771M), while automotive revenue fell from $82,419M to $69,526M. The recurring software charge is FSD (Supervised) at $99 a month, with 1.74 million active subscriptions at 2026-09-30 [S8, S1, S121].

### The vehicle does not pay for the research budget

| Per unit (one vehicle delivered), Q3 2026 | USD per unit | Note | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| Automotive revenue | 42,259 | $20,560M ÷ 486,532 deliveries | S9 |
| Cost of automotive revenue | (34,436) | materials, labour, overhead, warranty, tariffs | S8 |
| Automotive gross profit | 7,823 | 18.5% margin | S8 |
| Regulatory credits inside that profit | 232 | $113M ÷ 486,532; no matching cost | S8 |
| Automotive gross profit excluding credits | 7,590 | 18.1% of $20,447M ex-credit revenue | S8 |
| Group R&D and SG&A per unit | (9,817) | $4,776M ÷ 486,532, all charged to the car | S9 |
| Automotive-only operating contribution | (1,994) | a loss before energy and services | derived |
| Energy and services gross profit per unit | 3,470 | $1,688M ÷ 486,532 | S8 |
| Group operating profit per unit | 1,476 | $718M ÷ 486,532 | S9 |
| Interest income per unit | 915 | $445M ÷ 486,532 | S8 |
| Pre-tax profit per unit | 1,965 | $956M ÷ 486,532 | S8 |

A delivered car carried $42,259 of automotive revenue and $34,436 of cost, leaving $7,823 of gross profit, $7,590 excluding credits; spreading $4,776M of group research and development and selling cost over 486,532 deliveries costs $9,817 a vehicle, so the automotive line alone runs at -$1,994 a vehicle. Energy and services add $3,470 a vehicle, turning it into $1,476 of operating profit and $1,965 of pre-tax profit with interest income. Cost per vehicle was $33,666 in Q4 2025 and $34,436 in Q3 2026, so unit cost is not falling; the rise in ex-credit margin from 15.4% to 18.1% came with a richer Asia-Pacific mix, not from the factory [S9, S8].

::: evidence
**The reported credit collapse is a clawback of past revenue, not yet a collapse in current demand — but the contracted backlog says it is coming.**

Reported credit revenue fell from $542M in Q4 2025 to $380M in Q1 2026, $146M in Q2 2026 and $113M in Q3 2026, after $1,993M in FY2025. The Q3 figure is net of a $475M reversal of previously recognised credits for contractual returns, so gross sales were $588M, higher than Q4 2025. The forward indicator is worse: contracted obligations with original terms over one year fell to $384M at 2026-09-30 from $841M at 2025-12-31. Toyota and Stellantis left Tesla's European CO2 pool for 2026; Tesla names no credit buyer [S8, S83, S1, S123].
:::

### Storage's 33% is a tariff refund, not a run-rate

Energy reported $954M of gross profit on $2,881M of revenue in Q3 2026, 33.1%, after 20.4% in Q2 2026. The 10-Q note says Tesla recognised $526M of IEEPA tariff refunds as a reduction to energy cost of revenue and $339M as a reduction to energy revenue for refunds owed to customers; first-half amounts were immaterial. Removing the $526M cost credit leaves $428M, or 14.8%, with the $339M customer pass-through still depressing revenue. The earnings call also cited warranty true-ups, but no filing quantifies that piece, so the $526M cannot be split and 14.8% is the conservative ex-refund figure; adding the $339M back as well would give 23.8%, but that assumes the customer price cuts reverse. Q1's 39.5% and Q2's 20.4% carry no refund, so the Q3 improvement is entirely the refund: ex-refund, Q3 is below Q2 [S8, S9, S117].

| Energy segment, $M unless stated | Q1 2026 | Q2 2026 | Q3 2026 | 9M 2026 | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Revenue | 2,408 | 3,139 | 2,881 | 8,428 | S9 |
| Gross profit as reported | 952 | 640 | 954 | 2,546 | S9 |
| Gross margin as reported | 39.5% | 20.4% | 33.1% | 30.2% | S9 |
| IEEPA refund to cost of revenue | — | — | 526 | 526 | S8 |
| Gross profit ex-refund | 952 | 640 | 428 | 2,020 | S8, S9 (derived) |
| Gross margin ex-refund | 39.5% | 20.4% | 14.8% | 24.0% | S8, S9 (derived) |

| Storage benchmark | Gross margin | Period | Basis | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Tesla energy | 33.1% / 14.8% | Q3 2026 | as reported / ex-IEEPA refund | S8, S9 |
| Fluence | 13.1%; 5.1% | FY2025; June 2026 quarter | as reported | S174, S61 |
| Sungrow storage | 36.49% | FY2025 | as reported | S176 |
| CATL storage batteries | 23.96% | H1 2026 | as reported | S177 |

At 14.8%, Tesla is near Fluence's 13.1% fiscal-year margin, not six times Fluence's 5.1% June 2026 quarter, which carried liquidated damages and cost overruns. Sungrow's storage business earned 36.49% in FY2025 and CATL's storage batteries 23.96% in H1 2026; a vertically integrated Megapack should sit between the integrator and the cell maker, not at a structural premium. Revenue per kWh fell to $210 in Q3 2026 from $274 in Q1, and ex-refund gross profit per kWh was $31 against $70 reported. The counter-case is that Q2 2026's 20.4% needed no refund, Megapack is nearly sold out through 2027, services earned a record 15.9% and the ex-credit automotive margin rose to 18.1%; if those hold, 14.8% is a trough, not a run-rate [S8, S9, S117].

### Services is the quiet second engine, and robotaxi is the unpriced one

Services and other grew revenue 33% to $4,605M and gross profit to a record $734M, 15.9%, from 14.1% in Q2 2026 and 10.5% a year earlier; used vehicles, collision, maintenance and Supercharging are the lines, and Rivian's software and services segment earned 42% on $605M, so Tesla's margin is below the best comparable on 7.6 times the revenue. Robotaxi is the largest unpriced unit economic in the case: Tesla reports nearly two million cumulative unsupervised miles, a 1,051-vehicle authorised Texas fleet and a Cybercab launch, but no revenue, no paid trips and no cost per paid mile. Insurance, remote supervision, vehicle depreciation, charging and maintenance are the cost lines; each is undisclosed. If total cost is 60% of the fare, a 2x cost per mile turns a 40% contribution margin into -20%; if cost is 50%, 2x leaves zero. A revenue line with positive contribution is the fact that would move the valuation; without it the 15% autonomy branch of the bull case rests on miles, not money [S9, S120, S153].

### What breaks even, and what cannot be measured

| Line of business | Pricing metric | Price per unit | Period | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Vehicles | per vehicle delivered, blended across models | $42,259 revenue, $34,436 cost | Q3 2026 | S9 |
| Regulatory credits | per credit sold to another automaker | not disclosed; $113M net of a $475M reversal | Q3 2026 | S8 |
| Energy storage | per kWh deployed, Megapack and Powerwall blended | $210/kWh revenue, $70/kWh gross profit | Q3 2026 | S9 |
| FSD (Supervised) | per vehicle per month | $99 | 2026-10 | S121 |
| Megapack to SpaceX | per project, milestone billed | not disclosed; $626M of revenue | 9M 2026 | S8 |
| Robotaxi and Cybercab | per ride | not disclosed | Q3 2026 | S9 |

At Q3 2026 unit economics, the automotive line covers its share of group cost only at 629,000 deliveries a quarter excluding credits (611,000 including them), 29% above the 486,532 delivered. Tesla discloses no customer-acquisition cost — there is no marketing line in the statements — so SG&A at 7.2% of revenue is the nearest proxy and CAC payback and LTV:CAC cannot be computed from the filings; the claim that Tesla acquires buyers more cheaply than Ford or GM is therefore untested. Judged on operating margin, Tesla's 2.6% sits below GM's 8.2% EBIT-adjusted and Ford's 5.5%, while its 18.1% ex-credit gross margin is level with BYD's 18%: the difference is the operating cost line, not the car. The diligence question is what FSD subscription revenue and Megapack-only margin actually are, because those two numbers decide whether the group earns more than its cost of capital [S115, S116, S119].

arguments.markdown:
Tesla sells cars, storage and services, and the returns are lower and more borrowed than the headlines suggest: the car earned an 18.1% ex-credit gross margin in Q3 2026, short of group research and selling cost; storage's 33.1% falls to 14.8% without the $526M IEEPA tariff refund; and interest income supplied 46.5% of pre-tax profit. The return is earned on a mixed gross-profit pool and cash pile, not a structurally superior unit economic model. The automotive segment took 73.3% of third-quarter 2026 revenue ($20,560M of $28,046M), services and other 16.4% ($4,605M) and energy generation and storage 10.3% ($2,881M). The buyer differs in each: a retail or fleet customer pays cash or finances a car at transfer of control; an energy customer — a utility, developer or data-centre operator — pays on project milestones across quarters; a service customer pays per transaction for repair, maintenance or charging; another automaker pays for regulatory credits at transfer of title. Energy was 6.2% of FY2023 revenue ($6,035M) and 13.5% in FY2025 ($12,771M), while automotive revenue fell from $82,419M to $69,526M; the recurring software charge is FSD (Supervised) at $99 a month, with 1.74 million active subscriptions at 2026-09-30 [S8, S9, S1, S121].

### The vehicle does not pay for the research budget

| Per unit (one vehicle delivered), Q3 2026 | USD per unit | Note | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| Automotive revenue | 42,259 | $20,560M ÷ 486,532 deliveries | S9 |
| Cost of automotive revenue | (34,436) | materials, labour, overhead, warranty, tariffs | S8 |
| Automotive gross profit | 7,823 | 18.5% margin | S8 |
| Regulatory credits inside that profit | 232 | $113M ÷ 486,532; no matching cost | S8 |
| Automotive gross profit excluding credits | 7,590 | 18.1% of $20,447M ex-credit revenue | S8 |
| Group R&D and SG&A per unit | (9,817) | $4,776M ÷ 486,532, all charged to the car | S9 |
| Automotive-only operating contribution | (1,994) | a loss before energy and services | derived |
| Energy and services gross profit per unit | 3,470 | $1,688M ÷ 486,532 | S8 |
| Group operating profit per unit | 1,476 | $718M ÷ 486,532 | S9 |
| Interest income per unit | 915 | $445M ÷ 486,532 | S8 |
| Pre-tax profit per unit | 1,965 | $956M ÷ 486,532 | S8 |

A delivered car carried $42,259 of automotive revenue and $34,436 of cost, leaving $7,823 of gross profit, $7,590 excluding credits; spreading $4,776M of group research and development and selling cost over 486,532 deliveries costs $9,817 a vehicle, so the automotive line alone runs at -$1,994 a vehicle. Energy and services add $3,470 a vehicle, turning it into $1,476 of operating profit and $1,965 of pre-tax profit with interest income. Cost per vehicle was $33,666 in Q4 2025 and $34,436 in Q3 2026, so unit cost is not falling; the rise in ex-credit margin from 15.4% to 18.1% came with a richer Asia-Pacific mix, not from the factory [S9, S8].

::: evidence
**The reported credit collapse is a clawback of past revenue, not yet a collapse in current demand — but the contracted backlog says it is coming.**

Reported credit revenue fell from $542M in Q4 2025 to $380M in Q1 2026, $146M in Q2 2026 and $113M in Q3 2026, after $1,993M in FY2025. The Q3 figure is net of a $475M reversal of previously recognised credits for contractual returns, so gross sales were $588M, higher than Q4 2025. The forward indicator is worse: contracted obligations with original terms over one year fell to $384M at 2026-09-30 from $841M at 2025-12-31. Toyota and Stellantis left Tesla's European CO2 pool for 2026; Tesla names no credit buyer [S8, S83, S1, S123].
:::

### Storage's 33% is a tariff refund, not a run-rate

Energy reported $954M of gross profit on $2,881M of revenue in Q3 2026, 33.1%, after 20.4% in Q2 2026. The 10-Q note says Tesla recognised $526M of IEEPA tariff refunds as a reduction to energy cost of revenue and $339M as a reduction to energy revenue for refunds owed to customers; first-half amounts were immaterial. Removing the $526M cost credit leaves $428M, or 14.8%, with the $339M customer pass-through still depressing revenue. The earnings call also cited warranty true-ups, but no filing quantifies that piece, so the $526M cannot be split and 14.8% is the conservative ex-refund figure; adding the $339M back as well would give 23.8%, but that assumes the customer price cuts reverse. Q1's 39.5% and Q2's 20.4% carry no refund, so the Q3 improvement is entirely the refund: ex-refund, Q3 is below Q2. At 14.8%, Tesla is near Fluence's 13.1% fiscal-year margin, not six times Fluence's 5.1% June 2026 quarter, which carried liquidated damages and cost overruns; Sungrow's storage business earned 36.49% in FY2025 and CATL's storage batteries 23.96% in H1 2026, so a vertically integrated Megapack sits between the integrator and the cell maker, not at a structural premium. Revenue per kWh fell to $210 in Q3 2026 from $274 in Q1, and ex-refund gross profit per kWh was $31 against $70 reported. The counter-case is that Q2 2026's 20.4% needed no refund, Megapack is nearly sold out through 2027, services earned a record 15.9% and the ex-credit automotive margin rose to 18.1%; if those hold, 14.8% is a trough, not a run-rate [S8, S9, S117].

|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Revenue | 2,408 | 3,139 | 2,881 | 8,428 | S9 |
| Gross profit as reported | 952 | 640 | 954 | 2,546 | S9 |
| Gross margin as reported | 39.5% | 20.4% | 33.1% | 30.2% | S9 |
| IEEPA refund to cost of revenue | — | — | 526 | 526 | S8 |
| Gross profit ex-refund | 952 | 640 | 428 | 2,020 | S8, S9 (derived) |
| Gross margin ex-refund | 39.5% | 20.4% | 14.8% | 24.0% | S8, S9 (derived) |

| Storage benchmark | Gross margin | Period | Basis | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Tesla energy | 33.1% / 14.8% | Q3 2026 | as reported / ex-IEEPA refund | S8, S9 |
| Fluence | 13.1%; 5.1% | FY2025; June 2026 quarter | as reported | S174, S61 |
| Sungrow storage | 36.49% | FY2025 | as reported | S176 |
| CATL storage batteries | 23.96% | H1 2026 | as reported | S177 |

### Services is the quiet second engine, and robotaxi is the unpriced one

Services and other grew revenue 33% to $4,605M and gross profit to a record $734M, 15.9%, from 14.1% in Q2 2026 and 10.5% a year earlier; used vehicles, collision, maintenance and Supercharging are the lines, and Rivian's software and services segment earned 42% on $605M, so Tesla's margin is below the best comparable on 7.6 times the revenue. Robotaxi is the largest unpriced unit economic in the case: Tesla reports nearly two million cumulative unsupervised miles, a 1,051-vehicle authorised Texas fleet and a Cybercab launch, but no revenue, no paid trips and no cost per paid mile. Insurance, remote supervision, vehicle depreciation, charging and maintenance are the cost lines; each is undisclosed. If total cost is 60% of the fare, a 2x cost per mile turns a 40% contribution margin into -20%; if cost is 50%, 2x leaves zero. A revenue line with positive contribution is the fact that would move the valuation; without it the 15% autonomy branch of the bull case rests on miles, not money [S9, S120, S153].

### What breaks even, and what cannot be measured

| Line of business | Pricing metric | Price per unit | Period | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Vehicles | per vehicle delivered, blended across models | $42,259 revenue, $34,436 cost | Q3 2026 | S9 |
| Regulatory credits | per credit sold to another automaker | not disclosed; $113M net of a $475M reversal | Q3 2026 | S8 |
| Energy storage | per kWh deployed, Megapack and Powerwall blended | $210/kWh revenue, $70/kWh gross profit | Q3 2026 | S9 |
| FSD (Supervised) | per vehicle per month | $99 | 2026-10 | S121 |
| Megapack to SpaceX | per project, milestone billed | not disclosed; $626M of revenue | 9M 2026 | S8 |
| Robotaxi and Cybercab | per ride | not disclosed | Q3 2026 | S9 |

At Q3 2026 unit economics, the automotive line covers its share of group cost only at 629,000 deliveries a quarter excluding credits (611,000 including them), 29% above the 486,532 delivered. Tesla discloses no customer-acquisition cost — there is no marketing line in the statements — so SG&A at 7.2% of revenue is the nearest proxy and CAC payback and LTV:CAC cannot be computed from the filings; the claim that Tesla acquires buyers more cheaply than Ford or GM is therefore untested. Judged on operating margin, Tesla's 2.6% sits below GM's 8.2% EBIT-adjusted and Ford's 5.5%, while its 18.1% ex-credit gross margin is level with BYD's 18%: the difference is the operating cost line, not the car. The diligence question is what FSD subscription revenue and Megapack-only margin actually are, because those two numbers decide whether the group earns more than its cost of capital [S115, S116, S119].

arguments.markdown:
Tesla's technology position in 2026 is two facts usually merged in the narrative: the largest supervised-driving data pool and one of the cheapest large-scale EV manufacturing bases in the industry, and almost no verified driverless revenue. Active FSD subscriptions reached 1.74 million at 30 September 2026 against 10.2 million vehicles delivered to date — 17.1% of the lifetime fleet — while cumulative unsupervised Robotaxi miles were "nearly two million", 0.9% of the 220.6 million rider-only miles Waymo had logged through March 2026. The 1.74 million is a company definition that includes upfront FSD purchases and monthly subscriptions and excludes free trials; management put about half the paid base on monthly plans on 21 October 2026, so roughly 870,000 are subscribers worth about $1.0bn a year at list and roughly 870,000 are one-time buyers. Partially verified: the count comes from the Q3 2026 shareholder update, the split from call commentary rather than a filed figure [S9, S151, S152, S173].

### What Tesla actually sells

| Product | Stage | Revenue or share | Next milestone | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| FSD (Supervised) | Commercial, 9 EU countries | 1.74m subscriptions; revenue not disclosed | Unsupervised release | S9, S1 |
| Robotaxi / Cybercab | Paid driverless in Texas | 1,051 vehicles authorised at 2026-10-27; revenue not disclosed | Paid-trip disclosure | S9, S125 |
| Model 3 / Model Y | Mature | 478,237 units, Q3 2026; 19.6% group gross margin | Next platform | S9 |
| Cybertruck, Semi, Roadster | Ramp / design | 8,295 other-model units, Q3 2026 | Semi ramp; Roadster launch | S9 |
| Megapack, Powerwall | Scaling | $2.881bn in Q3 2026; 13.7 GWh | 50 GWh Texas ramp | S9, S60 |
| Optimus | Internal production | Zero external revenue | External pilot sale | S9, S99 |

### Mechanism: end-to-end vision and a one-sided flywheel

Tesla removed radar and maps camera pixels directly to driving commands with an end-to-end neural network, trained on clips harvested from the fleet and run on in-house inference silicon. The flywheel is real but overwhelmingly *supervised*: the Q3 2026 update charts cumulative FSD miles on a 0-16 billion axis against 2.0 million unsupervised miles. Supervised miles teach perception; they do not certify that the network can be left alone, which is why the federal safety file matters more than the mileage chart [S60].

| Metric | Value | Method | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| Active FSD subscriptions | 1.74m (2026-09-30) | Company count | S9 |
| FSD penetration of fleet | 17.1% | 1.74m / 10.2m deliveries | S9 |
| FSD monthly subscribers | ~870,000 | Half the paid base, call 2026-10-21 | S152, S173 |
| FSD upfront buyers | ~870,000 | Remainder of the 1.74m | S152, S173 |
| FSD subscription run-rate | ~$1.0bn a year, unaudited | 870,000 × $99 × 12, US list | S121, S152 |
| Deferred revenue, connectivity/FSD/Supercharging/OTA | $4.08bn at 2026-09-30 | Company note; FSD not separable | S8 |
| Cumulative unsupervised Robotaxi miles | 2.0m, 8x QoQ | Company count | S9 |
| Installed AI training compute | 225+ MW | Company nameplate | S9 |
| 4680 capacity, Texas | 40+ GWh/yr, dry electrode both sides | Company nameplate | S60 |
| Storage deployed | 13.7 GWh Q3; 36.0 GWh 9M | Company deliveries | S9 |

### The safety file is the binding constraint

NHTSA's Office of Defects Investigation opened Engineering Analysis EA26002 on 18 March 2026 into whether FSD detects degraded visibility — glare, fog, dust — and warns the driver in time, covering an estimated 3,203,754 vehicles from model years 2016-2026, after nine confirmed incidents including one pedestrian fatality; two further FSD probes remain open, one on traffic-law violations across 2,882,566 vehicles with 80 incidents. Tesla's own analysis reportedly found its degradation-detection update "may have affected" only 3 of 9 incidents, which points to an architectural limit of camera-only sensing rather than a tuning defect. An engineering analysis is the last step before a recall, and a recall would narrow the operating domain or force hardware across millions of cars whose liability terms for paid driverless rides are not disclosed [S87, S88, S100].

::: evidence
**The camera-only bet is being tested by the regulator, not the market.** EA26002 covers 3.2 million FSD-equipped vehicles and Tesla's fix reportedly addresses a third of the reviewed incidents; the filings give no remedy or timetable. That is the largest un-priced technical risk in the autonomy option [S87, S88].
:::

### Comparison: four autonomy models, two assisted ones

| Operator | Sensing | Verified scale | Regulatory position | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Tesla | Camera-only, in-house inference silicon | 2.0m cumulative unsupervised miles; 1,051 vehicles authorised in Texas at 2026-10-27 | Paid driverless only in Texas under SB 2807; California testing permit with a safety driver | S9, S125, S89 |
| Waymo | Lidar, radar and camera | 220.6m rider-only miles to 2026-03; about 500,000 paid rides a week | California deployment authorised | S151 |
| Pony.ai, WeRide, Baidu | Lidar and camera | Pony: 1,776 vehicles built by 2026-05-24, $8.6m Q1 robotaxi revenue; WeRide: about 1,300 robotaxis globally at 2026-04-30; Baidu: 3.2m driverless rides in Q1 2026 | Zone-limited driverless permits in Chinese cities | S178 |
| Huawei, Momenta | Camera and lidar on OEM vehicles | More than 80% of China's urban NOA market | L2+/L3 consumer systems, driver liable | S168 |
| GM, Ford, comma.ai | Super Cruise and BlueCruise camera-radar; openpilot camera | Hands-off, eyes-on only; openpilot: five crashes, three deaths, federal probe opened 2026-09 | No driverless revenue | S170, S179 |

### Moat: accumulation, not exclusion

| Barrier | Difficulty (1-10) | Why | Time to replicate | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Supervised fleet data | 8 | 10.2m cars; FSD miles charted to 16bn | 4-6 years | S9 |
| Dry-electrode cell process | 7 | Battery Day 2020 to Austin output in 2026 | 3-4 years | S60 |
| Manufacturing and integration | 8 | 134,785 employees; cells, cathode and refining in-house | 5+ years | S1 |
| State permits | 6 | Bilateral and political; not purchasable | 1-3 years | S89, S91 |
| Composite | 6.5/10 | Minimum 3-year lead on a geofenced service | — | S9, S60 |

The replication test is unflattering to a patent story: 50 funded engineers with every published Tesla patent could build a geofenced driverless service in two to three years — Waymo needed eleven years from its 2009 start — but could not reproduce the fleet data or the factories. Tesla's 10-K concedes the point by design, pledging irrevocably not to sue any party acting in good faith for infringing its electric-vehicle patents. California is the harder gate: on 23 October 2026 the DMV lists Tesla Robotaxi LLC only as a testing-permit holder requiring a safety driver, and the state's regulator confirmed in March 2026 that Tesla is not operating an autonomous vehicle service, its paid rides running on a limousine permit [S1, S89, S90].

| IP instrument | Covers | Status | Relevance | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Patent non-assertion pledge | EV and related-equipment patents | Irrevocable for good-faith users | Removes patents as a barrier | S1 |
| Trade secrets, NDAs | Cell process, manufacturing know-how | In force | Protects dry-electrode yield | S1 |
| In-house inference silicon; Samsung foundry deal | AI4/AI5 design and fabrication | Austin fab equipment commissioning 2027 | Cost and performance control | S1, S9 |

Tesla publishes no patent count, so a patent-number-level table cannot be built from its disclosures; a USPTO assignee search would settle portfolio size and freedom-to-operate risk, and it has been requested.

### Robotaxi unit economics: the undisclosed half of the model

Insurance, teleoperation and depreciation per vehicle decide whether a paid mile contributes anything, and the filing discloses none of them. The disclosed pieces describe a small fleet with a modest revenue benchmark, not a network whose contribution can be modelled.

| Item | Disclosed? | Figure | What it means | Source |

arguments.markdown:
Tesla sells cars, storage and services, and the returns are lower than the headlines suggest: the car earned an 18.1% ex-credit gross margin in Q3 2026, short of group research and selling cost; storage's 33.1% falls to 14.8% without the $526M IEEPA tariff refund; and interest income supplied 46.5% of pre-tax profit. The return is earned on a mixed gross-profit pool and cash pile, not a structurally superior unit economic model. The automotive segment took 73.3% of third-quarter 2026 revenue ($20,560M of $28,046M), services and other 16.4% ($4,605M) and energy generation and storage 10.3% ($2,881M). The buyer differs in each: a retail or fleet customer pays cash or finances a car at transfer of control; an energy customer — a utility, developer or data-centre operator — pays on project milestones across quarters; a service customer pays per transaction for repair, maintenance or charging; another automaker pays for regulatory credits at transfer of title. Energy was 6.2% of FY2023 revenue ($6,035M) and 13.5% in FY2025 ($12,771M), while automotive revenue fell from $82,419M to $69,526M; the recurring software charge is FSD (Supervised) at $99 a month, with 1.74 million active subscriptions at 2026-09-30 [S8, S9, S1, S121].

### The vehicle does not pay for the research budget

| Per unit (one vehicle delivered), Q3 2026 | USD per unit | Note | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| Automotive revenue | 42,259 | $20,560M ÷ 486,532 deliveries | S9 |
| Cost of automotive revenue | (34,436) | materials, labour, overhead, warranty, tariffs | S8 |
| Automotive gross profit | 7,823 | 18.5% margin | S8 |
| Regulatory credits inside that profit | 232 | $113M ÷ 486,532; no matching cost | S8 |
| Automotive gross profit excluding credits | 7,590 | 18.1% of $20,447M ex-credit revenue | S8 |
| Group R&D and SG&A per unit | (9,817) | $4,776M ÷ 486,532, all charged to the car | S9 |
| Automotive-only operating contribution | (1,994) | a loss before energy and services | derived |
| Energy and services gross profit per unit | 3,470 | $1,688M ÷ 486,532 | S8 |
| Group operating profit per unit | 1,476 | $718M ÷ 486,532 | S9 |
| Interest income per unit | 915 | $445M ÷ 486,532 | S8 |
| Pre-tax profit per unit | 1,965 | $956M ÷ 486,532 | S8 |

A delivered car carried $42,259 of automotive revenue and $34,436 of cost, leaving $7,823 of gross profit, $7,590 excluding credits; spreading $4,776M of group research and development and selling cost over 486,532 deliveries costs $9,817 a vehicle, so the automotive line alone runs at -$1,994 a vehicle. Energy and services add $3,470 a vehicle, turning it into $1,476 of operating profit and $1,965 of pre-tax profit with interest income. Cost per vehicle was $33,666 in Q4 2025 and $34,436 in Q3 2026, so unit cost is not falling; the rise in ex-credit margin from 15.4% to 18.1% came with a richer Asia-Pacific mix, not from the factory [S9, S8].

::: evidence
**The reported credit collapse is a clawback of past revenue, not yet a collapse in current demand — but the contracted backlog says it is coming.**

Reported credit revenue fell from $542M in Q4 2025 to $380M in Q1 2026, $146M in Q2 2026 and $113M in Q3 2026, after $1,993M in FY2025. The Q3 figure is net of a $475M reversal of previously recognised credits for contractual returns, so gross sales were $588M, higher than Q4 2025. The forward indicator is worse: contracted obligations with original terms over one year fell to $384M at 2026-09-30 from $841M at 2025-12-31. Toyota and Stellantis left Tesla's European CO2 pool for 2026; Tesla names no credit buyer [S8, S83, S1, S123].
:::

### Storage's 33% is a tariff refund, not a run-rate

Energy reported $954M of gross profit on $2,881M of revenue in Q3 2026, 33.1%, after 20.4% in Q2 2026. The 10-Q note says Tesla recognised $526M of IEEPA tariff refunds as a reduction to energy cost of revenue and $339M as a reduction to energy revenue for refunds owed to customers; first-half amounts were immaterial. Removing the $526M cost credit leaves $428M, or 14.8%, with the $339M customer pass-through still depressing revenue. The earnings call also cited warranty true-ups, but no filing quantifies that piece, so the $526M cannot be split and 14.8% is the conservative ex-refund figure; adding the $339M back would give 23.8% only if the customer price cuts reverse. Q1's 39.5% and Q2's 20.4% carry no refund, so the Q3 improvement is entirely the refund: ex-refund, Q3 is below Q2. At 14.8%, Tesla is near Fluence's 13.1% fiscal-year margin, not six times Fluence's 5.1% June 2026 quarter. Sungrow's storage business earned 36.49% in FY2025 and CATL's storage batteries 23.96% in H1 2026, so a vertically integrated Megapack sits between the integrator and the cell maker, not at a structural premium. Revenue per kWh fell to $210 in Q3 2026 from $274 in Q1, and ex-refund gross profit per kWh was $31 against $70 reported. The counter-case is that Q2 2026's 20.4% needed no refund, Megapack is nearly sold out through 2027, services earned a record 15.9% and the ex-credit automotive margin rose to 18.1%; if those hold, 14.8% is a trough, not a run-rate [S8, S9, S117].

| Energy segment, $M unless stated | Q1 2026 | Q2 2026 | Q3 2026 | 9M 2026 | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Revenue | 2,408 | 3,139 | 2,881 | 8,428 | S9 |
| Gross profit as reported | 952 | 640 | 954 | 2,546 | S9 |
| Gross margin as reported | 39.5% | 20.4% | 33.1% | 30.2% | S9 |
| IEEPA refund to cost of revenue | — | — | 526 | 526 | S8 |
| Gross profit ex-refund | 952 | 640 | 428 | 2,020 | S8, S9 (derived) |
| Gross margin ex-refund | 39.5% | 20.4% | 14.8% | 24.0% | S8, S9 (derived) |

| Storage benchmark | Gross margin | Period | Basis | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Tesla energy | 33.1% / 14.8% | Q3 2026 | as reported / ex-IEEPA refund | S8, S9 |
| Fluence | 13.1%; 5.1% | FY2025; June 2026 quarter | as reported | S174, S61 |
| Sungrow storage | 36.49% | FY2025 | as reported | S176 |
| CATL storage batteries | 23.96% | H1 2026 | as reported | S177 |

### Services is the quiet second engine, and robotaxi is the unpriced one

Services and other grew revenue 33% to $4,605M and gross profit to a record $734M, 15.9%, from 14.1% in Q2 2026 and 10.5% a year earlier; Rivian's software and services segment earned 42% on $605M, so Tesla's margin is below the best comparable on 7.6 times the revenue. Robotaxi is the largest unpriced unit economic in the case: Tesla reports nearly two million cumulative unsupervised miles, a 1,051-vehicle authorised Texas fleet and a Cybercab launch, but no revenue, no paid trips and no cost per paid mile. Insurance, remote supervision, depreciation, charging and maintenance are undisclosed cost lines. If total cost is 60% of the fare, a 2x cost per mile turns a 40% contribution margin into -20%; if cost is 50%, 2x leaves zero. A positive-contribution revenue line is what would move the valuation; without it the 15% autonomy branch of the bull case rests on miles, not money [S9, S120, S153].

### What breaks even, and what cannot be measured

| Line of business | Pricing metric | Price per unit | Period | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Vehicles | per vehicle delivered, blended across models | $42,259 revenue, $34,436 cost | Q3 2026 | S9 |
| Regulatory credits | per credit sold to another automaker | not disclosed; $113M net of a $475M reversal | Q3 2026 | S8 |
| Energy storage | per kWh deployed, Megapack and Powerwall blended | $210/kWh revenue, $70/kWh gross profit | Q3 2026 | S9 |
| FSD (Supervised) | per vehicle per month | $99 | 2026-10 | S121 |
| Megapack to SpaceX | per project, milestone billed | not disclosed; $626M of revenue | 9M 2026 | S8 |
| Robotaxi and Cybercab | per ride | not disclosed | Q3 2026 | S9 |

At Q3 2026 unit economics, the automotive line covers its share of group cost only at 629,000 deliveries a quarter excluding credits (611,000 including them), 29% above the 486,532 delivered. Tesla discloses no customer-acquisition cost, so SG&A at 7.2% of revenue is the nearest proxy and CAC payback and LTV:CAC cannot be computed; the cheaper-CAC claim versus Ford and GM is untested. On operating margin, Tesla's 2.6% sits below GM's 8.2% EBIT-adjusted and Ford's 5.5%, while its 18.1% ex-credit gross margin is level with BYD's 18%: the difference is the operating cost line, not the car. The diligence question is what FSD subscription revenue and Megapack-only margin actually are, because those two numbers decide whether the group earns more than its cost of capital [S115, S116, S119].

The mix also explains the capital-allocation problem: the segments that earn a margin are not the ones absorbing most of the capital, and the one that absorbs it does not cover its own operating cost. Until the filings disclose returns on robotaxi and Megapack capital separately, group return on capital is the only honest scorecard, and it is falling.

arguments.markdown:
Tesla's technology position in 2026 is two facts usually merged in the narrative: the largest supervised-driving data pool and one of the cheapest large-scale EV manufacturing bases in the industry, and almost no verified driverless revenue. Active FSD subscriptions reached 1.74 million at 30 September 2026, 17.1% of the 10.2 million vehicles delivered to date, while cumulative unsupervised Robotaxi miles were "nearly two million", 0.9% of the 220.6 million rider-only miles Waymo had logged through March 2026. The 1.74 million is a company definition that includes upfront FSD purchases and monthly subscriptions and excludes free trials; management put about half the paid base on monthly plans on 21 October 2026, so roughly 870,000 are subscribers worth about $1.0bn a year at list and roughly 870,000 are one-time buyers. Partially verified: the count is filed, the split is call commentary [S9, S151, S152, S173].

### What Tesla actually sells

| Product | Stage | Revenue or share | Next milestone | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| FSD (Supervised) | Commercial, 9 EU countries | 1.74m subscriptions; revenue not disclosed | Unsupervised release | S9, S1 |
| Robotaxi / Cybercab | Paid driverless in Texas | 1,051 authorised at 2026-10-27; revenue not disclosed | Paid-trip disclosure | S9, S125 |
| Model 3 / Model Y | Mature | 478,237 units, Q3 2026; 19.6% group margin | Next platform | S9 |
| Cybertruck, Semi, Roadster | Ramp / design | 8,295 other models, Q3 2026 | Semi ramp | S9 |
| Megapack, Powerwall | Scaling | $2.881bn, Q3 2026; 13.7 GWh | 50 GWh Texas ramp | S9, S60 |
| Optimus | Internal production | Zero external revenue | External pilot sale | S9, S99 |

### Mechanism: end-to-end vision and a one-sided flywheel

Tesla removed radar and maps camera pixels directly to driving commands with an end-to-end neural network, trained on clips harvested from the fleet and run on in-house inference silicon. The flywheel is real but overwhelmingly *supervised*: the Q3 2026 update charts cumulative FSD miles on a 0-16 billion axis against 2.0 million unsupervised miles. Supervised miles teach perception, not the absence of supervision, which is why the federal safety file matters more than the mileage chart [S60].

| Metric | Value | Method | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| Active FSD subscriptions | 1.74m (2026-09-30) | Company count | S9 |
| FSD monthly subscribers | ~870,000 | Half the paid base, call 2026-10-21 | S152, S173 |
| FSD upfront buyers | ~870,000 | Remainder of the 1.74m | S152, S173 |
| FSD subscription run-rate | ~$1.0bn a year, unaudited | 870,000 × $99 × 12, US list | S121, S152 |
| Deferred revenue, connectivity/FSD/Supercharging/OTA | $4.08bn at 2026-09-30 | Company note; FSD not separable | S8 |
| Cumulative unsupervised Robotaxi miles | 2.0m, 8x QoQ | Company count | S9 |
| 4680 capacity, Texas | 40+ GWh/yr, dry electrode both sides | Company nameplate | S60 |
| Storage deployed | 13.7 GWh Q3; 36.0 GWh 9M | Company deliveries | S9 |

### The safety file is the binding constraint

NHTSA's Office of Defects Investigation opened Engineering Analysis EA26002 on 18 March 2026 into whether FSD detects degraded visibility — glare, fog, dust — and warns the driver in time, covering an estimated 3,203,754 vehicles from model years 2016-2026, after nine confirmed incidents including one pedestrian fatality; a second FSD probe covers 2,882,566 vehicles and 80 traffic-law incidents. Tesla's own analysis reportedly found its degradation-detection update "may have affected" only 3 of 9 incidents, which points to an architectural limit of camera-only sensing rather than a tuning defect. An engineering analysis is the last step before a recall, and a recall would narrow the operating domain or force hardware across millions of cars whose liability terms for paid driverless rides are not disclosed [S87, S88, S100].

::: evidence
**The camera-only bet is being tested by the regulator, not the market.** EA26002 covers 3.2 million FSD-equipped vehicles and Tesla's fix reportedly addresses a third of the reviewed incidents; the filings give no remedy or timetable. That is the largest un-priced technical risk in the autonomy option [S87, S88].
:::

### Comparison: four autonomy models, two assisted ones

| Operator | Sensing | Verified scale | Regulatory position | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Tesla | Camera-only, in-house silicon | 2.0m unsupervised miles; 1,051 vehicles authorised in Texas at 2026-10-27 | Paid driverless only in Texas; California testing permit with a safety driver | S9, S125, S89 |
| Waymo | Lidar, radar and camera | 220.6m rider-only miles to 2026-03; about 500,000 paid rides a week | California deployment authorised | S151 |
| Pony.ai, WeRide, Baidu | Lidar and camera | Pony: 1,776 vehicles built by 2026-05-24, $8.6m Q1 robotaxi revenue; WeRide: about 1,300 robotaxis at 2026-04-30; Baidu: 3.2m driverless rides in Q1 2026 | Zone-limited driverless permits in China | S178 |
| Huawei, Momenta | Camera and lidar on OEM vehicles | More than 80% of China's urban NOA market | L2+/L3 systems, driver liable | S168 |
| GM, Ford, comma.ai | Super Cruise, BlueCruise, openpilot | Hands-off, eyes-on only; openpilot: five crashes, three deaths, federal probe 2026-09 | No driverless revenue | S170, S179 |

### Moat: accumulation, not exclusion

| Barrier | Difficulty (1-10) | Why | Time to replicate | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Supervised fleet data | 8 | 10.2m cars; FSD miles charted to 16bn | 4-6 years | S9 |
| Dry-electrode cell process | 7 | Battery Day 2020 to Austin output in 2026 | 3-4 years | S60 |
| Manufacturing and integration | 8 | 134,785 employees; cells and cathode in-house | 5+ years | S1 |
| State permits | 6 | Bilateral and political; not purchasable | 1-3 years | S89, S91 |

The replication test is unflattering to a patent story: 50 funded engineers with every published Tesla patent could build a geofenced driverless service in two to three years — Waymo needed eleven years from its 2009 start — but could not reproduce the fleet data or the factories. Tesla's 10-K concedes the point, pledging irrevocably not to sue any party acting in good faith for infringing its electric-vehicle patents. California is the harder gate: on 23 October 2026 the DMV lists Tesla Robotaxi LLC only as a testing-permit holder requiring a safety driver, and the state's regulator confirmed in March 2026 that Tesla is not operating an autonomous vehicle service, its paid rides running on a limousine permit [S1, S89, S90].

| IP instrument | Covers | Status | Relevance | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Patent non-assertion pledge | EV and related-equipment patents | Irrevocable for good-faith users | Removes patents as a barrier | S1 |
| In-house inference silicon; Samsung foundry deal | AI4/AI5 design and fabrication | Austin fab equipment commissioning 2027 | Cost and performance control | S1, S9 |

Tesla publishes no patent count, so a patent-number table cannot be built; a USPTO assignee search would settle portfolio size and freedom-to-operate risk and has been requested.

### Robotaxi unit economics: the undisclosed half of the model

Insurance, teleoperation and depreciation per vehicle decide whether a paid mile contributes, and none is disclosed.

| Item | Disclosed? | Figure | What it means | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Authorised fleet, Texas | Yes | 1,051 vehicles at 2026-10-27; Cybercab entered 2026-09-03; Austin hours 06:00-24:00 | A city pilot; unit cost not disclosed | S125, S9 |
| Remote supervision | Partly | Remote operators implicated in crashes | An uncosted cost line | S153 |
| Insurance and liability | No | Not disclosed | Decides whether a paid mile contributes | S9 |
| Revenue per paid mile | No | Robotaxi not broken out of Services and Other | Contribution cannot be computed | S9 |
| Benchmark | Pony.ai | $8.6m Q1 2026 revenue on 1,776 vehicles, about $4,800 per vehicle per quarter | At that rate 1,051 cars would produce about $5m a quarter | S178 |

### Optimus is a research programme with a production line

Tesla began Optimus production in Fremont in Q3 2026 and calls the process "suitable for a commercial product", but discloses no units, cycle times, error rates or customers; independent estimates put 1,000-1,200 units across Fremont and Giga Texas with zero external sales. Figure AI has logged 1,250+ hours at BMW and Agility Robotics 65,000+ hours across nine sites, both with paying customers, so Optimus should carry no revenue in a 12-month model [S99].

Tesla's manufacturing and supervised-data advantages are real and hard to buy, but the priced asset is unsupervised autonomy, which today carries a fatality-linked engineering analysis, one authorising state, a pilot fleet and no disclosed revenue. Confidence is high on filings and regulator records, medium on driverless scale, low on Optimus and robotaxi unit economics, where disclosure is absent rather than adverse. The disclosures that would move this: Robotaxi revenue, paid trips and cost per trip reported quarterly; a California driverless deployment permit; and dry-electrode cell cost per kWh against purchased cells. If the first and third come good while the engineering analysis closes without a hardware remedy, the option is worth materially more than a pilot; a recall that restricts the operating domain would remove the revenue bridge.

Tesla closed at $399.81 on 2026-10-30, a $1,580.4bn market capitalisation, 12.7% higher over the past month — a window that includes the 2026-10-21 third-quarter report — and 28.5% higher over three months, yet still 12.4% lower over twelve months against the S&P 500's 10.8% gain [S11, S20]. Energy leads the sector table by 17.6 points over three months against technology's 2.4, and consumer discretionary trails the index.

The verdict is Sell, with zero long exposure and, at most, a capped short; the composite score is 3.8 out of 10. One distribution governs the report: bull 30%, split between autonomy proof and a SpaceX combination, at $506.05; base 40% at $266, -33.5%; bear 22% at $156, -61%; and a full de-rating at 8%, from $64 to $101, for an expected twelve-month return of -25.2%. That is a de-rating call rather than a liquidation call: the reported car, storage and services businesses are worth $139-160bn, or $35-40 a share, against the $1,580.4bn capitalisation, and 90-91% of the equity is an option on autonomy revenue the filings do not book [S8, S9].

The positives are real, and they are why this is a de-rating call rather than a liquidation call. Energy earns a storage gross margin roughly in line with Fluence's fiscal 2025 once the third-quarter tariff refunds are stripped out — 14.8% against 13.1% — the balance sheet holds net cash alongside large undrawn facilities, the US electric-vehicle franchise still sets the price, and a listed SpaceX with both boards' committees offers a premium-bearing exit. Those cards are in the briefing table; none of them changes what the buyer pays today [S9, S61].

The risks to the call are as specific as the thesis. An announced combination at a premium would gap the shares above the bull case, a California deployment permit plus a robotaxi revenue line would turn the option into cash flow, and a recall from the open engineering analysis would cut the option the other way. Confidence is high in the arithmetic of value and low in the durability of the multiple; the diligence that would settle the second is listed below.

Consensus is Hold, with an average target within a rounding error of the price, so the view here is deliberately non-consensus: the market capitalises the autonomy option while this call prices it at zero until a revenue line is disclosed. The one question that decides the case is robotaxi revenue per vehicle-week in Texas and whether it is positive at the contribution level after insurance, depreciation and remote supervision. Across nine months, payables rose $3,868M to $17,239M and the cash conversion cycle fell to 2.6 days from 13.0, so without the payables build nine-month free cash flow would have been -$1,985M. Capital expenditure nearly doubled from $6,134M a year earlier, and the 2026 plan was restated between filings — "in excess of $25 billion" in July 2026, "in excess of $20 billion" in October 2026 — leaving full-year 2026 free cash flow between -$1,290M and +$1,160M depending on whether Q4 operating cash flow matches Q4 2025's $3,813M or Q3 2026's $6,263M [S8, S9, S83, S102].

|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Return on invested capital | 28.3% | 13.7% | 7.0% | 5.5% | S12, S13, S1, S8 |
| Return on equity | 27.9% | 10.5% | 4.9% | 3.8% | S12, S13, S1, S8 |
| Days sales outstanding | 13.2 | 16.5 | 17.6 | 16.3 | S12, S13, S1, S8 |
| Days inventory outstanding | 62.9 | 54.7 | 58.2 | 61.5 | S12, S13, S1, S8 |
| Days payables outstanding | 66.6 | 56.7 | 62.8 | 75.3 | S12, S13, S1, S8 |
| Cash conversion cycle (days) | 9.5 | 14.4 | 13.0 | 2.6 | S12, S13, S1, S8 |
| Interest coverage | 56.99x | 20.22x | 12.88x | 9.96x | S12, S13, S1, S8 |
| Stock-based compensation / revenue | 1.9% | 2.0% | 3.0% | 4.2% | S12, S13, S1, S8 |
| Net cash | 24,437 | 28,685 | 35,906 | 36,180 | S12, S13, S1, S8 |

Cash of $17,853M and short-term investments of $27,594M against $9,267M of debt gave $36,180M of net cash at 2026-09-30, and three credit agreements signed in September 2026 lifted unused committed facilities to $30.00B from $6.43B at 2025-12-31, so the $20B capex year is funded several times over without equity. Nothing has been returned to shareholders: no dividend and no repurchase from FY2021 to Q3 2026, while $2,000M of cash went into the xAI investment and converted into SpaceX Class A stock in March 2026 [S8, S1, S10, S115, S104].

### The EBITDA bridge and the price it supports

| Adjusted EBITDA bridge, $M | Value | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Q4 2025 | 4,154 | S9 |
| Q1 2026 | 3,668 | S9 |
| Q2 2026 | 3,273 | S9 |
| Q3 2026 | 3,900 | S9 |
| Trailing twelve months | 14,995 | S9 |
| Less Q3 2026 IEEPA energy refund | (526) | S8 |
| Normalised trailing | 14,469 | S8, S9 (derived) |
| Base case: held flat, no credit recovery, no robotaxi line, energy at 15% | 14,500 | derived |

Trailing adjusted EBITDA of $14,995M is the sum of four quarters; subtracting the $526M Q3 2026 IEEPA energy refund gives $14,469M, held at $14.5bn in the base case and 12 points of energy margin below the old 27% midpoint on $12.3bn of trailing energy revenue. The bull case's $506.05 is not an EBITDA output: 3,952.6M shares × $506.05 = $2,000bn, exactly the first market-capitalisation gate of the 2025 CEO award, and 131 times the $15.3bn of EBITDA the same case assumes. A 70x multiple on $14.5bn plus $36.18bn of net cash gives $266, the 40% base case; the report's distribution — 30% bull at $506.05, 40% base at $266, 22% bear at $156 and 8% full de-rating at $64-101 — produces a -25.2% expected return [S9, S8, S10].

### What flatters the number, and what would change it

Interest income of $1,301M was 42.9% of nine-month pre-tax income and $445M was 46.5% of the Q3 2026 figure, against 17.5% in FY2024. Stock-based compensation of $3,346M in nine months is 4.3% of revenue and the main reason non-GAAP profit more than doubles GAAP profit; EPS is struck on 3,240M basic and 3,541M diluted weighted-average shares against 3,952,648,559 issued at 2026-09-30, and the 710M gap is 423.7M unearned 2025 award shares and 286.4M unvested 2018 restricted shares already inside the issued count, with the diluted count adding about 301M options and RSUs. Warranty adjustments flattered automotive cost while the warranty reserve rose 20.9%. Sensitivity: a percentage point of ex-credit automotive margin is worth $800M a year on $80,000M of revenue, 6.4 times a point of energy margin at $12,300M, and each $1B of capex is $1B of free cash flow. The $1.5bn cut from the earlier $16.0bn base is 12 points of energy margin on $12.3bn of trailing revenue (27% to 15%); at 14-18% energy margin, $14.5bn of adjusted EBITDA and $20B of capex, free cash flow is roughly $0 to +$0.5bn, not the $2.0bn the 30% energy assumption implied. ::: info danger
The most serious red flag is the composition of free cash flow: nine-month free cash flow is smaller than the rise in payables that produced it, capex was re-scoped in the same quarter that new credit lines were arranged, and the cash balance generating almost half of pre-tax profit is the only reason reported earnings look positive at the operating level.
