arguments.markdown:
Tesla's technology position in 2026 is two facts usually merged in the narrative: the largest supervised-driving data pool and one of the cheapest large-scale EV manufacturing bases in the industry, and almost no verified driverless revenue. Active FSD subscriptions reached 1.74 million at 30 September 2026, 17.1% of the 10.2 million vehicles delivered to date, while cumulative unsupervised Robotaxi miles were "nearly two million", 0.9% of the 220.6 million rider-only miles Waymo had logged through March 2026. The 1.74 million is a company definition that includes upfront FSD purchases and monthly subscriptions and excludes free trials; management put about half the paid base on monthly plans on 21 October 2026, so roughly 870,000 are subscribers worth about $1.0bn a year at list and roughly 870,000 are one-time buyers. Partially verified: the count is filed, the split is call commentary [S9, S151, S152, S173].

### What Tesla actually sells

| Product | Stage | Revenue or share | Next milestone | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| FSD (Supervised) | Commercial, 9 EU countries | 1.74m subscriptions; revenue not disclosed | Unsupervised release | S9, S1 |
| Robotaxi / Cybercab | Paid driverless in Texas | 1,051 authorised at 2026-10-27; revenue not disclosed | Paid-trip disclosure | S9, S125 |
| Model 3 / Model Y | Mature | 478,237 units, Q3 2026; 19.6% group margin | Next platform | S9 |
| Cybertruck, Semi, Roadster | Ramp / design | 8,295 other models, Q3 2026 | Semi ramp | S9 |
| Megapack, Powerwall | Scaling | $2.881bn, Q3 2026; 13.7 GWh | 50 GWh Texas ramp | S9, S60 |
| Optimus | Internal production | Zero external revenue | External pilot sale | S9, S99 |

### Mechanism: end-to-end vision and a one-sided flywheel

Tesla removed radar and maps camera pixels directly to driving commands with an end-to-end neural network, trained on clips harvested from the fleet and run on in-house inference silicon. The flywheel is real but overwhelmingly *supervised*: the Q3 2026 update charts cumulative FSD miles on a 0-16 billion axis against 2.0 million unsupervised miles. Supervised miles teach perception, not the absence of supervision, which is why the federal safety file matters more than the mileage chart [S60].

| Metric | Value | Method | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| Active FSD subscriptions | 1.74m (2026-09-30) | Company count | S9 |
| FSD monthly subscribers | ~870,000 | Half the paid base, call 2026-10-21 | S152, S173 |
| FSD subscription run-rate | ~$1.0bn a year, unaudited | 870,000 × $99 × 12, US list | S121, S152 |
| Deferred revenue, connectivity/FSD/Supercharging/OTA | $4.08bn at 2026-09-30 | Company note; FSD not separable | S8 |
| Cumulative unsupervised Robotaxi miles | 2.0m, 8x QoQ | Company count | S9 |
| 4680 capacity, Texas | 40+ GWh/yr, dry electrode both sides | Company nameplate | S60 |
| Storage deployed | 13.7 GWh Q3; 36.0 GWh 9M | Company deliveries | S9 |

### The safety file is the binding constraint

NHTSA's Office of Defects Investigation opened Engineering Analysis EA26002 on 18 March 2026 into whether FSD detects degraded visibility — glare, fog, dust — and warns the driver in time, covering an estimated 3,203,754 vehicles, after nine confirmed incidents including one pedestrian fatality; a second FSD probe covers 2,882,566 vehicles and 80 traffic-law incidents. Tesla's own analysis reportedly found its degradation-detection update "may have affected" only 3 of 9 incidents, which points to an architectural limit of camera-only sensing rather than a tuning defect. An engineering analysis is the last step before a recall, and a recall would narrow the operating domain or force hardware across millions of cars whose liability terms for paid driverless rides are not disclosed [S87, S88, S100].

::: evidence
**The camera-only bet is being tested by the regulator, not the market.** EA26002 covers 3.2 million FSD-equipped vehicles and Tesla's fix reportedly addresses a third of the reviewed incidents; the filings give no remedy or timetable [S87, S88].
:::

### Comparison: four autonomy models, two assisted ones

| Operator | Sensing | Verified scale | Regulatory position | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Tesla | Camera-only, in-house silicon | 2.0m unsupervised miles; 1,051 vehicles authorised in Texas at 2026-10-27 | Paid driverless only in Texas; California testing permit with a safety driver | S9, S125, S89 |
| Waymo | Lidar, radar and camera | 220.6m rider-only miles to 2026-03; about 500,000 paid rides a week | California deployment authorised | S151 |
| Pony.ai, WeRide, Baidu | Lidar and camera | Pony: 1,776 vehicles built by 2026-05-24, $8.6m Q1 robotaxi revenue; WeRide: about 1,300 robotaxis at 2026-04-30; Baidu: 3.2m driverless rides in Q1 2026 | Zone-limited driverless permits in China | S178 |
| Huawei, Momenta | Camera and lidar on OEM vehicles | More than 80% of China's urban NOA market | L2+/L3 systems, driver liable | S168 |
| GM, Ford, comma.ai | Super Cruise, BlueCruise, openpilot | Hands-off, eyes-on only; openpilot: five crashes, three deaths, federal probe 2026-09 | No driverless revenue | S170, S179 |

### Moat: accumulation, not exclusion

| Barrier | Difficulty (1-10) | Why | Time to replicate | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Supervised fleet data | 8 | 10.2m cars; FSD miles charted to 16bn | 4-6 years | S9 |
| Dry-electrode cell process | 7 | Battery Day 2020 to Austin output in 2026 | 3-4 years | S60 |
| Manufacturing and integration | 8 | 134,785 employees; cells and cathode in-house | 5+ years | S1 |

The replication test is unflattering to a patent story: 50 funded engineers with every published Tesla patent could build a geofenced driverless service in two to three years but could not reproduce the fleet data or the factories. Tesla's 10-K concedes the point, pledging irrevocably not to sue any party acting in good faith for infringing its electric-vehicle patents. California is the harder gate: on 23 October 2026 the DMV lists Tesla Robotaxi LLC only as a testing-permit holder requiring a safety driver, and the state's regulator confirmed in March 2026 that Tesla is not operating an autonomous vehicle service, its paid rides running on a limousine permit [S1, S89, S90].

| IP instrument | Covers | Status | Relevance | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Patent non-assertion pledge | EV and related-equipment patents | Irrevocable for good-faith users | Removes patents as a barrier | S1 |
| In-house inference silicon; Samsung foundry deal | AI4/AI5 design and fabrication | Austin fab equipment commissioning 2027 | Cost and performance control | S1, S9 |

Tesla publishes no patent count; a USPTO assignee search would settle portfolio size and freedom-to-operate risk and has been requested.

### Robotaxi unit economics: the undisclosed half of the model

| Item | Disclosed? | Figure | What it means | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Authorised fleet, Texas | Yes | 1,051 vehicles at 2026-10-27; Cybercab entered 2026-09-03; Austin hours 06:00-24:00 | A city pilot; unit cost not disclosed | S125, S9 |
| Remote supervision | Partly | Remote operators implicated in crashes | An uncosted cost line | S153 |
| Insurance and liability | No | Not disclosed | Decides whether a paid mile contributes | S9 |
| Revenue per paid mile | No | Robotaxi not broken out of Services and Other | Contribution cannot be computed | S9 |
| Benchmark | Pony.ai | $8.6m Q1 2026 revenue on 1,776 vehicles, about $4,800 per vehicle per quarter | At that rate 1,051 cars would produce about $5m a quarter | S178 |

Insurance, teleoperation and depreciation per vehicle decide whether a paid mile contributes, and none is disclosed; the visible pieces describe a city pilot with a modest revenue benchmark.

### Optimus is a research programme with a production line

Tesla began Optimus production in Fremont in Q3 2026 and calls the process "suitable for a commercial product", but discloses no units, cycle times, error rates or customers; independent estimates put 1,000-1,200 units across Fremont and Giga Texas with zero external sales. Figure AI has logged 1,250+ hours at BMW and Agility Robotics 65,000+ hours across nine sites, both with paying customers, so Optimus should carry no revenue in a 12-month model [S99].

Tesla's manufacturing and supervised-data advantages are real and hard to buy, but the priced asset is unsupervised autonomy, which today carries a fatality-linked engineering analysis, one authorising state, a pilot fleet and no disclosed revenue. Confidence is high on filings, medium on driverless scale, low on Optimus and robotaxi unit economics, where disclosure is absent rather than adverse. The disclosures that would move this: Robotaxi revenue, paid trips and cost per trip reported quarterly; a California driverless deployment permit; and dry-electrode cell cost per kWh against purchased cells. If the first and third come good while the engineering analysis closes without a hardware remedy, the option is worth materially more than a pilot; a recall that restricts the operating domain would remove the revenue bridge.

### Optimus is a research programme with a production line

arguments.markdown:
Tesla converted $1,531M of free cash flow in Q3 2026, but the statements no longer show it earning its cost of capital: a 5.5% trailing return on invested capital sits 57 basis points above the ten-year Treasury, $41,778M of capex since 2023 has coincided with a 61% fall in operating income, and the profit that remains leans on interest income, a payables build and $526M of one-off energy tariff refunds. Normalising those refunds puts trailing adjusted EBITDA at $14,469M, and at 70x that plus net cash the report's 40% base case is $266 a share [S8, S12, S11].

### Revenue recovered, operating profit did not

| Line item ($M unless stated) | FY2023 | FY2024 | FY2025 | Q3 2026 | 9M 2026 | TTM to 2026-09-30 | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Revenue | 96,773 | 97,690 | 94,827 | 28,046 | 78,669 | 103,570 | S12, S13, S1, S8 |
| Gross profit | 17,660 | 17,450 | 17,094 | 5,494 | 14,965 | 19,974 | S12, S13, S1, S8 |
| Research and development | 3,969 | 4,540 | 6,411 | 2,761 | 7,078 | 8,861 | S12, S13, S1, S8 |
| Selling, general and administrative | 4,800 | 5,150 | 5,834 | 2,015 | 5,830 | 7,485 | S12, S13, S1, S8 |
| Operating income | 8,891 | 7,076 | 4,355 | 718 | 2,057 | 3,466 | S12, S13, S1, S8 |
| Net income | 14,997 | 7,091 | 3,794 | 787 | 2,378 | 3,218 | S12, S13, S1, S8 |
| Diluted EPS ($) | 4.30 | 2.04 | 1.08 | 0.22 | 0.67 | 0.91 | S12, S13, S1, S8 |
| Operating cash flow | 13,256 | 14,923 | 14,747 | 6,263 | 14,897 | 18,710 | S12, S13, S1, S8 |
| Capital expenditure | 8,898 | 11,339 | 8,527 | 4,732 | 13,014 | 15,407 | S12, S13, S1, S8 |
| Free cash flow | 4,358 | 3,584 | 6,220 | 1,531 | 1,883 | 3,296 | S12, S13, S1, S8 |

Revenue fell for two years before the 2026 rebound while operating income fell throughout, from $8,891M in FY2023 to $3,466M trailing, because research and development rose from $3,969M to $8,861M and selling and administrative cost from $4,800M to $7,485M against gross profit that stayed between $17.1B and $20.0B. Q3 2026 revenue was $28,046M, gross profit $5,494M (19.6%), operating income $718M (2.6%), net income $787M and diluted EPS $0.22, on deliveries down 2% to 486,532 from 497,099, so price, mix and a weaker dollar carried the top line. GAAP net income of $787M compared with non-GAAP of $1,697M, and diluted EPS of $0.22 with $0.48. The quarter also absorbed a $475M reversal of previously recognised regulatory credit revenue, so the 2.6% operating margin understates the underlying figure by 1.7 points [S12, S13, S1, S8].

### Free cash flow is a payables loan and a capex pause

Nine-month operating cash flow of $14,897M exceeded the $13,014M of capital expenditure to leave $1,883M of free cash flow, against $6,220M for FY2025. Management attributes $3.51 billion of the $3.96 billion year-on-year operating-cash-flow increase to working capital, and in Q3 2026 alone free cash flow of $1,531M rested on a $2,590M working-capital inflow, of which accounts payable supplied $1,920M and accrued liabilities $1,950M; stripping it out, quarterly free cash flow was -$1,059M, and $3,670M of capex sat in liabilities at 2026-09-30. Across nine months, payables rose $3,868M to $17,239M and the cash conversion cycle fell to 2.6 days from 13.0, so without the payables build nine-month free cash flow would have been -$1,985M. Capital expenditure nearly doubled from $6,134M a year earlier, and the 2026 plan was restated between filings — "in excess of $25 billion" in July 2026, "in excess of $20 billion" in October 2026 — leaving full-year 2026 free cash flow between -$1,290M and +$1,160M depending on whether Q4 operating cash flow matches Q4 2025's $3,813M or Q3 2026's $6,263M [S8, S9, S83, S102].

### The balance sheet carries the plan; the capital does not earn its keep

| Metric | FY2023 | FY2024 | FY2025 | TTM to 2026-09-30 | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Return on invested capital | 28.3% | 13.7% | 7.0% | 5.5% | S12, S13, S1, S8 |
| Return on equity | 27.9% | 10.5% | 4.9% | 3.8% | S12, S13, S1, S8 |
| Days sales outstanding | 13.2 | 16.5 | 17.6 | 16.3 | S12, S13, S1, S8 |
| Days inventory outstanding | 62.9 | 54.7 | 58.2 | 61.5 | S12, S13, S1, S8 |
| Days payables outstanding | 66.6 | 56.7 | 62.8 | 75.3 | S12, S13, S1, S8 |
| Cash conversion cycle (days) | 9.5 | 14.4 | 13.0 | 2.6 | S12, S13, S1, S8 |
| Interest coverage | 56.99x | 20.22x | 12.88x | 9.96x | S12, S13, S1, S8 |
| Stock-based compensation / revenue | 1.9% | 2.0% | 3.0% | 4.2% | S12, S13, S1, S8 |
| Net cash | 24,437 | 28,685 | 35,906 | 36,180 | S12, S13, S1, S8 |

Cash of $17,853M and short-term investments of $27,594M against $9,267M of debt gave $36,180M of net cash at 2026-09-30, and three credit agreements signed in September 2026 lifted unused committed facilities to $30.00B from $6.43B at 2025-12-31, so the $20B capex year is funded several times over without equity. The obligations outside the debt line matter more: $7,955M of minimum lease payments at 2025-12-31, of which $1,320M falls due within twelve months; an accrued warranty reserve of $7,414M that grew 20.9% in nine months against 10% delivery growth; and $7,055M of deferred revenue. Returns have fallen faster than margins: return on invested capital went from 28.3% in FY2023 to 13.7%, 7.0% and 5.5% trailing, and return on equity from 27.9% to 3.8%; the 5.5% compares with a 4.93% ten-year Treasury yield on 2026-10-30, leaving 57 basis points for equity risk. The capex record explains it: $41,778M spent in FY2023 through the first nine months of 2026 against a $5,425M fall in operating income over the same span, an incremental return that is negative at group level. Nothing has been returned to shareholders: no dividend and no repurchase from FY2021 to Q3 2026, while $2,000M of cash went into the xAI investment and converted into SpaceX Class A stock in March 2026 [S8, S1, S10, S115, S104].

### The EBITDA bridge and the price it supports

| Adjusted EBITDA bridge, $M | Value | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Q4 2025 | 4,154 | S9 |
| Q1 2026 | 3,668 | S9 |
| Q2 2026 | 3,273 | S9 |
| Q3 2026 | 3,900 | S9 |
| Trailing twelve months | 14,995 | S9 |
| Less Q3 2026 IEEPA energy refund | (526) | S8 |
| Normalised trailing | 14,469 | S8, S9 (derived) |
| Base case: held flat, no credit recovery, no robotaxi line, energy at 15% | 14,500 | S8, S9 (derived) |

Trailing adjusted EBITDA of $14,995M is the sum of four quarters; subtracting the $526M Q3 2026 IEEPA energy refund gives $14,469M, held at $14.5bn in the base case and 12 points of energy margin below the old 27% midpoint on $12.3bn of trailing energy revenue. The bull case's $506.05 is not an EBITDA output: 3,952.6M shares × $506.05 = $2,000bn, exactly the first market-capitalisation gate of the 2025 CEO award, and 131 times the $15.3bn of EBITDA the same case assumes. A 70x multiple on $14.5bn plus $36.18bn of net cash gives $266, the 40% base case; the report's distribution — 30% bull at $506.05, 40% base at $266, 22% bear at $156 and 8% full de-rating at $64-101 — produces a -25.2% expected return [S9, S8, S10].

### What flatters the number, and what would change it

Interest income of $1,301M was 42.9% of nine-month pre-tax income and $445M was 46.5% of the Q3 2026 figure, against 17.5% in FY2024. Stock-based compensation of $3,346M in nine months is 4.3% of revenue and the main reason non-GAAP profit more than doubles GAAP profit; EPS is struck on 3,240M basic and 3,541M diluted weighted-average shares against 3,952,648,559 issued at 2026-09-30, and the 710M gap is 423.7M unearned 2025 award shares and 286.4M unvested 2018 restricted shares already inside the issued count, with the diluted count adding 301M options and RSUs. Warranty adjustments flattered automotive cost while the warranty reserve rose 20.9%. Sensitivity: a percentage point of ex-credit automotive margin is worth $800M a year on $80,000M of revenue, 6.4 times a point of energy margin at $12,300M, and each $1B of capex is $1B of free cash flow. The $1.5bn cut from the $16.0bn base is 12 points of energy margin on $12.3bn of trailing revenue (27% to 15%); at 14-18% energy margin, $14.5bn of adjusted EBITDA and $20B of capex, free cash flow is roughly $0 to +$0.5bn, not the $2.0bn the 30% energy assumption implied. The variable that moves the outcome most is capex, worth $5B in a single restatement between July and October 2026 — more than six points of automotive margin. The diligence question is what the 2027 capex number is and whether the payables build reflects renegotiated terms or deferred payments [S8, S83, S1, S117, S102].

::: info danger
The most serious red flag is the composition of free cash flow: nine-month free cash flow is smaller than the rise in payables that produced it, capex was re-scoped in the same quarter that new credit lines were arranged, and the cash balance generating almost half of pre-tax profit is the only reason reported earnings look positive at the operating level. Reported free cash flow is a ceiling, not a run-rate.
:::

arguments.markdown:
Tesla's technology position in 2026 is two facts usually merged in the narrative: the largest supervised-driving data pool and one of the cheapest large-scale EV manufacturing bases in the industry, and almost no verified driverless revenue. Active FSD subscriptions reached 1.74 million at 30 September 2026, 17.1% of the 10.2 million vehicles delivered to date, while cumulative unsupervised Robotaxi miles were 2.0 million, 0.9% of the 220.6 million rider-only miles Waymo had logged through March 2026. The 1.74 million is a company definition that includes upfront FSD purchases and monthly subscriptions and excludes free trials; management put half the paid base on monthly plans on 21 October 2026, so 870,000 are subscribers worth $1.0bn a year at list and 870,000 are one-time buyers. Partially verified: the count is filed, the split is call commentary [S9, S151, S152, S173].

### What Tesla actually sells

| Product | Stage | Revenue or share | Next milestone | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| FSD (Supervised) | Commercial, 9 EU countries | 1.74m subscriptions; revenue not disclosed | Unsupervised release | S9, S1 |
| Robotaxi / Cybercab | Paid driverless in Texas | 1,051 authorised at 2026-10-27; revenue not disclosed | Paid-trip disclosure | S9, S125 |
| Model 3 / Model Y | Mature | 478,237 units, Q3 2026; 19.6% group margin | Next platform | S9 |
| Cybertruck, Semi, Roadster | Ramp / design | 8,295 other models, Q3 2026 | Semi ramp | S9 |
| Megapack, Powerwall | Scaling | $2.881bn, Q3 2026; 13.7 GWh | 50 GWh Texas ramp | S9, S60 |
| Optimus | Internal production | Zero external revenue | External pilot sale | S9, S99 |

### Mechanism: end-to-end vision and a one-sided flywheel

Tesla removed radar and maps camera pixels directly to driving commands with an end-to-end neural network, trained on fleet clips and run on in-house inference silicon. The flywheel is real but overwhelmingly *supervised*: the Q3 2026 update charts cumulative FSD miles on a 0-16 billion axis against 2.0 million unsupervised miles. Supervised miles teach perception, not the absence of supervision, which is why the federal safety file matters more than the mileage chart [S60].

| Metric | Value | Method | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| Active FSD subscriptions | 1.74m (2026-09-30) | Company count | S9 |
| FSD monthly subscribers | 870,000 | Half the paid base, call 2026-10-21 | S152, S173 |
| FSD subscription run-rate | $1.0bn a year, unaudited | 870,000 × $99 × 12, US list | S121, S152 |
| Deferred revenue, connectivity/FSD/Supercharging/OTA | $4.08bn at 2026-09-30 | Company note; FSD not separable | S8 |
| Cumulative unsupervised Robotaxi miles | 2.0m, 8x QoQ | Company count | S9 |
| 4680 capacity, Texas | 40+ GWh/yr, dry electrode both sides | Company nameplate | S60 |
| Storage deployed | 13.7 GWh Q3; 36.0 GWh 9M | Company deliveries | S9 |

### The safety file is the binding constraint

NHTSA's Office of Defects Investigation opened Engineering Analysis EA26002 on 18 March 2026 into whether FSD detects degraded visibility — glare, fog, dust — and warns the driver in time, covering 3,203,754 vehicles, after nine confirmed incidents including one pedestrian fatality; a second FSD probe covers 2,882,566 vehicles and 80 traffic-law incidents. Tesla's own analysis reportedly found its degradation-detection update "may have affected" only 3 of 9 incidents, which points to an architectural limit of camera-only sensing rather than a tuning defect. An engineering analysis is the last step before a recall, and a recall would narrow the operating domain or force hardware across millions of cars whose liability terms for paid driverless rides are not disclosed [S87, S88, S100].

::: evidence
**The camera-only bet is being tested by the regulator, not the market.** EA26002 covers 3.2 million FSD-equipped vehicles and Tesla's fix reportedly addresses a third of the reviewed incidents [S87, S88].
:::

### Comparison: four autonomy models, two assisted ones

Measured on verified driverless operation, Tesla is behind Waymo and behind the Chinese operators, not ahead.

| Dimension | Tesla | Waymo | Pony.ai, WeRide, Baidu | Huawei, Momenta | GM, Ford, comma.ai | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Sensing | Camera-only, in-house silicon | Lidar, radar and camera | Lidar and camera | Camera and lidar on OEM vehicles | Camera-radar; camera | S9, S151, S178, S170 |
| Verified scale | 2.0m unsupervised miles; 1,051 vehicles authorised in Texas at 2026-10-27 | 220.6m rider-only miles to 2026-03; 500,000 paid rides a week | Pony: 1,776 vehicles built by 2026-05-24, $8.6m Q1 robotaxi revenue; WeRide: 1,300 robotaxis at 2026-04-30; Baidu: 3.2m driverless rides in Q1 2026 | 80%+ of China's urban NOA market | Hands-off, eyes-on only; openpilot: five crashes, three deaths, federal probe 2026-09 | S9, S125, S151, S178, S168, S179 |
| Regulatory position | Paid driverless only in Texas; California testing permit with a safety driver | California deployment authorised | Zone-limited driverless permits in China | L2+/L3 systems, driver liable | No driverless revenue | S89, S151, S178 |
| Cost model | Owned fleet | Owned fleet, partner vehicles | Own fleet plus partners | Licensed to OEMs | Subscription or $999 device | S9, S178, S170 |

### Moat: accumulation, not exclusion

| Barrier | Difficulty (1-10) | Why | Time to replicate | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Supervised fleet data | 8 | 10.2m cars; FSD miles charted to 16bn | 4-6 years | S9 |
| Dry-electrode cell process | 7 | Battery Day 2020 to Austin output in 2026 | 3-4 years | S60 |
| Manufacturing and integration | 8 | 134,785 employees; cells and cathode in-house | 5+ years | S1 |

The replication test is unflattering to a patent story: 50 funded engineers with every published Tesla patent could build a geofenced driverless service in two to three years but could not reproduce the fleet data or the factories. Tesla's 10-K concedes the point, pledging irrevocably not to sue any party acting in good faith for infringing its electric-vehicle patents. California is the harder gate: on 23 October 2026 the DMV lists Tesla Robotaxi LLC only as a testing-permit holder requiring a safety driver, and the state's regulator confirmed in March 2026 that Tesla is not operating an autonomous vehicle service, its paid rides running on a limousine permit [S1, S89, S90].

| IP instrument | Covers | Status | Relevance | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Patent non-assertion pledge | EV and related-equipment patents | Irrevocable for good-faith users | Removes patents as a barrier | S1 |
| In-house inference silicon; Samsung foundry deal | AI4/AI5 design and fabrication | Austin fab equipment commissioning 2027 | Cost and performance control | S1, S9 |

Tesla publishes no patent count; a USPTO assignee search, requested, would settle portfolio size and freedom-to-operate risk.

### Robotaxi unit economics: the undisclosed half of the model

| Item | Disclosed? | Figure | What it means | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Authorised fleet, Texas | Yes | 1,051 vehicles at 2026-10-27; Cybercab entered 2026-09-03; Austin hours 06:00-24:00 | A city pilot; unit cost not disclosed | S125, S9 |
| Remote supervision | Partly | Remote operators implicated in crashes | An uncosted cost line | S153 |
| Insurance and liability | No | Not disclosed | Decides whether a paid mile contributes | S9 |
| Revenue per paid mile | No | Robotaxi not broken out of Services and Other | Contribution cannot be computed | S9 |
| Benchmark | Pony.ai | $8.6m Q1 2026 revenue on 1,776 vehicles, $4,800 per vehicle per quarter | At that rate 1,051 cars would produce $5m a quarter | S178 |

Insurance, teleoperation and depreciation decide whether a paid mile contributes; none is disclosed.

### Optimus is a research programme with a production line

Tesla began Optimus production in Fremont in Q3 2026 and calls the process "suitable for a commercial product", but discloses no units, cycle times, error rates or customers; independent estimates put 1,000-1,200 units across Fremont and Giga Texas with zero external sales. Figure AI has logged 1,250+ hours at BMW and Agility Robotics 65,000+ hours across nine sites, both with paying customers, so Optimus should carry no revenue in a 12-month model [S99].

Tesla's manufacturing and supervised-data advantages are real and hard to buy, but the priced asset is unsupervised autonomy, which today carries a fatality-linked engineering analysis, one authorising state, a pilot fleet and no disclosed revenue. Confidence is high on filings, medium on driverless scale, low on Optimus and robotaxi unit economics, where disclosure is absent. The disclosures that would move this: Robotaxi revenue, paid trips and cost per trip reported quarterly; a California driverless deployment permit; and dry-electrode cell cost per kWh against purchased cells. If the first and third come good while the engineering analysis closes without a hardware remedy, the option is worth materially more than a pilot; a recall that restricts the operating domain would remove the revenue bridge.

arguments.markdown:
Tesla's technology position in 2026 is two facts usually merged in the narrative: the largest supervised-driving data pool and one of the cheapest large-scale EV manufacturing bases in the industry, and almost no verified driverless revenue. Active FSD subscriptions reached 1.74 million at 30 September 2026, 17.1% of the 10.2 million vehicles delivered to date, while cumulative unsupervised Robotaxi miles were 2.0 million, 0.9% of the 220.6 million rider-only miles Waymo had logged through March 2026. The 1.74 million includes upfront FSD purchases and monthly subscriptions and excludes free trials; management put half the paid base on monthly plans on 21 October 2026, so 870,000 are subscribers worth $1.0bn a year at list and 870,000 are one-time buyers. Partially verified: the count is filed, the split is call commentary [S9, S151, S152, S173].

### What Tesla actually sells

| Product | Stage | Revenue or share | Next milestone | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| FSD (Supervised) | Commercial, 9 EU countries | 1.74m subscriptions; revenue not disclosed | Unsupervised release | S9, S1 |
| Robotaxi / Cybercab | Paid driverless in Texas | 1,051 authorised at 2026-10-27; revenue not disclosed | Paid-trip disclosure | S9, S125 |
| Model 3 / Model Y | Mature | 478,237 units, Q3 2026; 19.6% group margin | Next platform | S9 |
| Cybertruck, Semi, Roadster | Ramp / design | 8,295 other models, Q3 2026 | Semi ramp | S9 |
| Megapack, Powerwall | Scaling | $2.881bn, Q3 2026; 13.7 GWh | 50 GWh Texas ramp | S9, S60 |
| Optimus | Internal production | Zero external revenue | External pilot sale | S9, S99 |

### Mechanism: end-to-end vision and a one-sided flywheel

Tesla removed radar and maps camera pixels directly to driving commands with an end-to-end neural network, trained on fleet clips and run on in-house inference silicon. The flywheel is real but overwhelmingly *supervised*: the Q3 2026 update charts cumulative FSD miles on a 0-16 billion axis against 2.0 million unsupervised miles. Supervised miles teach perception, not the absence of supervision; the federal safety file matters more than the mileage chart [S60].

| Metric | Value | Method | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| Active FSD subscriptions | 1.74m (2026-09-30) | Company count | S9 |
| FSD monthly subscribers | 870,000 | Half the paid base, call 2026-10-21 | S152, S173 |
| FSD subscription run-rate | $1.0bn a year, unaudited | 870,000 × $99 × 12, US list | S121, S152 |
| Deferred revenue, connectivity/FSD/Supercharging/OTA | $4.08bn at 2026-09-30 | Company note; FSD not separable | S8 |
| Cumulative unsupervised Robotaxi miles | 2.0m, 8x QoQ | Company count | S9 |
| 4680 capacity, Texas | 40+ GWh/yr, dry electrode both sides | Company nameplate | S60 |
| Storage deployed | 13.7 GWh Q3; 36.0 GWh 9M | Company deliveries | S9 |

### The safety file is the binding constraint

NHTSA's Office of Defects Investigation opened Engineering Analysis EA26002 on 18 March 2026 into whether FSD detects degraded visibility — glare, fog, dust — and warns the driver in time, covering 3,203,754 vehicles, after nine confirmed incidents including one pedestrian fatality; a second FSD probe covers 2,882,566 vehicles and 80 traffic-law incidents. Tesla's own analysis reportedly found its degradation-detection update "may have affected" only 3 of 9 incidents, which points to an architectural limit of camera-only sensing. An engineering analysis is the last step before a recall, and a recall would narrow the operating domain or force hardware across millions of cars whose liability terms for paid driverless rides are not disclosed [S87, S88, S100].

::: evidence
**The camera-only bet is being tested by the regulator, not the market.** EA26002 covers 3.2 million FSD-equipped vehicles and Tesla's fix reportedly addresses a third of the reviewed incidents [S87, S88].
:::

### Comparison: four autonomy models, two assisted ones

Measured on verified driverless operation, Tesla is behind Waymo and behind the Chinese operators, not ahead.

| Dimension | Tesla | Waymo | Pony.ai, WeRide, Baidu | Huawei, Momenta | GM, Ford, comma.ai | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Sensing | Camera-only, in-house silicon | Lidar, radar and camera | Lidar and camera | Camera and lidar on OEM vehicles | Camera-radar; camera | S9, S151, S178, S170 |
| Verified scale | 2.0m unsupervised miles; 1,051 vehicles authorised in Texas at 2026-10-27 | 220.6m rider-only miles to 2026-03; 500,000 paid rides a week | Pony: 1,776 vehicles built by 2026-05-24, $8.6m Q1 robotaxi revenue; WeRide: 1,300 robotaxis at 2026-04-30; Baidu: 3.2m driverless rides in Q1 2026 | 80%+ of China's urban NOA market | Hands-off, eyes-on only; openpilot: five crashes, three deaths, federal probe 2026-09 | S9, S125, S151, S178, S168, S179 |
| Regulatory position | Paid driverless only in Texas; California testing permit with a safety driver | California deployment authorised | Zone-limited driverless permits in China | L2+/L3 systems, driver liable | No driverless revenue | S89, S151, S178 |
| Cost model | Owned fleet | Owned fleet, partner vehicles | Own fleet plus partners | Licensed to OEMs | Subscription or $999 device | S9, S178, S170 |

### Moat: accumulation, not exclusion

| Barrier | Difficulty (1-10) | Why | Time to replicate | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Supervised fleet data | 8 | 10.2m cars; FSD miles charted to 16bn | 4-6 years | S9 |
| Dry-electrode cell process | 7 | Battery Day 2020 to Austin output in 2026 | 3-4 years | S60 |
| Manufacturing and integration | 8 | 134,785 employees; cells and cathode in-house | 5+ years | S1 |

The replication test is unflattering to a patent story: 50 funded engineers with every published Tesla patent could build a geofenced driverless service in two to three years but could not reproduce the fleet data or the factories. Tesla's 10-K concedes the point, pledging irrevocably not to sue any party acting in good faith for infringing its electric-vehicle patents. California is the harder gate: on 23 October 2026 the DMV lists Tesla Robotaxi LLC only as a testing-permit holder requiring a safety driver, and the state's regulator confirmed in March 2026 that Tesla is not operating an autonomous vehicle service, its paid rides running on a limousine permit [S1, S89, S90].

| IP instrument | Covers | Status | Relevance | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Patent non-assertion pledge | EV and related-equipment patents | Irrevocable for good-faith users | Removes patents as a barrier | S1 |
| In-house inference silicon; Samsung foundry deal | AI4/AI5 design and fabrication | Austin fab equipment commissioning 2027 | Cost and performance control | S1, S9 |

Tesla publishes no patent count; a USPTO assignee search, requested, would settle portfolio size and freedom-to-operate risk.

### Robotaxi unit economics: the undisclosed half of the model

| Item | Disclosed? | Figure | What it means | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Authorised fleet, Texas | Yes | 1,051 vehicles at 2026-10-27; Cybercab entered 2026-09-03; Austin hours 06:00-24:00 | A city pilot; unit cost not disclosed | S125, S9 |
| Remote supervision | Partly | Remote operators implicated in crashes | An uncosted cost line | S153 |
| Insurance and liability | No | Not disclosed | Decides whether a paid mile contributes | S9 |
| Revenue per paid mile | No | Robotaxi not broken out of Services and Other | Contribution cannot be computed | S9 |
| Benchmark | Pony.ai | $8.6m Q1 2026 revenue on 1,776 vehicles, $4,800 per vehicle per quarter | At that rate 1,051 cars would produce $5m a quarter | S178 |

None of these cost lines is disclosed.

### Optimus is a research programme with a production line

Tesla began Optimus production in Fremont in Q3 2026 and calls the process "suitable for a commercial product", but discloses no units, cycle times, error rates or customers; independent estimates put 1,000-1,200 units across Fremont and Giga Texas with zero external sales. Figure AI has logged 1,250+ hours at BMW and Agility Robotics 65,000+ hours across nine sites, both with paying customers, so Optimus should carry no revenue in a 12-month model [S99].

Tesla's manufacturing and supervised-data advantages are real and hard to buy, but the priced asset is unsupervised autonomy, which today carries a fatality-linked engineering analysis, one authorising state, a pilot fleet and no disclosed revenue. Confidence is high on filings, medium on driverless scale, low on Optimus and robotaxi unit economics, where disclosure is absent. The disclosures that would move this: Robotaxi revenue, paid trips and cost per trip reported quarterly; a California driverless deployment permit; and dry-electrode cell cost per kWh against purchased cells. If the first and third come good while the engineering analysis closes without a hardware remedy, the option is worth more than a pilot; a recall that restricts the operating domain would remove the revenue bridge.

arguments.markdown:
Tesla's strategy is no longer self-funded, and the filings now say so. With 2026 capital expenditure guided above $20 billion against $15.0 billion of trailing Adjusted EBITDA (Q4 2025 to Q3 2026), Tesla signed three credit agreements totalling $30 billion in September 2026 and states that heightened capital spending "will necessitate additional funding beyond our operating cash flow" [S8]. That sentence, not the robotaxi narrative, is the strategy disclosure that matters for the next twelve months: the autonomy, energy and robotics options are now financed partly with balance-sheet capacity.

### The plan has three pillars and one new capital sink

The stated plan, carried in the 10-K and in the 2025 CEO Performance Award, is to convert a hardware business into an autonomy and robotics business: FSD (Supervised) and Robotaxi, energy storage, and Optimus, funded by a vehicle business that delivered 1.32 million units in the first nine months of 2026 [S10]. What is new is the depth of vertical integration behind it — 225+ MW of training compute, an in-house inference chip, a Samsung foundry collaboration and a company semiconductor fab commissioning equipment in 2027 — which turns a software roadmap into a fixed-cost programme closer to a foundry than to an automaker.

| Milestone | Target date | Status | What it proves | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Robotaxi at commercial scale (1 million in operation, per the 2025 award) | No public date | 300+ Cybercabs claimed in Austin; 1,051 vehicles authorised in Texas at 2026-10-27 | Whether autonomy has revenue at scale | S10, S9, S125 |
| Cybercab start of production | 1H 2026 (stated 2026-01) | Rides began 2026-09-03; 125,000+ capacity listed | Execution on the purpose-built robotaxi | S60, S9 |
| Tesla Semi volume production | 1H 2026 | Volume production began Q3 2026 | Heavy-truck adjacency | S60, S9 |
| Optimus Gen 3 start of production | Before end-2026 (stated 2026-01) | Production began at Fremont in Q3 2026 | Robotics credibility | S60, S9 |
| Megapack 3 and Megablock at Megafactory Houston | 2026 | Texas Megafactory began production Q3 2026 at 50 GWh planned; product-level start not disclosed | Energy as a genuine second engine | S60, S9 |
| Fully dry-electrode 4680 cells | Disclosed as achieved 2026-01 | Both electrodes made in Austin; 40+ GWh Texas capacity | Battery cost advantage | S60 |
| 400 MW of AI training compute | End-2026 | 225+ MW installed at Q3 2026 | Compute self-sufficiency | S9 |
| California driverless deployment permit | No public target | Not held at 2026-10-23; testing permit with driver only | Geographic expansion beyond Texas | S89 |

### The track record is mixed, and the split is informative

Energy and manufacturing promises have largely been kept: Megafactory Texas started production in Q3 2026, Optimus production began in Fremont ahead of the January 2026 target to start before the end of 2026, and 36.0 GWh of storage was deployed in nine months against 46.7 GWh for all of 2025. Autonomy promises have not: the 2025 award still lists "1 million Robotaxis in commercial operation" and "10 million active FSD subscriptions" as unmet operational milestones, against 300+ claimed Cybercabs, 1,051 vehicles authorised in Texas and 1.74 million subscriptions, and none of the 423.7 million shares has been earned because the first tranche also needs $2.0 trillion of market capitalisation plus one operational milestone [S9, S10]. The pattern is that Tesla ships physical products within a quarter or two of plan and ships software-defined promises years late — which is why the robotaxi timeline should be discounted but the Megapack and Semi timelines should not.

### Resources fit the plan only at the low end

Nine-month capex of $13.01 billion against guidance of "in excess of $20 billion" leaves $7.0 billion for the fourth quarter, after a Q2 spike of $5.79 billion; the guidance was cut from "more than $25 billion" in the 10-Q rather than in the shareholder letter. Free cash flow of $1.53 billion in Q3 2026 depended on $2.59 billion of working-capital inflow, and $3.67 billion of equipment and construction spend sat unpaid in liabilities. Against that, $45.45 billion of cash and $30 billion of undrawn facilities mean the plan is affordable — just not self-funded [S8, S102]. The mechanism matters: borrowing to fund a call option on autonomy converts equity risk into refinancing risk, and the return on that borrowing depends on Robotaxi revenue the company does not yet disclose, so the cost of the strategy now appears in interest and covenants rather than in a share count.

| Partner or counterparty | Scope | Signed | Status | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Samsung | US manufacturing of semiconductors for AI inference and training | 2025 | In progress; Austin fab equipment commissioning 2027 | S1, S9 |
| SpaceX (related party) | Megapack purchases; $626m of energy revenue in 9M 2026 | Ongoing | $588m of the $729m receivable for undelivered Megapacks | S8 |
| xAI | Grok in-cabin assistant deployed in Cybercab | 2026 | Live; Tesla holds under 1% of SpaceX after a $2.0bn March 2026 investment | S9, S8 |
| Cell suppliers | Purchased lithium-ion cells for vehicles and storage | Not disclosed | Battery availability remains the limiting factor on vehicle output | S9 |

The related-party lines deserve emphasis. SpaceX bought $626 million of Megapacks in the first nine months of 2026, 7.4% of $8.43 billion of energy revenue, and $588 million of the receivable was billed for units not yet delivered — revenue quality a third-party backlog would not show. Tesla also invested $2.0 billion in SpaceX common stock in March 2026 and holds under 1% of the company [S8]. That is capital allocation and customer concentration inside the second engine, and it means the energy story is more dependent on one related buyer than the order-rate language implies.

### What the second curves are actually worth

Energy is the one adjacency already at scale and profitable: 13.7 GWh deployed in Q3 2026 alone, 50 GWh of new Texas capacity and record order rates, which is why it deserves to be valued as a business with a discount for the related-party share. Robotaxi is an option whose value is capped by permits and by the federal safety file rather than by manufacturing capacity — 300+ claimed Cybercabs is a pilot, and neither trips nor revenue are disclosed inside $4.605 billion of services revenue. Optimus is further still, with zero external sales and no published throughput, and the semiconductor fab adds a foundry's fixed-cost risk to a company already guiding more than $20 billion of capex. Margins carry the bill: Q3 2026 operating income was $718 million on $28.05 billion of revenue, a 2.6% operating margin, while regulatory credits, the highest-margin revenue line, fell from $2.76 billion in 2024 to $1.99 billion in 2025 [S1, S9]. For an investor this is the crux — the plan's returns sit in businesses with no disclosed revenue, while its costs land on a 2.6%-margin income statement.

### What must be true in twelve months

Three things must hold for the strategy to stay credible without new equity: Robotaxi revenue must be disclosed as its own line with paid trips growing outside Texas; capex must land at or below the guided floor with free cash flow positive before working-capital swings; and energy must keep compounding with third-party demand large enough to absorb the new capacity. The signposts are a California driverless deployment permit, a quarterly Robotaxi revenue disclosure, the close or escalation of NHTSA's EA26002, and whether the credit facilities are drawn at all. If all four move positively, the strategy is self-sustaining on debt and the option value is real; if none does, the company is borrowing against a low-margin auto business to fund revenue it cannot yet show, and the right posture is to wait for the Robotaxi line rather than pay for it in advance.

Historically, in developing compensation recommendations for our Chief Executive Officer, the Compensation Committee and Special Committee, as applicable, have sought both to appropriately reward our Chief Executive Officer’s previous and current contributions and to create incentives for our Chief Executive Officer to continue to contribute significantly to successful results in the future. Each of the 2025 CEO Performance Award, the 2018 CEO Performance Award and the performance-based stock option award granted to our Chief Executive Officer in August 2012 (the “ 2012 CEO Performance Award ”) incentivized future performance when granted. The grant of restricted stock to Mr. Musk in August 2025 (“ 2025 CEO Interim Award ”) was intended to retain him in recognition of his inability to exercise the fully earned 2018 CEO Performance Award due to the ongoing litigation then pending before the Delaware Supreme Court (together with its constituent and related litigation, “ Tornetta ”). The Special Committee recognized the lack of meaningful compensation for Mr. Musk since the 2012 CEO Performance Award was last earned in 2017 as well as the continued uncertainty around a resolution in Tornetta and its impact on Mr. Musk’s ability to exercise the 2018 CEO Performance Award, and the Special Committee assessed the possibility of a good-faith payment in recognition of his accomplishments and to honor Tesla’s compensation promises. The 2025 CEO Interim Award was scheduled to vest upon the second anniversary of August 3, 2025, subject to Mr. Musk remaining in continuous service as CEO or as an executive officer responsible for product development or operations (as approved by the Board’s disinterested directors) through such second anniversary. {"content":[{"type":"text","text":"## Funding History & Valuation (funding_valuation, revision 5 by Valuation Analyst, 8,939 characters)
Tesla closes at $399.81 on NasdaqGS on 2026-10-30, a $1,580.4bn market capitalisation and $1,544.2bn enterprise value; on the businesses its filings describe — cars, storage, services — it is worth $139-160bn, or $35-40 a share. The other $1,420-1,441bn, 90-91% of the equity, rests on robotaxi, FSD and Optimus revenue the quarterly report does not yet book, and the buyer pays 103x trailing adjusted EBITDA for the whole. The reported businesses cannot carry the price; the shares are a claim on a multiple, not earnings [S8, S9].

| Metric | Value | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Last price | $399.81 at 2026-10-30 20:00 UTC, NasdaqGS, USD | S11 |
| Market capitalisation | $1,580.4bn on 3,952,648,559 shares | S8, S11 |
| Enterprise value | $1,544.2bn after $36,180m net cash | S8 |
| 52-week close range | $297.38-$498.83, 51% of the way up | S11 |
| Returns | 1M +12.7%, 3M +28.5%, 12M -12.4% against the S&P 500's -0.9%, +1.2%, +10.8% | S11, S20 |
| Liquidity | $13.8bn a day, 20-day average 36.30m shares | S11 |
| Trailing P/E | 439.4x against a peer median of 19.1x | S8, S11, S15 |
| EV/adjusted EBITDA | 103.0x on $14,995m trailing | S9, S11 |
| Free-cash-flow yield | 0.2% on $3,303m trailing | S9, S11 |
| Active FSD subscriptions | 1.74m at 2026-09-30, +67%; company-defined to include 870,000 one-time buyers held in deferred revenue and 870,000 monthly subscribers | S9, S8, S152, S173 |
| Insider activity, 6 months | no purchases; 19 sales of $13.32m, 17 under 10b5-1 plans | S2 |

### The price pays for a multiple, not for earnings

Trailing revenue is $103.6bn, adjusted EBITDA $15.0bn, operating income $3.47bn and free cash flow $3.3bn after $15.4bn of capital expenditure. That is 445x EV/operating income, a 0.2% free-cash-flow yield and 14.9x sales, against 17.3x EV/EBITDA for BYD and 19.1x earnings for General Motors below. The EBITDA the company prefers adds back $4.3bn of stock compensation, up from $2.8bn in FY2025, so 103x becomes 144x before that add-back. One turn is worth $15.0bn: the price is a rating, and a delay in autonomy compresses the rating, not the earnings. The capital structure has added supply, not raised capital: no external equity since the 2010 IPO; the nine months to 2026-09-30 were funded from $14,897m of operating cash flow, $5,834m of debt and $314m of option proceeds, and 202m new shares lifted the count to 3,953m — $80.8bn of new equity at the closing price [S8, S9, S2].

| Event | Date | Amount | Detail | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Shares outstanding | 2025-12-31 to 2026-09-30 | +202m shares | 3,751m to 3,953m, +5.4% | S8 |
| Option and RSU settlements | six months to 2026-09-09 | 304.0m shares delivered, 17.5m withheld | $7.10bn exercise value, $7.09bn withheld for tax | S2 |
| Cash from option exercises | Q3 2026 | $314m | option exercises and other stock issuances | S9 |
| Debt issued | nine months to 2026-09-30 | $5,834m | $4,331m in Q1, $348m in Q2, $1,155m in Q3 | S9 |
| 2025 CEO Performance Award | vote 2025-11-06 | 423,743,904 shares | contingent; every tranche gated from a $2,000bn market capitalisation | S10 |
| Dividends and buybacks | since 2010 | none | no dividend ever declared, no repurchase programme | S1 |

### What the reported businesses are worth

| Method | Inputs | Value | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| Automotive and regulatory credits | $75.0bn trailing revenue at 0.6-0.8x EV/sales, above GM and Ford's multiples | $45-60bn | S9, S15, S17 |
| Energy generation and storage | $12.3bn trailing revenue, 30.2% nine-month gross margin, at 2.5-3.0x sales; CATL earns 19.8x | $31-37bn | S9, S133 |
| Services and other | $16.3bn trailing revenue, +32% year on year, at 1.5x sales | $24bn | S9 |
| Net cash at 2026-09-30 | $45,447m cash and short-term investments less $9,267m debt | $36,180m | S8 |
| SpaceX equity stake | $2,002m bought in Q1 2026 plus $863m unrealised gain | $2,865m | S9 |
| Total, reported businesses | | $139-160bn, $35-40 a share | S8, S9 |
| Residual in the price | $1,580.4bn less the total | $1,420-1,441bn, 90-91% | S8, S11 |

The split matters more than the total. Energy, the best-margin segment at 33.1% gross, is 12% of trailing revenue and fell 16% year on year as Megapack prices fell; services grew 32% and set a record $734m of gross profit. Neither stretches to a trillion dollars at peer multiples. A generous automotive recovery — 10% operating margin on $75bn at 25x — lifts the total to $288bn, $73 a share, and still leaves 82% of the price unexplained [S9].

### What the price requires by 2030

| Multiple applied to enterprise value | Required adjusted EBITDA | Versus $15.0bn trailing | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| 17.3x, BYD's multiple | $89.3bn | 6.0x | S131 |
| 25x | $61.8bn | 4.1x | S131 |
| 40x | $38.6bn | 2.6x | S131 |
| 80x, the multiple management's own $4.0tn tranche implies on $50bn | $19.3bn | 1.3x | S127 |

Inverting the price gives the same answer. The residual $1,441bn, discounted at 10% and valued at 20x 2030 operating income, needs $105bn of 2030 operating income; at 40x, $53bn. At a 25% robotaxi margin and $100,000 of revenue per vehicle-year, that is 2.1-4.2m vehicles by 2030, against 1,051 authorised robotaxis in Texas on 2026-10-27 and 125,000 units of installed Cybercab capacity a year: 17-34 years of factory output and two to four times the one-million-robotaxi milestone the board paired with a $3.5tn market capitalisation [S125, S127]. The ladder is less demanding than the price: the $4.0tn tranche implies 80x, below the 103x the shares carry.

| Company | P/E (TTM) | EV/sales | EV/EBITDA (XBRL basis) | FCF yield | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Tesla | 439.4x | 14.9x | 169.0x | 0.2% | S8, S11 |
| General Motors | 19.1x | n/m | n/m | 19.5% | S15, S16 |
| Ford | n/m | n/m | n/m | 11.3% | S17, S18 |
| Rivian | n/m | 2.6x | n/m | -23.8% | S19 |
| BYD | 21.2x | n/d | 17.3x | n/d | S132, S131 |
| CATL | 19.8x | n/d | n/d | n/d | S133 |
| Fluence Energy | n/m | n/m | n/m | -14.6% | S61, S62 |

Tesla's own history agrees. The P/E was 34.0x at the end of 2022, 57.8x in 2023, 204.6x in 2024 and 420.8x in 2025 as diluted EPS fell from $4.90 to $1.08, and is 439.4x now; EV/sales, the steadier measure, is 14.9x inside a 14.7-16.5x band, because revenue doubled while the shares returned -0.8% over five years. A 4.93% ten-year Treasury yield, a VIX at its 77th percentile and a 326bp high-yield spread make a 439x earnings multiple harder to hold than it was in 2021 [S11, S12, S22].

### Consensus, guidance and the dates that reset the multiple

Consensus is Hold — 24 buy, 1 strong buy, 20 hold and 3 sell across 48 firms — with an average target of $408.61, 2.2% above the close; an 83-analyst sample gives $442.13, 10.6% above. Targets run from Jefferies at $400 to RBC at $480, and Q3 2026 adjusted EPS was $0.48 against $0.45 expected. Tesla gives no numeric revenue or EPS guidance, promises only "hardware-related profits accompanied by an acceleration of SI, software and fleet-based profits", and cut capital expenditure to $20bn from more than $25bn. The dates that reset the multiple are the fourth-quarter 2026 results in the last week of January 2027, on the pattern of the FY2025 10-K filed 2026-01-29, the first Cybercab deployment outside Austin, and the SpaceX committee process. The counter-argument is that the premium buys an option that is maturing: 1.74m active FSD subscriptions, an attach rate above 75% of North American deliveries, nearly 2m unsupervised Robotaxi miles, and a fleet that grew from 739 to 1,051 vehicles in eighteen days. The 1.74m is company-sourced, not a recurring-revenue base: free trials are excluded and the CFO put half the paid base on monthly plans on 2026-10-21, so 870,000 buyers paid once — cash held in $4.08bn of deferred revenue that includes FSD — and 870,000 pay $99 a month. The "approaching $1 billion" FSD run-rate is therefore arithmetic on the monthly half at US list, $1.03bn a year, not audited revenue, under 1% of the $103.6bn top line, a ceiling before regional pricing and churn. If robotaxi unit economics are proven in 2027, 103x on today's EBITDA is a discount to what the business would then earn. The weak version fails — energy caps at $37bn — and no company in the peer table pairs a 30% energy gross margin with 32% services growth above 30x earnings. Confidence in the arithmetic is high, in the multiple's durability low, because durability rests on evidence the company has not disclosed. For a buyer at $399.81 the implication is that the return depends on a re-rating that robotaxi disclosure would have to earn, while the downside is carried by the multiple; on this arithmetic there is no margin of safety in the price, and the three questions that would change that are revenue per robotaxi-week in Austin, the energy segment's operating margin, and whether a capital-return policy ever replaces permanent dilution [S128, S9, S8, S152, S173, S125]."}],"isError":false}

{"content":[{"type":"text","text":"## Investment Potential & Thesis (thesis, revision 4 by Lead Analyst, 8,785 characters)
Tesla is the industry's strongest capability attached to its most expensive claim on it. At $399.81 on 2026-10-30 the equity is capitalised at $1,580.4bn on $3.47bn of trailing operating income, while the businesses the filings describe — cars, storage and services — are worth $139-160bn, or $35-40 a share, on peer multiples. The judgement is Sell, and it is a de-rating call rather than a liquidation call: the reported value is a floor of $35-50 a share, the twelve-month range runs from $64 in a full de-rating to $506.05 at the award gate, and 90-91% of the price is an option on revenue the quarterly report does not book. If the need is real — 23.0m electric units in 2026, 28% of global light-vehicle sales — and if the capability is defensible — 1.74m active FSD subscriptions and a 14.8% ex-refund storage gross margin against Fluence's 13.1% fiscal-2025 figure — then the economics still do not scale. The residual $1,420-1,441bn needs $105bn of 2030 operating income at 20x, or 2.1-4.2m robotaxis at a 25% margin, against 1,051 authorised vehicles in Texas on 2026-10-27 and 125,000 units of annual Cybercab capacity. At $399.81 the case is attractive only if the price falls toward the base case [S8, S9, S11, S125, S127, S137, S61].

Consensus is Hold, not Sell: 24 buy, 1 strong buy, 20 hold and 3 sell across 48 firms, with an average target of $408.61, 2.2% above the close. The market prices autonomy as a 2028 cash flow, while the record shows 2.0m cumulative unsupervised Robotaxi miles — 0.9% of the 220.6m rider-only miles Waymo had logged through March 2026 — a California permit that allows testing with a safety driver and nothing driverless, and a Texas service of 1,051 vehicles against Waymo's 500,000 paid rides a week across ten cities [S128, S151, S142, S89]. A 2.2% consensus upside and a -33.5% base case are two prices for the same option.

The mechanism is the multiple, not the earnings. Tesla trades at 103x trailing adjusted EBITDA of $14,995m and 439.4x earnings, against a peer median of 19.1x and BYD's 17.3x. The operating margin was 2.6% in Q3 2026, interest income was 46.5% of pre-tax profit, nine-month free cash flow of $1,883m was smaller than the $3,868m payables build that produced it, and a 5.5% ROIC sits 57bp above a 4.93% ten-year Treasury [S11, S131, S15, S9, S8, S22]. A delay in autonomy compresses the rating, not the earnings, so the drawdown does not require a bad quarter.

The base case is built from the trailing number, not from a forecast. Energy is the best business, but its Q3 2026 gross margin of 33.1% contains $526m of IEEPA tariff refunds and warranty true-ups; ex-refund it is about $428m on $2,881m of revenue, or 14.8%, against Fluence's 13.1% fiscal 2025 and 5.1% June quarter, and energy is 12% of revenue, down 16% year on year. Earnings quality scores 3 because nine-month free cash flow of $1,883m is smaller than the $3,868m payables build, interest income was 46.5% of Q3 2026 pre-tax profit, and a 5.5% ROIC sits 57bp above a 4.93% ten-year Treasury. The balance sheet is the one dimension above neutral at 6: $36,180m of net cash and $30.0bn of undrawn facilities fund the $20bn capex plan without equity. Management and governance scores 3: the board committed $2.0bn to xAI after a shareholder measure against it drew 1.06bn votes to 916.3m, the compensation committee chair also sits on SpaceX's board, and the 423,743,904-share award is gated from a $2,000bn market capitalisation, so dilution arrives only in up states. Catalysts and exit score 4 because a listed SpaceX at $2.01tn, with both boards' committees and a 20-35% broker premium, implies $480-540 a share, a real exit that substitutes for rather than adds to the bull case. ESG and regulatory licence score 4: automotive credits fell to $1,993m in FY2025 from $2,763m, NHTSA's EA26002 covers 3,203,754 vehicles, and the NLRB dismissed its Buffalo complaint on 2026-10-29 [S8, S9, S22, S61, S10, S96, S154].

Market growth scores 4 and competitive position 5. The pools that pay Tesla's bills are shrinking by policy in the US and China, while the growing pool, Europe and grid storage, is smaller and priced per unit; the company holds the largest share of America's electric-vehicle market yet is fourth in China, and its autonomy mileage is a small fraction of the incumbent's. The score is not lower because Tesla still sets the US price and builds storage at a lower cost than listed integrators; it is not higher because none of those advantages compounds into the revenue line the price requires. The counter-evidence is that energy and services are compounding and the balance sheet is net cash, which is why this is a de-rating call rather than a solvency call.

The recommendation does not change in any branch, only on an event rather than a lower price. The report uses one set: bull 30% — 15% autonomy proof and 15% a SpaceX combination — at $506.05, +26.6%; base 40% at $266, -33.5%, which is 70x on $14.5bn of adjusted EBITDA plus $36.18bn of net cash; bear 22% at $156, -61%; and a full de-rating at 8%, $64-101, -79%. The expected twelve-month return is -25.2%. The base-case EBITDA is the trailing $14,995m less $526m of Q3 one-offs, held at $14.5bn on an energy margin of 14-18%; the bull price is not an EBITDA output at all, because $506.05 across 3,952.6m shares is the $2,000bn award gate. A merger announced at a premium would end the standalone short at the exchange ratio; a disclosed robotaxi revenue line with positive contribution, or a California driverless deployment entry, would move autonomy into the valuation and force a re-underwrite [S8, S9, S127, S154].

{"content":[{"type":"text","text":"## Executive Briefing (executive_summary, revision 5 by Lead Analyst, 6,852 characters)
Tesla closed at $399.81 on 2026-10-30, a $1,580.4bn market capitalisation, 12.7% higher over the past month — a window that includes the 2026-10-21 third-quarter report — and 28.5% higher over three months, yet still 12.4% lower over twelve months against the S&P 500's 10.8% gain [S11, S20]. The index backdrop is firm: the S&P 500 sits at 7,580.07, up 10.7% year to date and 3.4% below its 52-week high, with the Nasdaq 8.2% below its own. The rates backdrop is not: the VIX is 19.42, in its 77th percentile, the ten-year Treasury yields 4.93% and high-yield spreads are 326bp. Energy leads the sector table by 17.6 points over three months against technology's 2.4, and consumer discretionary trails the index.

The verdict is Sell, with zero long exposure and, at most, a capped short; the composite score is 3.8 out of 10. One distribution governs the report: bull 30%, split between autonomy proof and a SpaceX combination, at $506.05; base 40% at $266, -33.5%; bear 22% at $156, -61%; and a full de-rating at 8%, from $64 to $101, for an expected twelve-month return of -25.2%. That is a de-rating call rather than a liquidation call: the reported car, storage and services businesses are worth $139-160bn, or $35-40 a share, against the $1,580.4bn capitalisation, and 90-91% of the equity is an option on autonomy revenue the filings do not book [S8, S9].

The positives are real, and they are why this is a de-rating call rather than a liquidation call. Energy earns a storage gross margin roughly in line with Fluence's fiscal 2025 once the third-quarter tariff refunds are stripped out — 14.8% against 13.1% — the balance sheet holds net cash alongside large undrawn facilities, the US electric-vehicle franchise still sets the price, and a listed SpaceX with both boards' committees offers a premium-bearing exit. Those cards are in the briefing table; none of them changes what the buyer pays today [S9, S61].

The risks to the call are as specific as the thesis. An announced combination at a premium would gap the shares above the bull case, a California deployment permit plus a robotaxi revenue line would turn the option into cash flow, and a recall from the open engineering analysis would cut the option the other way. Confidence is high in the arithmetic of value and low in the durability of the multiple; the diligence that would settle the second is listed below.

Consensus is Hold, with an average target within a rounding error of the price, so the view here is deliberately non-consensus: the market capitalises the autonomy option while this call prices it at zero until a revenue line is disclosed. If no line appears inside the year, the base and bear cases carry the return, and the buyer of the shares is paid nothing to wait.

The one question that decides the case is robotaxi revenue per vehicle-week in Texas and whether it is positive at the contribution level after insurance, depreciation and remote supervision. The next diligence actions are the fourth-quarter report, the California DMV deployment list, the NHTSA engineering-analysis resolution and the SpaceX exchange ratio; the conditions for investing are a disclosed robotaxi revenue line with positive contribution, a driverless deployment permit, an energy gross margin that holds without tariff refunds, and capex inside the plan with positive free cash flow before working capital. ### The price pays for a multiple, not for earnings

Trailing revenue is $103.6bn, adjusted EBITDA $15.0bn, operating income $3.47bn and free cash flow $3.3bn after $15.4bn of capital expenditure. That is 445x EV/operating income, a 0.2% free-cash-flow yield and 14.9x sales, against 17.3x EV/EBITDA for BYD and 19.1x earnings for General Motors below. The EBITDA the company prefers adds back $4.3bn of stock compensation, up from $2.8bn in FY2025, so 103x becomes 144x before that add-back. One turn is worth $15.0bn: the price is a rating, and a delay in autonomy compresses the rating, not the earnings. The capital structure has added supply, not raised capital: no external equity since the 2010 IPO; the nine months to 2026-09-30 were funded from $14,897m of operating cash flow, $5,834m of debt and $314m of option proceeds, and 202m new shares lifted the count to 3,953m — $80.8bn of new equity at the closing price [S8, S9, S2].

At a 25% robotaxi margin and $100,000 of revenue per vehicle-year, that is 2.1-4.2m vehicles by 2030, against 1,051 authorised robotaxis in Texas on 2026-10-27 and 125,000 units of installed Cybercab capacity a year: 17-34 years of factory output and two to four times the one-million-robotaxi milestone the board paired with a $3.5tn market capitalisation [S125, S127]. The P/E was 34.0x at the end of 2022, 57.8x in 2023, 204.6x in 2024 and 420.8x in 2025 as diluted EPS fell from $4.90 to $1.08, and is 439.4x now; EV/sales, the steadier measure, is 14.9x inside a 14.7-16.5x band, because revenue doubled while the shares returned -0.8% over five years. A 4.93% ten-year Treasury yield, a VIX at its 77th percentile and a 326bp high-yield spread make a 439x earnings multiple harder to hold than it was in 2021 [S11, S12, S22].

### Consensus, guidance and the dates that reset the multiple

Consensus is Hold — 24 buy, 1 strong buy, 20 hold and 3 sell across 48 firms — with an average target of $408.61, 2.2% above the close; an 83-analyst sample gives $442.13, 10.6% above. Targets run from Jefferies at $400 to RBC at $480, and Q3 2026 adjusted EPS was $0.48 against $0.45 expected. Tesla gives no numeric revenue or EPS guidance, promises only "hardware-related profits accompanied by an acceleration of SI, software and fleet-based profits", and cut capital expenditure to $20bn from more than $25bn. The dates that reset the multiple are the fourth-quarter 2026 results in the last week of January 2027, on the pattern of the FY2025 10-K filed 2026-01-29, the first Cybercab deployment outside Austin, and the SpaceX committee process. The counter-argument is that the premium buys an option that is maturing: 1.74m active FSD subscriptions, an attach rate above 75% of North American deliveries, nearly 2m unsupervised Robotaxi miles, and a fleet that grew from 739 to 1,051 vehicles in eighteen days. The 1.74m is company-sourced, not a recurring-revenue base: free trials are excluded and the CFO put half the paid base on monthly plans on 2026-10-21, so 870,000 buyers paid once — cash held in $4.08bn of deferred revenue that includes FSD — and 870,000 pay $99 a month. The "approaching $1 billion" FSD run-rate is therefore arithmetic on the monthly half at US list, $1.03bn a year, not audited revenue, under 1% of the $103.6bn top line, a ceiling before regional pricing and churn. If robotaxi unit economics are proven in 2027, 103x on today's EBITDA is a discount to what the business would then earn. The weak version fails — energy caps at $37bn — and no company in the peer table pairs a 30% energy gross margin with 32% services growth above 30x earnings. Confidence in the arithmetic is high, in the multiple's durability low, because durability rests on evidence the company has not disclosed. For a buyer at $399.81 the implication is that the return depends on a re-rating that robotaxi disclosure would have to earn, while the downside is carried by the multiple; on this arithmetic there is no margin of safety in the price, and the three questions that would change that are revenue per robotaxi-week in Austin, the energy segment's operating margin, and whether a capital-return policy ever replaces permanent dilution [S128, S9, S8, S152, S173, S125]."}],"isError":false}

Normalising those refunds puts trailing adjusted EBITDA at $14,469M, and at 70x that plus net cash the report's 40% base case is $266 a share [S8, S12, S11].

### Revenue recovered, operating profit did not

| Line item ($M unless stated) | FY2023 | FY2024 | FY2025 | Q3 2026 | 9M 2026 | TTM to 2026-09-30 | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Revenue | 96,773 | 97,690 | 94,827 | 28,046 | 78,669 | 103,570 | S12, S13, S1, S8 |
| Gross profit | 17,660 | 17,450 | 17,094 | 5,494 | 14,965 | 19,974 | S12, S13, S1, S8 |
| Research and development | 3,969 | 4,540 | 6,411 | 2,761 | 7,078 | 8,861 | S12, S13, S1, S8 |
| Selling, general and administrative | 4,800 | 5,150 | 5,834 | 2,015 | 5,830 | 7,485 | S12, S13, S1, S8 |
| Operating income | 8,891 | 7,076 | 4,355 | 718 | 2,057 | 3,466 | S12, S13, S1, S8 |
| Net income | 14,997 | 7,091 | 3,794 | 787 | 2,378 | 3,218 | S12, S13, S1, S8 |
| Diluted EPS ($) | 4.30 | 2.04 | 1.08 | 0.22 | 0.67 | 0.91 | S12, S13, S1, S8 |
| Operating cash flow | 13,256 | 14,923 | 14,747 | 6,263 | 14,897 | 18,710 | S12, S13, S1, S8 |
| Capital expenditure | 8,898 | 11,339 | 8,527 | 4,732 | 13,014 | 15,407 | S12, S13, S1, S8 |
| Free cash flow | 4,358 | 3,584 | 6,220 | 1,531 | 1,883 | 3,296 | S12, S13, S1, S8 |

Revenue fell for two years before the 2026 rebound while operating income fell throughout, from $8,891M in FY2023 to $3,466M trailing, because research and development rose from $3,969M to $8,861M and selling and administrative cost from $4,800M to $7,485M against gross profit that stayed between $17.1B and $20.0B. Q3 2026 revenue was $28,046M, gross profit $5,494M (19.6%), operating income $718M (2.6%), net income $787M and diluted EPS $0.22, on deliveries down 2% to 486,532 from 497,099, with price, mix and FX carrying the top line. GAAP net income of $787M compared with non-GAAP of $1,697M, and diluted EPS of $0.22 with $0.48. The quarter also absorbed a $475M reversal of previously recognised regulatory credit revenue, so the 2.6% operating margin understates the underlying figure by 1.7 points [S12, S13, S1, S8].

### Free cash flow is a payables loan and a capex pause

Nine-month operating cash flow of $14,897M exceeded the $13,014M of capital expenditure to leave $1,883M of free cash flow, against $6,220M for FY2025. Management attributes $3.51 billion of the $3.96 billion year-on-year operating-cash-flow increase to working capital, and in Q3 2026 alone free cash flow of $1,531M rested on a $2,590M working-capital inflow, of which accounts payable supplied $1,920M and accrued liabilities $1,950M; stripping it out, quarterly free cash flow was -$1,059M, and $3,670M of capex sat in liabilities at 2026-09-30. Across nine months, payables rose $3,868M to $17,239M and the cash conversion cycle fell to 2.6 days from 13.0, so without the payables build nine-month free cash flow would have been -$1,985M. Capex nearly doubled from $6,134M a year earlier and the 2026 plan was restated between filings — "in excess of $25 billion" in July 2026, "in excess of $20 billion" in October 2026 — leaving full-year 2026 free cash flow between -$1,290M and +$1,160M depending on whether Q4 operating cash flow matches Q4 2025's $3,813M or Q3 2026's $6,263M [S8, S9, S83, S102].

### The balance sheet carries the plan; the capital does not earn its keep

| Metric | FY2023 | FY2024 | FY2025 | TTM to 2026-09-30 | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Return on invested capital | 28.3% | 13.7% | 7.0% | 5.5% | S12, S13, S1, S8 |
| Return on equity | 27.9% | 10.5% | 4.9% | 3.8% | S12, S13, S1, S8 |
| Days sales outstanding | 13.2 | 16.5 | 17.6 | 16.3 | S12, S13, S1, S8 |
| Days inventory outstanding | 62.9 | 54.7 | 58.2 | 61.5 | S12, S13, S1, S8 |
| Days payables outstanding | 66.6 | 56.7 | 62.8 | 75.3 | S12, S13, S1, S8 |
| Cash conversion cycle (days) | 9.5 | 14.4 | 13.0 | 2.6 | S12, S13, S1, S8 |
| Interest coverage | 56.99x | 20.22x | 12.88x | 9.96x | S12, S13, S1, S8 |
| Stock-based compensation / revenue | 1.9% | 2.0% | 3.0% | 4.2% | S12, S13, S1, S8 |
| Net cash | 24,437 | 28,685 | 35,906 | 36,180 | S12, S13, S1, S8 |

Cash of $17,853M and short-term investments of $27,594M against $9,267M of debt gave $36,180M of net cash at 2026-09-30, and three credit agreements signed in September 2026 lifted unused committed facilities to $30.00B from $6.43B at 2025-12-31, so the $20B capex year is funded several times over without equity. The obligations outside the debt line matter more: $7,955M of minimum lease payments at 2025-12-31, of which $1,320M falls due within twelve months; an accrued warranty reserve of $7,414M that grew 20.9% in nine months against 10% delivery growth; and $7,055M of deferred revenue. Returns have fallen faster than margins: return on invested capital went from 28.3% in FY2023 to 13.7%, 7.0% and 5.5% trailing; that 5.5% compares with a 4.93% ten-year Treasury yield on 2026-10-30, leaving 57 basis points for equity risk. The capex record explains it: $41,778M spent in FY2023 through the first nine months of 2026 against a $5,425M fall in operating income over the same span, an incremental return that is negative at group level. Nothing has been returned to shareholders: no dividend or repurchase from FY2021 to Q3 2026, while $2,000M went into the xAI investment, converted into SpaceX Class A stock in March 2026 [S8, S1, S10, S115, S104].

### The EBITDA bridge and the price it supports

| Adjusted EBITDA bridge, $M | Value | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Q4 2025 | 4,154 | S9 |
| Q1 2026 | 3,668 | S9 |
| Q2 2026 | 3,273 | S9 |
| Q3 2026 | 3,900 | S9 |
| Trailing twelve months | 14,995 | S9 |
| Less Q3 2026 IEEPA energy refund | (526) | S8 |
| Normalised trailing | 14,469 | S8, S9 (derived) |
| Base case: held flat, no credit recovery, no robotaxi line, energy at 15% | 14,500 | S8, S9 (derived) |

Trailing adjusted EBITDA of $14,995M is the sum of four quarters; subtracting the $526M Q3 2026 IEEPA energy refund gives $14,469M, held at $14.5bn in the base case and 12 points of energy margin below the old 27% midpoint on $12.3bn of trailing energy revenue. The bull case's $506.05 is not an EBITDA output: 3,952.6M shares × $506.05 = $2,000bn, exactly the first market-capitalisation gate of the 2025 CEO award, and 131 times the $15.3bn of EBITDA the same case assumes. A 70x multiple on $14.5bn plus $36.18bn of net cash gives $266, the 40% base case; the report's distribution — 30% bull at $506.05, 40% base at $266, 22% bear at $156 and 8% full de-rating at $64-101 — produces a -25.2% expected return [S9, S8, S10].

### What flatters the number, and what would change it

Interest income of $1,301M was 42.9% of nine-month pre-tax income and $445M was 46.5% of the Q3 2026 figure, against 17.5% in FY2024. Stock-based compensation of $3,346M in nine months is 4.3% of revenue and the main reason non-GAAP profit more than doubles GAAP profit. Two share bases are in play: EPS uses 3,541M diluted weighted-average shares (3,240M basic plus 301M options and RSUs), not the 3,952,648,559 issued at 2026-09-30 used for market capitalisation; the 710M gap is 423.7M unearned 2025 award shares and 286.4M unvested 2018 restricted shares already inside the issued count, so earning or vesting them adds no new shares. Warranty adjustments flattered automotive cost while the warranty reserve rose 20.9%. Sensitivity: a point of ex-credit automotive margin is worth $800M on $80,000M of revenue, 6.4 times a point of energy margin at $12,300M, and each $1B of capex is $1B of free cash flow. The $1.5bn cut from the $16.0bn base is 12 points of energy margin on $12.3bn of trailing revenue (27% to 15%); at 14-18% energy margin, $14.5bn of adjusted EBITDA and $20B of capex, free cash flow is roughly $0 to +$0.5bn, not the $2.0bn the 30% energy assumption implied. Capex moves the outcome most: $5B in a single restatement between July and October 2026, more than six points of automotive margin. The diligence question is 2027 capex and whether the payables build reflects renegotiated terms or deferred payments [S8, S83, S1, S117, S102, S10].

::: info danger
The most serious red flag is the composition of free cash flow: nine-month free cash flow is smaller than the rise in payables that produced it, capex was re-scoped in the same quarter that new credit lines were arranged, and the cash balance generating 42.9% of nine-month pre-tax profit is doing more work than the operating business. Reported free cash flow is a ceiling, not a run-rate.
:::
