sources.title: IEA, Global EV Outlook 2026 (released 2026-05-20)
sources.claims: Global electric car sales expected to reach 23 million units in 2026, 28% of total car sales (2025: 20+ million, one in four new cars); Europe poised for the largest growth among major markets with sales up ~20% in 2026 so that one in three cars sold is electric; with existing policies EVs reach about half of global car sales by 2035. Provides the top-down TAM for Tesla's vehicle market (23M/0.28 implies ~82M global car sales in 2026).
sources.claims_weakened: The 2026 global figure is an estimate built on Q1 2026 trends and country submissions; it masks a US contraction, so global growth depends on China/Europe and exports.

sources.title: CnEVPost, China September NEV retail sales fall 16.7% as penetration hits record 67%, CPCA data (2026-10-12)
sources.claims: China passenger vehicle retail, September 2026 (CPCA): NEV retail 1.084 million (-16.7% YoY, ninth consecutive decline), 9M 7.758 million (-12.8%); BEV retail 765,000 (-7.38%), PHEV 232,000 (-35.56%), EREV 88,000 (-19.27%); NEV penetration record 67.0% of PV retail; total PV retail 1.618 million (-28.0%), 9M 13.33 million (-21.7%); NEV wholesale 1.666 million (+11.3%), BEV wholesale 1.126 million (+18.3%); NEV exports 558,000 (+163.5%), 9M 3.887 million (+138.8%). China NEV retail by brand, Sept 2026: BYD 246,816; Geely 119,682; Leapmotor 78,202; Tesla 64,837; Changan 61,732; SAIC-GM-Wuling 54,810; Chery 46,860; SAIC PV 40,280; Xiaomi 40,015; HIMA 37,490; Nio 37,231; GWM 32,048; Li Auto 31,817; Xpeng 30,599.
sources.claims_weakened: Contradicts the "China EV market compounds forever" view: NEV retail has fallen YoY for nine months, PHEV/EREV demand collapsed (-35.6%/-19.3%) while BEV wholesale still grew on exports; Tesla is only the fourth-largest NEV brand by retail in China.

sources.title: Cox Automotive / Kelley Blue Book, Q1 2026 EV sales report commentary
sources.claims: US EV sales Q1 2026: 216,399 units, down 27% year on year and 7.8% below Q4 2025 (which was down 36% YoY), the first full quarter after the $7,500 federal EV tax credit expired on 2025-09-30; Tesla took 54.2% of US EV sales in the quarter.
sources.claims_weakened: Shows the US market contracted by more than a quarter once the credit ended, so any Tesla US volume is being won inside a shrinking pool.

sources.title: ACEA, New car registrations: +5.7% in September 2026 year-to-date; battery-electric 22.7% market share (2026-10-22)
sources.claims: EU passenger car registrations January-September 2026: total market +5.7% year to date; BEV 1,931,465 units, 22.7% share (16.1% a year earlier); PHEV 860,257 units, 10.1%; HEV 3,090,530 units, 36.3%; petrol share 21.2% (27.7%), diesel 7.1% (9.3%); petrol+diesel 28.2% vs 36.9%. France BEV +79.1%, Germany +58.1%, Denmark +40.3%, Belgium +15.7%.
sources.claims_weakened: EU BEV growth is subsidy-supported ("buyer support measures") and the market total is propped up by PHEV (+10.1%); the Annex manufacturer table was not machine-readable, so Tesla's own EU registration count is not in this record.

sources.title: BloombergNEF Energy Storage Market Outlook 2026, via Energy-Storage.news
sources.claims: Global non-pumped-hydro energy storage: 112 GW installed in 2025 (+48% YoY); BNEF forecasts 158 GW / 459 GWh in 2026 (+41% in GW, +45% per the H2 2026 outlook), growth led by China and the US with India 26x and Australia nearly doubling; 3.1 TW cumulative by 2036. Gives the storage TAM in GWh to compare with Tesla's 36.0 GWh deployed in 9M 2026.
sources.claims_weakened: Notes policy mandates and record-low costs as drivers, i.e. part of storage demand is policy-created; the same source implies 2026 growth decelerating from 48% to 41-45%.

sources.title: TechCrunch, Waymo's skyrocketing ridership in one chart (2026-03-27)
sources.claims: Waymo was providing 500,000 paid robotaxi rides per week across 10 US cities as of 2026-03-27, roughly double April 2025, with about 4 million rider-only miles per week and roughly 3,000 vehicles; expansion to Miami, Atlanta, Washington DC and Tokyo during 2026. Sets the current scale of the only scaled paid robotaxi operator.
sources.claims_weakened: Waymo's ride count is company-reported and unaudited; it shows the paid robotaxi market today is a Waymo market, and Tesla's disclosed metric is cumulative unsupervised miles, not rides.

sources.title: MarketsandMarkets, Robotaxi Market worth $45.7 billion by 2030
sources.claims: Robotaxi market projected at USD 45.7 billion by 2030 from USD 0.4 billion in 2023 (91.8% CAGR), with Asia Pacific expected to be the largest market; used as the high end of the third-party TAM range.
sources.claims_weakened: A 91.8% CAGR implies a market 100x larger in seven years; against ~500,000 Waymo paid rides a week in 2026 the 2030 figure requires a fleet and regulatory build-out that no regulator has yet authorised.

sources.title: The Business Research Company, RoboTaxi Global Market Report 2026
sources.claims: Robotaxi market sized at USD 3.49 billion in 2025 growing to USD 5.5 billion in 2026 (57.4% CAGR), from a commercial research firm; used as the low end of third-party robotaxi TAM estimates against MarketsandMarkets' USD 45.7 billion by 2030.
sources.claims_weakened: Vendor research estimates of this market span more than 20x for 2030 (USD 27-204 billion across publishers), so none can carry a valuation; the bottom-up fare-based estimate is the more reliable anchor.

sources.title: TeslaNorth, Tesla still sells over half of America's EVs (2026-10-13), citing Cox Automotive/KBB Q3 2026 EV report
sources.claims: US EV sales Q3 2026: 266,630 units, +7.7% vs Q2 2026 and the strongest quarter in a year; Tesla sold an estimated 144,094 US EVs in Q3 2026 for 54% share, with Tesla's own US volume down almost 20% year on year, per Cox Automotive/Kelley Blue Book data; EVs were 6.4% of all US new-vehicle sales in Q3 2026. Year to date through September 2026 Tesla's 386,194 US deliveries were 52.9% of a US EV market that fell 30.3%, with Tesla down 14.4%.
sources.claims_weakened: Second-hand reporting of Cox data; it shows Tesla's US share rising to 54-59% while its absolute US volume falls, i.e. share gains inside a market that shrank by 30%, which is not a growth signal.

sources.title: CarNewsChina, Chinese NEV sales rankings in September 2026 (2026-10-01), with BYD, Xiaomi, Nio, Li Auto, Zeekr volumes
sources.claims: BYD September 2026: 456,713 passenger cars sold globally, of which 273,143 BEV and 183,570 PHEV; 180,700 exported; January-September 2026 cumulative 3,078,490 units. Confirms BYD's volume is 2.3x Tesla's 9M 2026 deliveries of 1,324,681 and that roughly 40% of BYD sales are plug-in hybrids, which compete with Tesla only partially.
sources.claims_weakened: BYD's BEV-only volume (273,143 in September) is closer to Tesla's global monthly run-rate, so the headline 2.3x gap overstates the direct BEV competition; BYD's domestic retail fell 13% YoY in September per the same reporting cycle.

sources.title: electrive, BEV registrations rose sharply across Europe in September (2026-10-22), citing ACEA
sources.claims: EU BEV registrations in September 2026 were 290,117, up 72.9% year on year, a 29.9% share of new EU car registrations for the month, per ACEA data; September was the first month in which BEV overtook petrol as the EU's largest powertrain.
sources.claims_weakened: A single month at 29.9% against a 22.7% year-to-date average shows EU demand is quarter-end and incentive sensitive, so run-rate extrapolation overstates the trend.

sources.title: Reuters, EU drops 2035 combustion engine ban as global EV shift faces reset (2025-12-16)
sources.claims: European Commission proposed on 2025-12-16 to drop the EU's effective 2035 ban on new combustion-engine cars, replacing the 100% CO2 reduction with a 90% tailpipe cut while keeping hybrids, e-fuels and some combustion engines possible after 2035; the file moved to Parliament and Council, with an April 2026 Parliament draft report proposing further changes and environment ministers still split. Establishes that the EU regulatory floor under BEV demand is being renegotiated through 2026-2027.
sources.claims_weakened: A softened 2035 target weakens the long-dated EU BEV demand backstop and supports hybrid-heavy mixes; it does not remove the 2025-2027 CO2 step that is currently driving EU BEV share from 16.1% to 22.7%.

sources.title: AInvest, BYD's strong exports counter weak domestic sales in September (2026-10), media calculation of BYD gross margin by region
sources.claims: BYD gross margin split reported for 2025: overseas gross margin 19.46% versus domestic 16.66%, with exports reaching 39% of September 2026 sales and domestic sales down 13% YoY; used only as a directional indicator that China-market pricing is harsher than export pricing for the largest Chinese EV maker.
sources.claims_weakened: A media calculation, not read from BYD's HKEX filing; BYD's segment definitions and the 2025 period make it not strictly comparable with Tesla's 18.5% Q3 2026 automotive gross margin.

sources.title: The Detroit News, European sales rebound offsets weaker demand for Tesla in U.S., China (2026-10-02)
sources.claims: Tesla's Q3 2026 deliveries of 486,532 (down 2% YoY) beat estimates because European sales recovered from a 2025 slump and offset weaker demand in the US and China; Berlin posted record production. Indicates Tesla's 2026 regional pattern is Europe up, US and China down.
sources.claims_weakened: A European rebound off a weak 2025 base does not mean Tesla is gaining European share: ACEA shows the EU BEV market itself grew far faster, so Tesla can grow units and still lose share.

sources.title: Axis Intelligence: Waymo statistics 2026 - rides, revenue, safety and fleet data
sources.claims: Waymo logged 220.6m rider-only miles by March 2026, was running about 500,000 paid rides a week, had annualised revenue of $355m as of February 2026 and an average San Francisco fare of $19.69 in Q4 2025-Q1 2026, and was valued at $126bn post-money in its February 2026 round. Waymo's 500k weekly rides imply roughly 26m rides a year, the base for the paid-robotaxi market size.
sources.claims_weakened: Corrects the 170m+ rider-only miles in the thesis to 220.6m by March 2026, which widens Tesla's verified mileage gap to about 0.9% of Waymo's; the $19.69 average fare supports the $0.3-0.5bn paid-market estimate rather than a larger one.

sources.title: Tech Insider: Tesla FSD subscriptions 1.74m vs $1bn run rate
sources.claims: Tesla said on 2026-10-21 that active FSD subscriptions reached 1.74m and the business is approaching a $1bn annual run rate; the count includes upfront buyers as well as monthly subscribers, and the CFO said over 1.7m paid customers with half on subscriptions, implying about $1.03bn at $99 a month. FSD was in more than 75% of new North American deliveries; a $1bn run rate is under 1% of revenue.
sources.claims_weakened: Weakens the bull case's 1.74m subscription evidence: half the base is one-time upfront purchases, FSD revenue is under 1% of the top line, and no standalone FSD revenue or churn is disclosed, so the autonomy-at-zero SOTP is only ~$20bn too harsh, not $1tn.

sources.title: Electrek: Tesla remote operators keep crashing its 'Robotaxis', data shows
sources.claims: Tesla has 36 unique Robotaxi incident reports in NHTSA Standing General Order data; five remote takeovers appear in the crash data and all five ended in a collision, in Dallas and Austin in August 2026. Waymo told Senator Ed Markey in February 2026 it has not used remote driving where a human performs the dynamic driving task. Tesla does not disclose how often remote operators intervene, so no intervention rate can be calculated.
sources.claims_weakened: Weakens the 2.0m unsupervised-mileage claim as evidence of a scalable driverless system; adds an undisclosed teleoperation cost and a 5-for-5 remote-takeover collision record to robotaxi unit economics.

sources.title: Univest: Tesla SpaceX merger - special committees, vote and exchange ratio
sources.claims: On 2026-10-20 Tesla closed at $373.71 (market value $1.48tn) and SpaceX at $147.79 ($2.01tn), so SpaceX trades as a listed security; both boards formed independent special committees, Musk is conflicted and no terms or exchange ratio are agreed. Tesla holders would own about 42% of a combined company at market parity and 47-50% with a 20-35% premium; RBC and JPMorgan expect a 20-35% premium for Tesla holders; approval needs 50% of all Tesla shares outstanding and the 2026-12-03 annual meeting carries no merger vote.
sources.claims_weakened: Contradicts the claim that a SpaceX combination would hand holders an unlisted security with no price; a listed $2.01tn counterparty and a 20-35% premium expectation make a merger a priced upside catalyst the Sell does not carry. The 50%-of-outstanding vote is a real hurdle.

sources.title: MarketBeat: Tesla (TSLA) short interest, October 2026
sources.claims: Tesla short interest was 69.35m shares, 2.19% of the public float, at the 2026-10-15 settlement, with a short-interest ratio of 2.2 days on 50.19m shares of average daily volume. A second source put the cost of borrow at 0.39% on 2026-10-29.
sources.claims_weakened: Weakens the scenario assumption that squeeze risk is high on a crowded short: 2.19% of float and 2.2 days to cover is a light short base, so a short squeeze is a headline event (merger, permit) rather than a positioning event.

sources.title: Hindustan Times explainer: Tesla-SpaceX merger - price, control and shareholder votes (2026-10-22)
sources.claims: Tesla ~$1.5tn and SpaceX ~$2tn before premium, combined ~$3.5tn; all-stock structures under study (SpaceX buys Tesla or a new holding company); special committees of independent directors, no terms agreed; RBC Capital Markets and JPMorgan expect a 20%-35% premium for Tesla holders (Reuters, 2026-10-21), others expect little or none; ~43% ownership at parity, ~47%-50% with that premium; Tesla approval needs a majority of all shares outstanding, not of votes cast; Musk holds ~20% of Tesla voting power and ~85% of SpaceX's; SpaceX Q3 2026 revenue $14.58bn, up 161%, AI $7.56bn; capex $19.6bn in the quarter, $35-40bn guided for Q4.
sources.claims_weakened: Weakens the section's claim that no priced change-of-control path exists and that a combination would deliver an unlisted security; also shows the premium is a broker expectation rather than a filed term.

sources.title: Space and Sky: SpaceX stock SPCX trades on Nasdaq - IPO, filings and Q2 2026 results
sources.claims: Space Exploration Technologies Corp. went public 2026-06-12, Class A common stock on Nasdaq Global Select Market and Nasdaq Texas under SPCX; IPO priced at $135 for 555,555,555 shares; CIK 0001181412; Q2 2026 revenue $7.8bn (+92%), net loss $541m, adjusted EBITDA $3.5bn, ~$100bn cash and securities, $47.5bn backlog; 7,607m Class A and 5,569m Class B shares outstanding at 2026-06-30; Cursor acquisition completed 2026-08-14 paid in 389.3m Class A shares.
sources.claims_weakened: Contradicts any description of SpaceX as a private or unlisted company; shows a priced, liquid acquirer whose shares can be consideration.

sources.title: Polymarket: Tesla and SpaceX merger officially announced by ...? (odds via search result, 2026-10-31)
sources.claims: Prediction market on an official Tesla-SpaceX merger announcement: about 18% implied probability by 2026-12-31 and 67% by 2027-12-31, on $1.7m of volume since the market launched 2026-01-29 (figures from the search-result summaries of the market, not read on the page itself).
sources.claims_weakened: Tempering: the near-term odds (18% by end-2026) are far below the 20-35% premium expectation, so an announcement inside 12 months is a minority branch; the odds are a crowd price, not a filing.

sources.title: TeslaNorth: Tesla sets 2026 annual shareholder meeting for December 3, no merger on the ballot (2026-10-19)
sources.claims: Tesla's DEF 14A sets the 2026 annual meeting for 2026-12-03 at Giga Texas with three votes: re-election of Musk, Denholm and Straubel, say-on-pay, and ratification of PwC; no SpaceX merger proposal on the ballot.
sources.claims_weakened: Removes the 2026-12-03 meeting as a merger catalyst; a vote would need a separate meeting and a majority of all shares outstanding.

sources.title: Wall Street Journal: Tesla stock fell 65% in 2022, its biggest-ever annual decline
sources.claims: Tesla fell about 65% in 2022 and shed more than $700bn of market value, the base rate for a multiple-led drawdown in this stock.
sources.claims_weakened: Claims that a 60% drawdown is an extreme or unrepeatable tail.

sources.title: TechCrunch: SpaceX and Tesla boards form special committees to review merger
sources.claims: Both boards formed special committees of independent directors to review a possible SpaceX-Tesla combination; no agreement reached.
sources.claims_weakened: Any claim that no change-of-control path exists or that the process is absent.

sources.title: India Today: Elon Musk's education — two Penn degrees awarded 1997, no Stanford enrolment
sources.claims: Musk earned a BA in physics from Penn's School of Arts and Sciences and a BS in economics from Wharton, both awarded in 1997; he transferred to Penn in 1992 after two years at Queen's University; Stanford confirmed in 2024 it had no record of him enrolling in its graduate programme.
sources.claims_weakened: The often-repeated claim that Musk completed or attended a Stanford PhD in applied physics; the article also notes critics have challenged the physics degree, though it states both degrees were awarded in 1997.

sources.title: China Daily: Tom Zhu profile — AUT bachelor's 2004, Duke MBA, Shanghai ramp
sources.claims: Tom Zhu earned a bachelor's degree from Auckland University of Technology in 2004 and an MBA from Duke University's Fuqua School of Business (year not stated); joined Tesla in 2014; built Gigafactory Shanghai in 10 months in 2019 at 65% lower cost than the Model 3 plant in the US; holds a New Zealand passport.
sources.claims_weakened: Any reading that Zhu's degree is a US or Chinese qualification; also any suggestion the Shanghai plant's cost advantage came only from labour rather than construction execution.

sources.title: Wikipedia: Robyn Denholm — Sydney economics degree, UNSW MCom 1999, career dates
sources.claims: Denholm graduated from the University of Sydney with a bachelor's degree in economics and from the University of New South Wales with a Master of Commerce in 1999; began her career at Arthur Andersen in Sydney in 1984 and was VP finance at Toyota Australia from 1989.
sources.claims_weakened: Any exact undergraduate graduation year: this source gives none, and its infobox labels the Sydney degree a BA while Tesla's proxy says Bachelor of Economics.

sources.title: Energy-Storage.News: Sungrow ships 25GWh in H1 2026, pulls back from US
sources.claims: Sungrow H1 2026 revenue RMB 30.912bn (-28.99% YoY), net profit RMB 5.259bn (-32.01%), BESS shipments 25 GWh; storage revenue RMB 15.456bn, half of group revenue.
sources.claims_weakened: Volume growth does not protect storage revenue: 25 GWh of shipments came with a 29% revenue decline, evidence that system prices are falling faster than volumes rise.

sources.title: ESS News: CATL storage revenue jumps 88% as H1 profit hits CNY 43.3 billion
sources.claims: CATL H1 2026 revenue CNY 276.92bn (+54.8%), group gross margin 23.93%; energy-storage segment revenue CNY 53.26bn (+87.5%, 19.2% of revenue) at a 23.96% gross margin; EV battery margin 20.63%; overseas margin 29.97% vs 21.16% in China.
sources.claims_weakened: Tesla's energy gross margin ex-refund (14.8%) sits below CATL's storage-segment margin (23.96%), so Tesla does not hold an unrivaled storage cost position.

sources.title: ChinaEVHome: CIC Bluebook - Momenta and Huawei control over 80% of China urban NOA market
sources.claims: Momenta held 65% of China's third-party urban NOA supplier market in March 2025-February 2026; Momenta and Huawei together control more than 80%; urban NOA adoption rises from 11.3% in 2025 to 62.4% by 2030.
sources.claims_weakened: Tesla's FSD is a marginal supplier in China's driver-assistance market, where Huawei and Momenta already hold the installed-base scale.

sources.title: LG Energy Solution: 2026 second-quarter financial results
sources.claims: Q2 2026 revenue KRW 7.6tn (+15.3% QoQ), operating profit KRW 113.3bn (1.5% operating margin); ESS revenue 4.6x YoY and high-20% of first-half revenue; more than KRW 3tn of new ESS orders; North America's largest ESS manufacturer.
sources.claims_weakened: A scaled ESS cell maker earns a 1.5% operating margin; storage is a low-margin volume business even for a low-cost Korean producer with local US capacity.

sources.title: Chariotz: Super Cruise vs BlueCruise vs FSD in 2026 - where each driver-assist system stands
sources.claims: GM Super Cruise is hands-free on about 750,000 compatible miles in the US and Canada; Ford BlueCruise covers more than 130,000 Blue Zone miles (97% of controlled-access highways in the US and Canada); both are Level 2, mapped-road, driver-monitored systems; Tesla FSD (Supervised) has the broader operational domain but is also Level 2 and under NHTSA EA26002.
sources.claims_weakened: Hands-free highway driving is an OEM commodity sold by GM and Ford; Tesla's differentiation is operational-domain breadth, not the existence of hands-free driving.

sources.title: SQ Magazine: Robotaxi statistics 2026 - fleet and safety
sources.claims: Pony.ai's robotaxi fleet exceeded 1,400 units on 2026-03-25 with a target of more than 3,000 by end-2026; Baidu Apollo Go delivered 3.4 million robotaxi trips in Q4 2025, up 200% year on year.
sources.claims_weakened: Tesla's 1,051 authorised Texas vehicles and 2.0 million unsupervised miles are small against Chinese operators as well as Waymo.

sources.title: Toutiao/min.news: Sungrow semi-annual report - energy-storage gross margin 32.43%
sources.claims: Sungrow's H1 2026 energy-storage segment gross margin was 32.43%, per coverage of its semi-annual report; the page itself returned HTTP 403 and the figure is taken from the search snippet.
sources.claims_weakened: Tesla's energy margin ex-refund (14.8%) is less than half Sungrow's storage-segment margin, so Tesla has no cost lead over Chinese storage manufacturers.

sources.title: Electrek: Tesla FSD 'subscriptions' hit 1.74M, counted the way Musk's pay package wants (2026-10-21)
sources.claims: Tesla's Q3 2026 shareholder letter defines 1.74m active FSD subscriptions to include both upfront purchases and monthly subscriptions (excluding free trials), following the 2025 CEO Performance Award definition; quarterly count rose from 1.04m in Q3 2025 to 1.74m in Q3 2026; Tesla stopped selling FSD as a one-time purchase on 2026-02-14 and now charges $99/month in the US; the letter does not disclose how many of the 1.74m pay monthly.
sources.claims_weakened: Any reading of 1.74m as a purely recurring subscriber base or as proof of software revenue momentum; the count includes legacy one-time buyers some years old.

sources.title: Fluence Energy, Inc. Reports 2025 Financial Results and Initiates 2026 Guidance
sources.claims: Fluence GAAP gross margin approximately 13.1% for fiscal year 2025 and 13.7% in Q4 FY2025, against 12.6% and 12.8% in fiscal 2024; the 5.1% June 2026 quarter is a low outlier, not the annual baseline.
sources.claims_weakened: A sixfold Tesla-versus-Fluence storage margin gap: Tesla's Q3 2026 energy margin ex-$526m refund is 14.8%, about 1.7 points above Fluence's FY2025 13.1%.

sources.title: OSHA Injury Tracking Application — establishment-specific injury and illness data (Form 300A)
sources.claims: OSHA publishes establishment-specific injury and illness data (Form 300A) submitted through the Injury Tracking Application: total case rate and days-away/restriction/transfer rate per establishment and year. It is the registry that would supply Tesla's total recordable case rate and days-away rate for comparison with GM, Ford and BYD.
sources.claims_weakened: The public interface requires an establishment-level query; Tesla's plant-level rates are not in a single downloadable figure in the record reviewed, so the section's workplace-safety comparison remains unverified.

sources.title: EnergyTrend: Sungrow 2025 revenue RMB 89.18bn, energy storage gross margin 36.49%
sources.claims: Sungrow's 2025 energy storage business revenue was RMB 37.29bn, up 49.39%, at a 36.49% gross margin, with 43 GWh of storage systems shipped, up 53.5%.
sources.claims_weakened: Sungrow is a component and inverter manufacturer, not a project integrator, so its margin is not directly comparable with Tesla's Megapack segment; the figure is as-reported and not adjusted for tariff refunds.

sources.title: Reuters: CATL first-half 2026 profit rises 42% on energy storage
sources.claims: CATL's energy storage battery gross margin fell to 24.0% in H1 2026 from 25.5% a year earlier, while first-half net profit rose 42%.
sources.claims_weakened: CATL sells cells and systems at component level, not integrated projects; its China cost base differs from Tesla's US and Shanghai Megapack assembly.

sources.title: BYDToday: China Robotaxi 2026 - Baidu, Pony.ai, WeRide and Commercial Scale
sources.claims: Baidu Apollo Go 3.2m fully driverless rides in Q1 2026 and more than 22m cumulative by April 2026; Pony.ai fleet above 1,700 (1,776 produced by 2026-05-24) with Q1 2026 robotaxi services revenue of US$8.6m (RMB 59.1m, +395.4% YoY); WeRide about 1,300 robotaxis globally and about 1,000 in China at 2026-04-30; XPeng's first production robotaxi rolled off the line in May 2026 with pilot operation planned for H2 2026.
sources.claims_weakened: Tesla's 2.0m cumulative unsupervised miles as evidence of autonomy leadership: Chinese operators disclose larger driverless ride counts and, in Pony.ai's case, standalone robotaxi revenue. Also weakens any read-across that Chinese L4 is only testing, and any claim that production of a robotaxi equals a paid service (the XPeng case).

sources.title: Ars Technica: Aftermarket driver assist under federal probe following fatal crashes (comma.ai openpilot)
sources.claims: NHTSA's Office of Defects Investigation is investigating comma.ai's aftermarket openpilot devices after five crashes into stopped or slow-moving vehicles; two crashes caused three deaths and 11 people were injured across four of the five. Establishes openpilot as a supervised aftermarket driver-assistance system with a federal safety file, not a driverless product.
sources.claims_weakened: Any suggestion that consumer-grade hands-off assistance (openpilot, and by extension supervised FSD) is converging on driverless operation without a regulatory step; also weakens the claim that Tesla's FSD safety file is unique among assisted-driving systems.

scope.decision: Whether to Buy or Sell Tesla (TSLA) equity now, at the current price, for an investment committee decision with a 12-month horizon.

spines.must_answer: Does the price offer a 12-month return that compensates for a 60% drawdown risk, and what does the multiple require that the filings do not show?
Is unsupervised autonomy monetisable inside twelve months, given the permit record, 2.0m unsupervised miles and Waymo's 220.6m rider-only miles?
How much of the demand and credit pool has policy already removed, and what dated rules govern autonomy, storage and sourcing?

research_plan.industry_map: Value chain: battery cells (CATL, BYD, Panasonic) -> vehicle assembly (Tesla, BYD, GM, Ford, Rivian, Lucid) -> charging and software -> paid autonomy (Waymo, Baidu Apollo Go, Tesla) and stationary storage (Tesla, CATL, Fluence, Sungrow) sold to utilities and commercial buyers. Decisive bottleneck: permits and per-unit cost in autonomy, and the cost of capital against a 103x multiple in public equity; Tesla's place is a scale vehicle maker with an unrivaled storage cost position and a sub-scale autonomy service (2.0m unsupervised miles, 0.9% of Waymo's rider-only miles, California testing permit only, 1,051 authorised Texas vehicles).
research_plan.geo_lens: Material. Three market systems are mapped: the United States (federal EV credit ended 2025-09-30; US EV sales -30.3% YTD; California DMV/CPUC and Texas SB 2807 govern paid autonomy), China (NEV retail -12.8% in 9M 2026; purchase tax at a 5% half-rate capped at RMB 15,000; BYD and Xiaomi set the price), and the European Union (BEV registrations +49% in 9M 2026; CO2 three-year averaging 2025-2027; December 2025 proposal to cut the 2035 target to 90%).
research_plan.policy_lens: Material and dated. US: the $7,500 consumer credit ended 2025-09-30; US EV sales -30.3% YTD and August 2026 -46.9% year on year; regulatory credits fell to $1,993m in FY2025 from $2,763m. Autonomy: NHTSA EA26002 covers 3,203,754 vehicles; California lists Tesla only for testing with a safety driver; Texas SB 2807 authorises commercial automated vehicles from 2026-05-28. EU: CO2 targets on a 2025-2027 three-year average; December 2025 proposal to cut the 2035 target to 90%; battery due diligence delayed to 2027-08-18. China: NEV purchase tax at a 5% half-rate capped at RMB 15,000. Tariffs and export controls affect cell sourcing and FSD training compute.

gates: Confirm company identity, legal entity, geography, stage, and business model.
Decide whether the geographic market context lens is material; if yes, map home, revenue, expansion, supplier, comparable-company, capital, exit markets and the investor perspective.
Decide whether the policy and geopolitics lens is material; if yes, map jurisdictions and perspective.
Complete the profile requirements before drafting.
Build the source register with source type, date, confidence, claims and a link or file/page reference.
Use visible source IDs such as [S1] as citations in the report.
Complete the evidence matrix for all material sections before drafting.
Run the pre-draft evidence gate and fix failures.
Draft the report from evidence, not from outline memory.
research_plan.hypothesis: Sell at $399.81 (2026-10-30): the reported businesses are worth $139-160bn, or $35-40 a share, against a $1,580.4bn capitalisation; 90-91% of the price is an option on autonomy revenue the filings do not book, the equity trades at 103x trailing adjusted EBITDA against BYD's 17.3x, and the expected 12-month return is -19.8%. The live counter-risk is a SpaceX share-for-share combination at a 20-35% premium ($480-540), which caps the short rather than changing the call.
research_plan.author: Lead Analyst

items: Use web and data tools for fresh facts whenever a company, market, price, policy, filing, funding, or executive fact may have changed.
For each major section, record targeted search strings, opened sources, source IDs, and why the selected sources are decision-grade rather than merely convenient.
Use the server's checks for deterministic QA, extraction, citation checks and the delivery folder; do not rely on a one-shot narrative draft.
Do not generate repeated filler paragraphs such as per-section original-document priority, citation-anchor blocks, or repeated metric-card copy; each section must contain content-specific analysis.
Before drafting, write a section distinctness plan: the unique decision question, mechanism, comparison set, counter-evidence, and best visual artifact for each section.
For each section, draft one final-report thesis sentence that directly analyzes the company; never copy internal plan labels or rubric language into the report.
Remove repeated visible scaffolds such as "Economic mechanism", "Comparison and benchmark", "Counter-evidence and risk" and "Investor implication"; keep the scaffold internal.
Use a verdict strip, compact decision cards, selected tables, and at most a few KPI strips; do not repeat the same card, grid or dashboard pattern in every section.
Before writing the executive briefing, summarize the non-consensus or consensus view and the exact evidence that changes the decision.
Treat OCR as a pipeline: inventory files, OCR scan- or slide-heavy material, and keep page, slide or table references for every extracted claim.
Check every page holding numbers, TAM, valuation, customers, clinical or regulatory claims, policy claims, financing terms or team credentials before relying on it.
Mark OCR-derived claims low confidence until checked or corroborated; use ranges for OCR-derived financial inputs.
Build a claim verification table for material company-provided claims: verified, partially verified, unverified, contradicted, or not publicly disclosed.
profile_requirements.evidence: Every profile item is evidenced in the register and the fourteen sections. Company identity and structure: Texas corporation since 2024-06-13, single class, 3,952,648,559 shares and a 19.8% CEO stake with 207,498,721 shares pledged [S1, S8, S10]. Product and technology: FSD at 1.74m subscriptions, 2.0m unsupervised Robotaxi miles, California testing permit with a safety driver only, NHTSA EA26002 over 3,203,754 vehicles [S9, S89, S87, S151]. Market: IEA 23.0m electric units in 2026, US EV sales -30.3% year to date, China NEV retail -12.8%, Europe BEV +49%, storage 158 GW/459 GWh [S137, S139, S138, S140, S141]. Competition: 52.9% US EV share, BYD 246,816 units against Tesla's 64,837 in China, Fluence 5.1% gross margin against Tesla's 33.1% [S145, S146, S61]. Unit economics and financials: -$1,994 a vehicle after group R&D and SG&A, 9M free cash flow of $1,883m below a $3,868m payables build, ROIC 5.5% against a 4.93% Treasury, net cash $36,180m [S8, S9]. Valuation and exit: SOTP $139-160bn ($35-40 a share) against $1,580.4bn, 103x adjusted EBITDA against BYD's 17.3x, SpaceX listed at $2.01tn with a 20-35% premium band [S11, S131, S154, S156]. Risk, ESG and policy: EA26002, credit revenue down to $1,993m, NLRB Buffalo complaint dismissed, EU CO2 three-year averaging [S87, S8, S96, S92]. Company-claim verification: every material company-only claim is labelled verified, partially verified, unverified or not disclosed, including the 1.74m FSD count (company-reported, half on subscription per the CFO), the 2.0m unsupervised miles (company-reported), the "almost sold out" 2027 Megapack book (company-only) and the 1,051-vehicle Texas fleet (independently reported) [S152, S151, S125]. Thesis, scenarios, scoring and executive summary: 31/40/29 probabilities, expected -19.8%, composite 3.8, Sell with a capped short; QA has been run on the full report and the independent review is the next gate.
profile_requirements.author: Lead Analyst

rows.belief: The pain Tesla solves is real but the addressable pool is contracting where Tesla sells most: US EV sales are 30.3% below 2025 after the $7,500 credit ended on 2025-09-30, and China NEV retail fell 12.8% in 9M 2026.
rows.evidence: US EV volume 266,630 in Q3 2026 at 6.4% of new-vehicle sales, -30.3% YTD; China NEV retail 7.758m in 9M 2026, -12.8% [S139, S145, S138]. Europe is the exception at 1.93m BEVs in 9M 2026, +49% units [S140, S147].
rows.counter_evidence: IEA still forecasts 23.0m electric units in 2026 (28% share) and half of global sales by 2035; Tesla reports its largest backlog in four years and says battery availability, not orders, capped Q3 2026 volume [S137, S9].
rows.confidence: high
rows.change: A reinstated US consumer incentive or a sustained recovery in China NEV retail above +5% year on year would widen the pool.

rows.belief: Tesla's advantages are real in supervised driving data, manufacturing integration and storage cost, but the priced asset — unsupervised autonomy — is a distant second to Waymo.
rows.evidence: 1.74m active FSD subscriptions on a 10.2m-vehicle fleet (17.1% attach); 2.0m cumulative unsupervised Robotaxi miles against Waymo's 170m+ rider-only and 500,000 paid rides a week; storage gross margin 33.1% vs Fluence's 5.1% [S9, S101, S61].
rows.counter_evidence: Camera-only sensing is under NHTSA Engineering Analysis EA26002 covering 3,203,754 vehicles with one fatality; Tesla holds no California driverless deployment permit and only a testing permit with a safety driver [S87, S89].
rows.confidence: high
rows.change: A California driverless deployment permit plus disclosed paid-trip economics would narrow the gap; a recall that restricts the operating domain would widen it.

rows.belief: The timing is wrong for the core: the markets that pay Tesla's bills are shrinking by policy while the markets that grow are smaller and priced per unit.
rows.evidence: US and China pools contracting; Europe +49% and storage +41% (158 GW/459 GWh in 2026) are the growth pools, but storage revenue per GWh fell 23% to $210m and paid robotaxi is a $0.3-0.5bn fare-based market [S141, S140, S142].
rows.counter_evidence: Europe's CO2 three-year averaging keeps the credit pool alive through 2027, and Texas SB 2807 authorises commercial automated vehicles from 2026-05-28 [S92, S91].
rows.confidence: medium
rows.change: A US federal incentive restored, or a faster EU/China recovery, would improve timing; an EU 2035 target cut to 90% would extend the policy drag.

rows.belief: Tesla can defend price in the US and scale storage, but it is sub-scale in China and has no disclosed European share, so unit growth should be underwritten below the market's.
rows.evidence: 52.9% US EV share in 9M 2026 with US volume -14.4%; fourth in China at 64,837 retail units in September against BYD's 246,816; 8,904 Supercharger stations and 84,465 connectors; Model 3/Y were 478,237 of 486,532 Q3 2026 deliveries [S145, S138, S9].
rows.counter_evidence: Tesla's US share gains inside a shrinking pool and record Berlin output show the brand retains pricing power where charging density matters [S9, S147].
rows.confidence: medium
rows.change: Disclosure of EU unit share, or a China volume recovery above 80,000 units a month, would change the view.

rows.belief: The car does not earn the group's profit: automotive alone runs at about -$1,994 a vehicle once group R&D and SG&A are charged, and energy plus services pay the operating cost.
rows.evidence: Q3 2026: $42,259 revenue and $34,436 cost per vehicle, $7,823 gross profit ($7,590 ex-credits) against $9,817 of group R&D and SG&A; auto breaks even near 611,000 deliveries a quarter vs 486,532; energy and services add $3,470 a vehicle [S9, S8].
rows.counter_evidence: Ex-credit automotive gross margin rose to 18.1% from 15.4% year on year, level with BYD's 18%, and services gross margin hit a record 15.9% [S8, S116].
rows.confidence: high
rows.change: A cost-per-vehicle reduction below $33,000 or deliveries above 611,000 a quarter without price cuts would flip the auto line positive.

rows.belief: Operating execution is real in manufacturing, but capital allocation and key-person risk are structural and only partly priced.
rows.evidence: Tom Zhu built Shanghai (>950,000 units) and Berlin set a record; the 10-K states the CEO "does not devote his full time and attention to Tesla"; the board committed $2.0bn to xAI after a shareholder measure against it drew 1.06bn votes to 916.3m [S1, S10, S104].
rows.counter_evidence: Seven of nine directors are independent, the CEO takes no salary, and the pay award's 12 tranches are gated from a $2tn market cap with a $334.09 offset [S10, S107].
rows.confidence: high
rows.change: A credible CEO succession framework, or an independent review of related-party flows, would reduce the discount.

rows.belief: There is no margin of safety: the reported businesses are worth $139-160bn, or $35-40 a share, against a $1,580.4bn capitalisation.
rows.evidence: Auto $45-60bn, energy $31-37bn, services $24bn, net cash $36.18bn and SpaceX stake $2.87bn; 103x trailing adjusted EBITDA (144x before the $4.3bn stock-comp add-back) vs BYD's 17.3x; P/E 439x [S8, S9, S11, S131].
rows.counter_evidence: The premium buys a maturing option: 1.74m FSD subscriptions, a paid take rate above 75% of North American deliveries and a Texas fleet that grew from 739 to 1,051 vehicles in 18 days [S9, S125].
rows.confidence: high
rows.change: Disclosed robotaxi revenue with positive contribution, or a peer transaction at a comparable multiple, would justify part of the premium.

rows.belief: No buyer can pay this price and the company returns no cash, so the 12-month exit is a sale into the market at whatever multiple prevails.
rows.evidence: GM, Ford and Rivian are worth $137.0bn combined; no dividend ever and no repurchase programme; the only change-of-control path is a share-for-share SpaceX combination under committee study with no price [S15, S17, S19, S126, S1].
rows.counter_evidence: $36.18bn of net cash, $30.0bn of undrawn facilities and $13.8bn of daily liquidity mean Tesla cannot be forced to raise equity [S8, S11].
rows.confidence: high
rows.change: A cash bid, a buyback authorisation or a priced SpaceX exchange ratio would create a real exit.

rows.belief: The price is roughly 10x the value of the reported businesses; 90-91% of the equity is an option on revenue the filings do not book.
rows.evidence: At $399.81 on 2026-10-30 the market cap is $1,580.4bn; the SOTP is $139-160bn; the residual $1,420-1,441bn needs $105bn of 2030 operating income at 20x, or 2.1-4.2m robotaxis at a 25% margin [S8, S11, S125, S127].
rows.counter_evidence: A generous auto recovery (10% operating margin on $75bn at 25x) lifts the total to $288bn, $73 a share, still 82% below spot [S9].
rows.confidence: high
rows.change: A disclosed robotaxi P&L and a California permit would move the option from narrative to cash flow and re-open the valuation.

rows.belief: Reported profit leans on interest income and one-offs; the operating margin of 2.6% understates Q3 2026 by 1.7 points only because of a credit reversal.
rows.evidence: Q3 2026 interest income $445m was 46.5% of pre-tax profit (42.9% for 9M); $475m credit reversal; SBC $3,346m in 9M (4.3% of revenue); warranty reserve up 20.9% in nine months against 10% delivery growth [S8, S1].
rows.counter_evidence: GAAP gross margin of 19.0% in 9M 2026 is the highest since 2023, and energy's 33.1% and services' 15.9% are genuine operating improvements [S8, S9].
rows.confidence: high
rows.change: A quarter with operating profit above $1.5bn excluding credits and interest income would show the core earning power.

rows.belief: Free cash flow is a payables loan and a capex pause, not a run-rate: 9M 2026 FCF of $1,883m is smaller than the $3,868m payables build that produced it.
rows.evidence: Q3 2026 FCF of $1,531m rested on a $2,590m working-capital inflow; stripping it out gives -$1,059m; capex guidance cut to >$20bn from >$25bn; FY2026 FCF seen at -$1,290m to +$1,160m [S8, S83, S102].
rows.counter_evidence: Operating cash flow of $14,897m in 9M 2026 and $30.0bn of undrawn facilities give ample funding without equity [S8].
rows.confidence: high
rows.change: Two consecutive quarters of positive FCF before working capital would establish a run-rate.

rows.belief: The balance sheet is strong enough to fund the plan but carries off-balance obligations that matter: leases, warranty and deferred revenue.
rows.evidence: $36,180m net cash at 2026-09-30; $30.0bn unused committed facilities after three September 2026 agreements; $7,955m minimum lease payments, $7,414m warranty reserve and $7,055m deferred revenue [S8].
rows.counter_evidence: Interest coverage fell to 9.96x from 56.99x in FY2023, and $3,670m of capex sat in liabilities at 2026-09-30 [S8].
rows.confidence: high
rows.change: A draw on the facilities to fund negative FCF, or a warranty charge above $1bn, would weaken the position.

rows.belief: Consensus is Hold with a 2.2% target upside; the market expects the autonomy option to be proven, while Tesla gives no numeric guidance and has just cut capex.
rows.evidence: 24 buy, 1 strong buy, 20 hold and 3 sell across 48 firms; average target $408.61; Q3 2026 adjusted EPS $0.48 vs $0.45 expected; capex cut to approximately $20bn [S128, S9].
rows.counter_evidence: An 83-analyst sample gives $442.13 (+10.6%), and the stock is 8.2% above its 50-day average after a 28.5% three-month run [S128, S11].
rows.confidence: medium
rows.change: A guidance framework with a robotaxi revenue line would let consensus converge on numbers rather than narratives.

rows.belief: The next 12 months have four dated resets, and the balance of risk into them is negative because the multiple, not the earnings, carries the price.
rows.evidence: Q4 2026 results in the last week of January 2027; first Cybercab deployment outside Austin; SpaceX committee process; NHTSA EA26002; annual meeting on 2026-12-03; 202m new shares in nine months (+5.4%) [S128, S125, S126, S87, S1].
rows.counter_evidence: A positive EA26002 closure and a California permit would be upside catalysts of the same magnitude [S89].
rows.confidence: medium
rows.change: A robotaxi revenue disclosure before the Q4 print, or a permit, would flip the catalyst sign.

rows.belief: Zero long exposure: the 12-month distribution is roughly -60% to +27% around a 2.2% consensus, and the Kelly fraction is negative.
rows.evidence: De-rating from 103x to 40x costs 60% of the price; the bull case to the first award gate adds 27%; realised drawdowns of 65.5% in 2022 and 40.4% from the 52-week high; VIX at its 77th percentile and 10-year Treasury at 4.93% [S11, S9, S10, S12].
rows.counter_evidence: $36,180m net cash is 2.3% of the capitalisation and a SpaceX combination could re-rate the shares inside the year [S8, S126].
rows.confidence: medium
rows.change: A disclosed robotaxi P&L with positive contribution would make a starter position defensible.

scenarios.driver: Two branches: 15% autonomy proof (a California driverless deployment permit and a disclosed robotaxi revenue line with positive contribution), 15% a SpaceX share-for-share combination at a 20-35% premium
scenarios.outcome: $506.05 a share, +26.6%; a combination at $480-540 pays the same band as the first 2025 award gate at a $2,000bn capitalisation
scenarios.implication: Cover or close the short; the standalone case re-rates only if the revenue line arrives

scenarios.driver: No robotaxi monetisation before 2028, the US pool near 6-7% of sales, energy revenue per GWh falling and margin at 14-18%, multiple at 70x
scenarios.outcome: $266 a share, -33.5%: 70x on $14.5bn of adjusted EBITDA plus $36.18bn of net cash
scenarios.implication: Remain short or underweight; no long entry into the Q4 2026 report

scenarios.driver: Two branches: 22% a 40x multiple after EA26002 converts to a restricting recall, California stays closed, US and China share erode and capex overruns force a facility draw; 8% a full de-rating to 15-25x as the multiple converges on the reported businesses
scenarios.implication: The short pays; add only on disclosure, not on price

assumptions.assumption: Autonomy stays unmonetised through 2027: no robotaxi revenue line is disclosed and the paid service stays in Texas
assumptions.disproof: A quarterly robotaxi revenue line with positive contribution, or a California driverless deployment permit, inside twelve months
assumptions.impact: The bull case, +26.6% at $506.05, replaces the base case, -33.5% at $266
assumptions.early_warning: Q4 2026 results in the last week of January 2027 pass without a robotaxi line

assumptions.assumption: The equity multiple holds above 40x adjusted EBITDA despite a 4.93% ten-year Treasury
assumptions.disproof: A move to 40x or below
assumptions.impact: -61% at 40x, $156; the 15-25x full de-rating gives $64-101, -79%
assumptions.early_warning: Ten-year Treasury above 5%; a quarterly miss against consensus

assumptions.assumption: Energy gross margin normalises to 14-18% once the $526m of Q3 2026 IEEPA tariff refunds and warranty true-ups roll off
assumptions.disproof: Two consecutive quarters above 20% with no tariff refunds and Megapack price per kWh stabilising
assumptions.impact: $1.5bn of EBITDA, $9-10 a share at 25x
assumptions.early_warning: Energy revenue per GWh below $200m, or margin below 14% in Q4 2026

assumptions.assumption: Capex lands at or below $20bn and free cash flow is non-negative before working-capital swings
assumptions.disproof: Q4 capex above $7bn, a third guidance change, or a second quarter of negative free cash flow ex-working capital
assumptions.impact: $5bn of free cash flow, $31 a share at 25x
assumptions.early_warning: A draw on the $30bn facilities; payables growth above 20% year on year

assumptions.assumption: A SpaceX share-for-share combination is attempted at a 20-35% premium, with a 15% probability inside twelve months
assumptions.disproof: The special committees end without terms, or the vote threshold fails
assumptions.impact: +20% to +35% adverse to a short
assumptions.early_warning: A filed exchange ratio; the 50%-of-outstanding vote count

consensus.consensus: Hold: 24 buy, 1 strong buy, 20 hold and 3 sell across 48 firms, average target $408.61, 2.2% above the $399.81 close on 2026-10-30; the market capitalises autonomy as a 2028 cash flow and treats the SpaceX combination as an alternative path to the same band.
consensus.our_view: Non-consensus Sell. The autonomy option is priced at zero until a robotaxi revenue line with positive contribution or a California driverless deployment permit is disclosed; the expected twelve-month return is -25.2%.
consensus.evidence: The divergence is the option, not the car: 90-91% of the $1,580.4bn capitalisation sits above $139-160bn of reported-business value. Autonomy shows 2.0m cumulative unsupervised Robotaxi miles, 0.9% of Waymo's 220.6m rider-only miles through 2026-03, a California testing permit that requires a safety driver, and 1,051 authorised vehicles in Texas on 2026-10-27. The base case applies 70x to $14.5bn of adjusted EBITDA, built from trailing $14,995m less $526m of Q3 2026 one-offs, and still lands at $266.
consensus.proof_event: The Q4 2026 10-Q segment disclosure in the last week of January 2027: a robotaxi revenue line with positive contribution, or its absence.

one_question.question: What is Robotaxi revenue per vehicle-week in Texas, and is it positive at the contribution level after insurance, depreciation and remote supervision?
one_question.why: It is the only figure that can turn 90-91% of the price from an option into a cash flow. A positive disclosed number validates the multiple and forces a re-rating toward the first award gate at $506.05; its absence, or a negative contribution, leaves the equity valued at 103x a declining auto business and points to the full de-rating.

modules.capital_efficiency: Automotive is the cash engine but not the profit engine: Q3 2026 gross profit of $7,823 a vehicle ($7,590 ex-credits) sits below $9,817 of group R&D and SG&A, while energy gross profit of $954m included $526m of one-off tariff refunds and warranty true-ups, leaving 14.8% on $2,881m of revenue. Nine-month free cash flow of $1,883m was smaller than the $3,868m payables build that produced it, and capex guidance moved from more than $25bn in July 2026 to more than $20bn in October, with $30bn of undrawn facilities as the backstop.
modules.position_sizing: Zero long. At most a capped short: cap the notional at 2.9% of NAV, so a 35% merger gap costs 1.0% of NAV, with $506.05 (the first award gate) as a reference stop that a gap can trade through. The Kelly fraction for a long is negative at the stated distribution. The market regime compounds the de-rating case: VIX 19.42 at the 77th percentile and a 4.93% ten-year Treasury leave the multiple no rate cushion.

answers.most_damaging_fact: The 'no buyer can pay' claim. SpaceX is listed at $2.01tn ($147.79 on 2026-10-20), both boards have independent special committees, and RBC and JPMorgan expect a 20-35% premium, $480-540 against $399.81 [S154, S156]. At the report's 15% merger weight that branch moves the stock +26.6% to $506.05, so the Sell is wrong by 20-35% if terms land inside twelve months. The second candidate is the 2.0m unsupervised-mile figure: if the 8x quarterly growth is independently verified and a California deployment permit follows, valuing autonomy at zero is wrong. The DMV list on 2026-10-23 still shows testing with a safety driver [S89], which is why the Sell survives today.
answers.company_only_claims: The positive case rests on company-only numbers: 2.0m cumulative unsupervised Robotaxi miles growing 8x quarter on quarter, the 1,051-vehicle Texas fleet, 'almost sold out' Megapacks for 2027, 1.74m FSD subscriptions including upfront buyers and the $1bn FSD run rate [S152]. The energy margin is no longer a positive company claim: Q3 2026's 33.1% is $526m of tariff refunds and warranty true-ups; ex-refund it is $428m on $2,881m, 14.8%, barely above Fluence's FY2025 13.1% [S174] and far from its 5.1% June quarter [S61]. Independent checks are the California DMV list, which shows testing only, and NHTSA EA26002; both cut against the timeline [S87, S89].
answers.generic_section: technology_product is no longer the weakest: it corrected Waymo to 220.6m rider-only miles, made Tesla 0.9% of the incumbent, and cut to six tags [S151]. market is the weakest now, but it is a disclosed gap rather than a generic section: Tesla's EU unit share is not disclosed, so Europe's 49% BEV growth is a market fact, not a Tesla share gain; the ACEA manufacturer table would settle it, and the section says so. competition is second: it still carries Waymo at '170m+' and a 'sixfold' storage margin that the 14.8% ex-refund figure contradicts [S8, S61, S174]. Both are corrections, not new research.
answers.unpriced_risk: The robotaxi cost per paid mile. The recommendation prices the de-rating and gives the merger branch 15%, but it treats the 15% autonomy branch as a permit event: Tesla discloses no revenue, rides, fare, insurance, remote-supervision ratio or cost per mile, and if cost per paid mile exceeds fare the branch is worth zero even with a California permit, taking expected return from -25.2% to -34.2% [S153]. NHTSA's remedy ($0.3-3.2bn) is a second unpriced cost channel; the crowded-short risk runs the other way, with 2.19% of float and 2.2 days to cover a light base [S155].
answers.first_challenge: The base case and the SOTP are 5-7x apart: $266 against $40-50, so which number is the recommendation asking me to underwrite? If the twelve-month target is $266 (-33.5%), the SOTP is a liquidation floor and the Sell is a de-rating call; if it is $40-50, the Sell is an -87% to -90% call the thesis does not defend. Second, the exit section still carries a 25-45% probability band and a -17% to -1.5% weighted return, while the report's single distribution gives the merger 15% and an expected -25.2%; one of the two has to give. Third, the 30% bull is defensible, but 15% of it is an autonomy branch whose cost per paid mile has never been published.
answers.downside_survival: Yes, as a de-rating call. A 50% smaller market takes the SOTP to $120-126bn, $30-32 a share, and destroys the base case's 70x on $14.5bn; revenue 30% lower gives $90 a share at 40x; CAC 2x adds $3.7bn and wipes the $3.47bn operating income; a six-month financing delay is not a solvency event with $36.18bn of net cash and $30.0bn undrawn, so the cost falls on the option. Multiples compress is the base and bear; free cash flow 30% lower changes little at a 0.2% yield. The conclusion fails only if the merger branch lands or the autonomy cost stack is positive, so the 15% weights, the 2.9% NAV cap and the $506.05 stop are the weak points, not the downside arithmetic.
answers.ocr_claims: No OCR-derived claims. Financial figures come from the 10-Q and the Q3 2026 update, governance from the proxy, permits from the California DMV page, all text-readable [S8, S10, S89]. The NHTSA EA26002 PDF did not yield machine-readable text in this pass, so the investigation scope (3,203,754 vehicles, nine incidents, one fatality) rests on the filing-based technology section and the registered NHTSA source rather than a fresh OCR reading [S87]; that is a corroboration gap, not an OCR claim.

rows.finding: Automotive regulatory credit revenue fell to $1,993M in FY2025 from $2,763M in FY2024 (-28%), then to $639M for the nine months to 2026-09-30 versus $1,451M a year earlier, and Tesla reversed $475M of previously recognised credit revenue in 2026 for contractual returns of delivered credits.
rows.mechanism: Credits were a near-zero-marginal-cost revenue line priced off the compliance gap of other automakers. When OBBBA restricted the federal programmes behind them, buyers' obligations shrank and previously sold credits became returnable, so the revenue both falls and reverses; the remaining performance obligation on multi-year credit contracts fell to $384M at 2026-09-30 from $841M at 2025-12-31 and $3.84B of RPO disappeared across 2025.
rows.benchmark: FY2023 $1,790M, FY2024 $2,763M, FY2025 $1,993M; the 2024 peak is the base rate for a programme that has now been legislated away in the US.
rows.weakens: Tesla still monetises European CO2 pooling and state ZEV programmes, and the $384M contracted backlog is not zero, so the line does not go to nil.
rows.implication: Treat the credit line as structurally impaired rather than cyclical: at the 9M 2026 run rate it contributes roughly $850M a year against $2.8B in 2024, so forecasts that carry a recovery in credits overstate high-margin revenue and gross margin.
rows.confidence: high - two filed statements, one audited, with the reversal quantified
rows.follow_up: How much of the $384M remaining obligation is with buyers whose own compliance position could still change, and what is the cash-refund exposure beyond the $475M already reversed?

rows.finding: On 2025-12-19 the Delaware Supreme Court reversed the Chancery rescission of Mr Musk's 2018 pay award, reinstating it with $1 in nominal damages and a reduced fee award; the replacement 2025 CEO Performance Award covers 423,743,904 restricted shares, and a 96.0M-share interim award granted 2025-08-03 vests on its second anniversary at a $23.34 purchase price.
rows.mechanism: The appeal outcome removed a multi-year governance tail: the company no longer faces a possible re-litigation of a $50bn-plus award, and the interim award's 'no double dip' clause caps total dilution at the 2018 award's share count. What remains is concentration: Mr Musk holds 699,580,882 shares (19.8% of 3,952,648,559 outstanding), of which 207,498,721 are pledged as loan collateral, while the 423.7M unearned shares carry an irrevocable proxy voting them proportionally to other shareholders.
rows.benchmark: Chancery rescinded the award on 2024-01-30 and denied revision on 2024-12-02 with a $345M fee award; 72% of disinterested shares had voted to ratify in 2024. Reversal on appeal is the unusual step - most Delaware pay challenges that reach judgment are not reversed.
rows.weakens: The December 2025 reversal is genuinely favourable to shareholders on litigation risk and removes an overhang that had been priced since 2024; a reader who treats the pay saga as unresolved is working from stale facts.
rows.implication: The governance discount should narrow on the litigation tail but not disappear: a pledged 207.5M-share block is a forced-selling channel in a drawdown, and 10.7% of shares outstanding granted to one person is a live dilution and key-person issue for the 12-month view.
rows.confidence: high - both the appellate outcome and the share counts are in filed documents
rows.follow_up: Will the 2026 annual meeting's say-on-pay (Proposal Two, 2026-12-03) draw a materially lower yes share than the 2024 ratification, and does the board publish a succession plan for the CEO role?

rows.finding: Tesla agreed in January 2026 to invest approximately $2.00bn in xAI Holdings Series E preferred; after SpaceX acquired xAI Holdings on 2026-02-02 the right converted into SpaceX Class A stock, and Tesla completed the $2.00bn purchase on 2026-03-12. In 2025 Tesla also recognised $430.1M of revenue from xAI (mostly Megapack sales) and $143.3M from SpaceX, and paid $4.8M to a security company owned by Mr Musk.
rows.mechanism: Related-party flows run in both directions: Tesla is a supplier to the CEO's other companies and a capital provider to them. The investment converts operating cash into a minority stake in a private company whose valuation the Audit Committee, not the market, had to opine on.
rows.benchmark: The 2024-2025 derivative suits over X/xAI conflicts were consolidated and were still at the motion-to-dismiss stage after 2025-10-22 argument, so no court has yet ruled on the conflict itself.
rows.weakens: The Audit Committee approved the transaction under a written policy requiring arm's-length terms, and the SpaceX stake is a liquid-ish asset rather than a write-off; revenue from xAI and SpaceX is small against $94.8bn of 2025 revenue.
rows.implication: This is the governance fact most likely to move institutional demand in the next 12 months: a $2.0bn related-party investment is 3-4% of Tesla's cash and investments, and proxy advisers treat related-party capital allocation as a voting trigger.
rows.confidence: high on the facts, low on the valuation effect - Tesla does not disclose the stake's carrying value separately
rows.follow_up: What valuation and governance rights attach to the SpaceX Class A stake, and is there a lock-up or transfer restriction that makes it illiquid on a 12-month view?

rows.finding: As of 2026-10-23 the California DMV lists TESLA ROBOTAXI LLC only as a holder of an autonomous-vehicle testing permit with a safety driver; Tesla appears on neither the driverless-testing list (updated 2026-10-22) nor the deployment list, which names only Mercedes-Benz, Nuro and Waymo. The California Public Utilities Commission confirmed in March 2026 that Tesla's California 'Robotaxi' runs on a limousine permit, outside AV passenger-service rules. In Texas, Senate Bill 2807 (not 2809) requires TxDMV authorisation for commercial automated vehicles from 2026-05-28.
rows.mechanism: Permitting, not technology, sets the addressable market for paid driverless rides. California is roughly 20% of US EV sales and the largest single AV market; a testing permit with a driver cannot generate driverless ride revenue, so the paid-service TAM in the next 12 months is limited to permissive states such as Texas plus any city-level arrangements.
rows.benchmark: Waymo holds both a California driverless testing authorisation and a deployment authorisation after a multi-year process; Tesla has held a testing-with-driver permit since 2025 without progressing to the next tier.
rows.weakens: Texas is permissive and Tesla already operates there; the TxDMV regime is a light registration-and-reporting framework rather than a cap on volume, and other states may follow Texas rather than California.
rows.implication: Value any 2026-2027 robotaxi revenue on Texas-style permissive jurisdictions only, and treat California launch dates as a 2027+ option that requires two separate approvals (DMV driverless testing, then DMV/CPUC deployment).
rows.confidence: high on the permit status (regulator's own list), medium on the CPUC characterisation (single-source reporting of an official statement)
rows.follow_up: Has TxDMV issued Tesla an authorisation, and under which entity? What is the CPUC's timetable for an AV passenger-service permit decision if Tesla applies?

rows.finding: NHTSA's Office of Defects Investigation opened Engineering Analysis EA26002 on 2026-03-18 into Tesla's FSD degradation-detection system, covering an estimated 3,203,754 vehicles (2016-2026 Model S/X, 2017-2026 Model 3, 2020-2026 Model Y, 2023-2026 Cybertruck). Separately, NHTSA records eight recall campaigns on the 2026 Model Y between 2025-05-30 and 2026-09-01, including a front-suspension fastener recall (26V558000, 2026-09-01) and a bumper recall (26V445000, 2026-07-07).
rows.mechanism: An Engineering Analysis is the last administrative step before NHTSA can seek a mandatory recall; a recall of a software-defined defect is cheap to remedy over the air but expensive in brand and in the legal record, because plaintiffs' experts can cite the agency's findings in the product-liability cases Tesla already faces.
rows.benchmark: The probe escalated from Preliminary Evaluation PE24031 within roughly a year - an unusual pace that signals agency seriousness; Tesla's eight 2026-Model-Y campaigns in 16 months is high for a single nameplate but consistent with its history of build-quality recalls.
rows.weakens: Tesla's 2025 10-K shows no consent order and no NHTSA enforcement penalty; software recalls are remedied remotely and have not stopped deliveries in the past.
rows.implication: Price a 12-month probability of an FSD recall as meaningful, with a low direct cash cost and a higher indirect cost through the autonomy narrative and litigation; a consent order, which NHTSA has not issued, would be the materially worse outcome.
rows.confidence: high on the existence and scope of EA26002 (agency resume plus corroborating reporting); medium on the vehicle count, which comes from secondary reporting because the resume PDF did not parse
rows.follow_up: What is the ODI's information-request schedule under EA26002, and has NHTSA opened the separate remote-driving probe reported by trade press?

rows.finding: Tesla faces a California Civil Rights Department race-discrimination action whose first (equitable-relief) trial phase ran from 2026-09-21 to a scheduled close on 2026-10-30 in Alameda County Superior Court, and an EEOC race-harassment and retaliation suit filed 2023-09-28 in the Northern District of California that is in discovery with no trial date. The NLRB dismissed a separate complaint over Buffalo plant IT rules on 2026-10-29.
rows.mechanism: Discrimination litigation bites through remedies rather than damages: injunctive relief can impose monitoring, training and reporting obligations on plant management, and a public finding of systemic discrimination raises the cost of hiring and of state-level incentives in the jurisdictions where Tesla builds.
rows.benchmark: The NLRB dismissal in the same week shows the enforcement record is mixed rather than uniformly adverse; Tesla settled a 2024 EEOC-adjacent matter and has faced repeated individual race cases at Fremont since 2017.
rows.weakens: Tesla's 10-K does not quantify any accrual for these matters, which usually signals management does not expect a material loss, and the NLRB outcome cuts against the 'compliance culture' bear case.
rows.implication: The CRD phase-one outcome, due around the report date, is a near-term headline and governance-quality signal; the cash exposure is not disclosed and is unlikely to be material against Tesla's balance sheet, but a finding would strengthen the case for board-level human-capital oversight.
rows.confidence: high on the docket facts, low on the outcome - the trial closed on the eve of the report date and no judgment is in the record
rows.follow_up: What did the CRD bench phase find, and does any injunctive relief extend to suppliers or staffing agencies?

rows.finding: The US federal consumer credit for new EVs ended on 2025-09-30 and IRS confirms 30D, 25E and 45W are unavailable for vehicles acquired after that date; Cox Automotive data show US EV sales down nearly 24% in H1 2026 versus H1 2025, with August 2026 sales of 78,895 units, down 46.9% year on year, while Tesla's US Model 3/Y volume fell from 481,166 in Q3 2025 to 406,585 in Q4 2025. In China the NEV purchase tax moved to a 5% half-rate with a RMB 15,000 cap from 2026-01-01, and in the EU the 15% 2025-2029 fleet target is now assessed on a 2025-2027 three-year average.
rows.mechanism: A $7,500 credit on a roughly $45,000 vehicle is a 17% price change at the point of sale; removing it shifts demand down and toward cheaper trims and hybrids. China's half-rate tax is a smaller shock (about 5% of price, capped) and Europe's averaging defers compliance rather than cutting it, so the three regimes pull in different directions at once.
rows.benchmark: Q3 2025 was a pull-forward peak across the industry (Ford Mach-E 20,177 to 9,658; Hyundai Ioniq 5 8,408 to 2,279 quarter on quarter), so the Q4 2025 cliff is partly timing rather than pure demand destruction.
rows.weakens: US EV sales rose more than 14% sequentially from Q1 to Q2 2026 and California's $3,500 MyFirstEV rebate from August 2026 puts a floor under the largest single state market; hybrids, not EVs, absorbed part of the shift.
rows.implication: The policy-driven demand shock is already in reported numbers rather than a forecast, so the 12-month question is whether Tesla's mix and cost cuts offset it; China and Europe look more supportive than the US on relative price.
rows.confidence: high on the statutory position (IRS), medium on the market response (Cox data reported second-hand)
rows.follow_up: What share of Tesla's 2026 US volume is lease versus purchase, and how much of the lost credit is being absorbed through residual-value support?

plan.decision_question: Do environmental, social and governance factors change Tesla's cost of capital, demand or licence to operate over the next 12 months?
plan.thesis_sentence: Tesla's ESG and policy position has already cost it real money in 2026 - a federal consumer credit that vanished, a regulatory-credit line that fell by more than half and then reversed $475M - but the binding constraint on the next twelve months is not reputational: it is that Tesla holds no California permit to run a driverless paid service and faces a 3.2-million-vehicle NHTSA engineering analysis, so the ESG judgement is that governance and product-safety risk, not the environmental story, set the discount rate.
plan.why_different: Every other section treats policy as an input to demand, cost or valuation; this section asks whether the compliance record itself changes the company's cost of capital, its permission to operate and its access to institutional capital - and it is the only section that prices the permit wall and the enforcement docket as first-order facts.
plan.mechanism: Policy sets the relative price of Tesla's product and the size of its credit revenue; enforcement and permitting set what Tesla is legally allowed to sell. When the credit disappeared the effective price of a Tesla in the US rose by roughly a sixth, and when the underlying programmes were restricted the credit buyers' obligation shrank and delivered credits became returnable. In autonomy the mechanism is different and harder: a testing permit is not a commercial licence, so technology progress does not convert into revenue until a second and third approval arrive.
plan.comparison_set: Waymo as the permitted-deployment benchmark in California; BYD and Chinese OEMs under a 5% purchase tax; legacy OEMs (Ford, Honda, Hyundai) that retreated from US EVs after the credit ended; Tesla's own 2024 credit peak as the base rate for a policy-dependent revenue line; and the pre-2024 governance discount as the base rate for pay-litigation overhangs.
plan.counter_evidence: Policy still favours Tesla in several places: Texas SB 2807 is a permissive registration regime that lets Tesla operate commercially where California will not; the EU three-year averaging keeps the CO2 credit pool alive through 2027; California's $3,500 rebate supports the largest US EV market; the NLRB dismissed its Buffalo complaint on 2026-10-29; NHTSA has issued no consent order; and the Delaware Supreme Court's 2025-12-19 reversal removed a governance tail rather than adding one. Much of the 'ESG hurts Tesla' narrative is stale - Tesla left the S&P 500 ESG index in 2022 and its cost of capital did not visibly re-rate.
plan.visual: Policy impact matrix (Factor | Exposure | Probability | Impact | Mitigant | Source) plus a regulatory record table and an ESG issues table; the credit-revenue collapse and the permit wall are the two rows that carry the judgement.
plan.prohibited: No 'ESG is a scam' framing, no 'green premium', no 'well positioned', no vague 'many lawsuits', no claim that Tesla operates a permitted robotaxi service in California, no reliance on the 2022 index exclusion as a current fact, no dual-class structure claim (Tesla has one class of common stock).
